News.title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people
News.content:
The work and pensions secretary has backed the idea that the government should legally guarantee young people help to get into employment.

Pat McFadden told the BBC that job support should be given a "legislative underpinning", adding the level of assistance on offer was currently "vague".

McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed.

But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers.

It comes ahead of a long-awaited review by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn, which will recommend on Tuesday that under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work.

His report is also expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales.

Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to health conditions, under the plans.

Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Milburn said the government should divert money away from the benefits system to boost work support, adding he wanted to see "billions" extra spent on help over the next decade.

However, the idea of reducing the entitlement of existing benefit claimants could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who scuppered a previous benefits-cutting plan under Sir Keir Starmer last year.

Milburn said the reduced entitlement for some should be accompanied by a new "duty on government" to provide jobs support to young people, such as apprenticeships, college places, job coaching, or a job.

He added that the temporary nature of previous job support schemes, including the Kickstart programme during the Covid pandemic, meant that they had been less effective as reducing long-term joblessness.

How the new guarantee would work in practice is not yet clear, with McFadden adding it would have to be "carefully" drafted.

Although local councils have some specific legal duties, including in the areas of child protection and homelessness, duties on central government currently tend to be much broader, such as operating a "comprehensive" health service.

News.title: Hannah Fry feels 'unbelievably lucky' after cervical cancer treatment
News.content:
Prof Hannah Fry has described feeling "unbelievably lucky" after being treated for cervical cancer.

The mathematician and BBC presenter, who recently took part in the second season of the Celebrity Traitors, said cancerous cells were discovered after she attended a cervical screening in 2020.

She underwent a hysterectomy, describing the experience to BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs as "horrific".

"As awful as that was, it had a full stop at the end of the sentence," the 42-year-old added. "I had my five-year clear the other day. I feel so unbelievably lucky."

In Sunday's episode, Fry told show host Lauren Laverne that she had delayed a cervical screening examination for months in 2020. After she attended one, the results "didn't come back for a few weeks," she said.

"Then I got a call from my GP telling me they needed me to come back and do another test, and they did a biopsy.

"I was trying hard not to panic but when they found it was in the lymphatic systemâ¦ that was when it really started to come down."

The broadcaster said she was told that her chances of survival depended on the cancerous cells not having spread to her lymph nodes, although it was not clear "how bad it was at that point".

"It's all about, basically, how far into your lymphatic system has it got. If it had not got into any lymph nodes, then the odds were in my favour and I had a really good chance of survival," she said.

Fry explained that this meant "if it was in one it would drop to a 60% chance of survival and two â the odds would go against me and it would be a 40% chance".

News.title: Watch: SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
News.content:
SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time.

"Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas.

The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.

But the first catch of the rocket's booster was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday. The booster was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames just above the sea.

The top part, known as the Ship, returned to Earth a few minutes behind schedule at around 15:20 local time (21:20 GMT) on Saturday, in the first-ever successful catch attempt.

News.title: Judo champion shakes up French  presidential race with surprise candidacy
News.content:
Apart from an overwhelming urge to pin one's opponent to the floor of the house, there is no obvious connection between politics and the world of top-level judo.

That has not stopped France's much-garlanded world heavyweight champion Teddy Riner from throwing his hat into the ring for next April's presidential race.

The Guadeloupe-born 37-year-old may have no experience of public office, no party behind him, and as yet no manifesto. All so far is a slogan La France qu'on aime (The France we love), a declaration on social media, and a campaign visit to a hospital in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.

But it would be a foolhardy pundit who would totally write off his chances.

Riner is, after all, one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, regularly topping the polls for embodying the nation's "values". He is a proven winner, with five Olympic golds and 11 world championships under his belt, as well as a successful career in business.

More than 28 million people have watched his election broadcast on Instagram and X, shot with proper presidential decorum against a backdrop of books and a French flag. Some 22% told an Ifop poll within 24 hours they "could" vote for him.

News.title: Beauty advent calendars can cost hundreds but are they value for money?
News.content:
It's easy to see the appeal of a beauty advent calendar. Like many women at this time of year, Julia says she often finds herself tempted to splurge on one - especially a perfume calendar. But she takes quite an unsentimental approach.

"I always look at what's in them. If I like enough of the fragrances, I'll buy it," says the 39-year old, who works as a senior commercial manager in engineering.

Luxury advent calendars are supposed to offer the thrill of a surprise but, for Julia, it is more important she actually wants the items inside - a thought that is also striking more and more customers in the wake of the scandal over the Skims calendar.

News.title: Man dies after being hit by ambulance
News.content:
A man has died after being struck by an ambulance transporting a patient near Sunderland, police have said.

Northumbria Police said the crash occurred on the A19, between the junctions for the A1018 and A690, shortly after 02:00 GMT.

The ambulance was travelling on the northbound carriageway and did not have its blue lights on when it hit the man, who was in his 30s and died at the scene.

Neither the patient nor their partner who were travelling in the ambulance were injured in the collision, while the vehicle's driver, a man in his 40s, was also not hurt and remained at the scene to assist police with their inquiries.

The North East Ambulance Service (NEAS) said the patient in the ambulance and their partner were transferred to another ambulance.

Officers from Northumbria Police's roads unit have launched an investigation into the collision.

Sgt Ben Rutherford said: "Our thoughts are firmly with the family and loved ones of the man who has tragically died following this collision.

"We will continue to support them in any way that we can at this incredibly difficult time."

Anyone with CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident itself or the moments leading up to the collision has been urged to contact the force.

Rutherford said anyone with information, no matter how insignificant it may seem, "could prove key to our investigation and help provide answers for the man's loved ones".

News.title: Schoolboy imposter subjected ex-professor and wife to 'terrifying ordeal'
News.content:
An imposter who made headlines around the world for posing as a school pupil in his 30s has appeared in court and admitted hiding in the home of his former university professor before subjecting him to a "terrifying ordeal"

Brian MacKinnon targeted Prof Brian Whiting, 87, as he lay in bed with his wife, the day after a BBC docudrama on his ruse was broadcast.

My Old School chronicled MacKinnon's return to Bearsden Academy, as Brandon Lee, a 16-year-old who had supposedly just moved to Scotland from Canada.

MacKinnon hatched the plan so he could pursue his dream of becoming a doctor having been thrown out of Glasgow University, when Prof Whiting was dean of the medical school.

News.title: Milder day in store before more cold health alerts take effect
News.content:
Another round of cold health alerts is set to come into force on Sunday following a brief break from the weekend's subzero temperatures.

After readings dipped as low as minus 7C early on Saturday, most places on Sunday morning were milder and free of frost.

Widespread rainfall will put a dampener on any outdoor plans, however, with hail and thunderstorms possible for parts of Wales and southern England.

Into the new week, the wintry chill is set to return with UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) cold-health alerts beginning for the north-east and north-west of England and Yorkshire and the Humber from 21:00 GMT on Sunday.

News.title: Sea of phones at Christmas event prompts backlash
News.content:
When BBC London uploaded a video, external of the Carnaby Street Christmas lights being switched on last week, the comments section filled with thousands of people reacting to what they saw.

But, it wasn't the bright lights or the pretty fireworks that they were reacting to, it was the sea of spectators filming on their phones.

"Remember when we used to look at stuff directly with our eyes? Those were the good old days," said one comment. Another simply said: "It's such a sad sad sight."

Former EastEnders actress Natalie Cassidy commented: "Why is this piece not mentioning the fact that no-one is looking through their eyes at this beautiful display? It's really scary and depressing."

Many of the comments questioned why people would film the fireworks rather than watch them in real life, with one saying: "Nice to see everyone living in the moment, there's a 90% chance they will never watch the video again too."

News.title: Banton hits century and bowlers sparkle for England to level ODI series against Australia
News.content:
Second one-day international, Adelaide

England 355-6 (50 overs): Banton 121, Cox 67, Root 62

Australia 220 all out (44.3 overs): Green 64, Renshaw 63; Atkinson 4-28

England won by 135 runs; series level at 1-1

Scorecard

Tom Banton scored a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impressed with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammered Australia to set up a series decider.

Banton scored a fine 121 â pushing his case for selection further with a second ODI hundred â in England's 355-6.

After being knocked over for 131 two days ago in Perth, England's total was their highest in one-day internationals in Australia.

And then their bowlers, who failed to defend 430 against Sri Lanka last month and were undone by an improbable last-wicket partnership against Pakistan, reduced Australia to 29-4 inside seven overs and easily closed out a 135-run victory.

The win ends a seven-match losing run against Australia across formats in Adelaide - and a run of six consecutive defeats by Australia in 50-over cricket away from home.

But, more significantly, it corrects their course after those damaging defeats against Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Australia and offers positives amid the frustrations going into the decider on Wednesday (03:30 GMT) in Hobart.

News.title: Man in life-threatening state after shop robbery
News.content:
A jewellery store employee is in a life-threatening condition after a robbery in broad daylight at a shop in Peterborough.

Cambridgeshire Police said six men raided Lala Jewellers on Gladstone Street at about 11:50 GMT on Saturday.

A senior councillor later said it was believed that the victim had been stabbed, external.

The city's MP described it as a "horrific and violent act", while police have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

They said shelves were emptied and two employees behind the counter were assaulted, before the thieves fled in separate vehicles.

Two of the robbers were wearing white, traditional Pakistani clothing, officers added.

One employee, a 50-year-old man, suffered serious injuries and was taken to hospital, where he remains in a life-threatening condition.

News.title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad
News.content:
DP World Tour Championship final leaderboard

-15 Hatton (Eng); -10 McIlroy (NI); -8 Chacarra (Spa), Lindell (Fin); -7 Olesen (Den), Reitan (Nor), Laporta (Ita), Lindberg (Swe), Perez (Fra)

Selected others: -4 Wallace (Eng); -3 Rahm (Spa), Schaper (SA); Level Fleetwwod (Eng), Reed (US), Fox (NZ); +1 Rai (Eng)

Full leaderboard

Rory McIlroy wiped away tears as he dedicated his eighth Race to Dubai victory to his ill father, Gerry.

Moments after matching Colin Montgomerie's record of season-long European tour titles on Sunday, the Northern Irishman was asked about the health of his father.

An emotional McIlroy revealed Gerry has been in hospital for two months after "a huge operation" - a double lung transplant - at the end of September.

"He's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy told the DP World Tour.

"But before I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him. He said to me: 'Go win The Race to Dubai'.

"This one's for him."

It came after a thrilling climax at the traditional season-ending DP World Tour Championship with Tyrrell Hatton securing a commanding victory, while McIlroy pipped Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra to the overall crown.

Hatton's closing six-under-par 66 helped him romp to a five-shot victory on 15 under par but most eyes were on the thrilling battle that went down to the final hole.

It is the fifth successive year that McIlroy has won the award and it has drawn him level with Montgomerie, the Scot who set a mark 21 years ago that few thought would ever be matched.

"Yeah, double digits," smiled McIlroy when asked what would be his final target of Race to Dubai victories.

"I'd love to surpass Monty next year and we'll go from there."

McIlroy's confidence in going along with a target shouted out by the fans surrounding the 18th green at the Earth Course in Dubai on Sunday was refreshing to hear.

But he appears to be playing and talking with a little more freedom in recent years - the sort of freedom that comes as a result of finally completing the career Grand Slam and winning successive Masters titles - and leads to declarations of winning 10, or more.

"Winning eight Order of Merits (Race to Dubai titles) was never in my list of goals growing up," said McIlroy, who closed with a bogey-free 67 to finish on 10 under and must surely now be considered Europe's greatest golfer.

"I remember Monty being a stalwart of the European tour and playing with him at the London Club in 2008, so to pull up alongside him and win eight of these means the world to me."

News.title: Call to review sentence for driver who killed boy and fled to Latvia
News.content:
Warwick Crown Court heard Dolars had been driving at 75-76mph in a 30mph zone when he struck the schoolboy, killing him instantly.

Judge Kristina Montgomery KC told him his speed had been "excessive" and added: "Your selfish and dangerous driving took his life."

But speaking after they left court, the family said they were unhappy with the sentence.

"They gave him the maximum they could, but it's not enough is it?," his father Clint said.

His mother Louise said as Dolars would only serve two-thirds of his sentence in prison, he would be out in six years.

"I know afterwards he can't drive," she added. "That's good to know - he's not going to be on the roads doing it to another family.

"To be in prison for six years, I think he should've got longer. My baby only had 12 years on this planet."

In her letter to Attorney General Ellie Reeves, Owatemi said she was asking if the legal threshold had been met for the case to be referred to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme, external.

She sat with the family during the sentencing and said it had been "heartbreaking" to watch the footage of the crash.

Owatemi said: "I make this request in light of the pain Keaton's family have endured, Dolars' decision to leave the scene and evade accountability for more than two years and the fact that his driving ban is substantially longer than his prison sentence."

She said she shared the family's concern that just over six years in custody failed to "reflect the seriousness of what Dolars did or the injustice they have endured".

In her letter she suggested the sentence should "make clear that dangerous driving carries serious consequences".

She also asked whether sufficient weight was given to Dolars' decision to flee the country, Keaton's vulnerability as a child pedestrian, the speed which Dolars was driving at and his failure to stop or call for help.

"I ask you to consider whether the court fully considered the sentencing powers available to it, including whether the statutory criteria for a life sentence were met," she said.

When is Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday officially falls on Friday 27 November 2026, but you can already shop hundreds of early deals. The likes of Sephora, Lookfantastic, and PlayStation have all launched their sales, with more retailers joining them as November progresses. So, while we're still more than two weeks away from the date itself, Black Friday shopping (and the savings that come with it) is well under way.

For those wondering why the date changes each year, Black Friday takes place the day after Thanksgiving in the US, which is always celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November. Whether it's worth waiting until then is another matter. Some of the strongest offers can appear well before the main event, so I'd recommend checking historical prices before deciding whether to buy now or hold out. Lucky for you, this is something myself and IndyBest’s shopping experts usually flag in our guides – so make sure to browse our descriptions in full before heading to the checkout.

When does Black Friday end?

Cyber Monday (30 November) marks the unofficial end of Black Friday each year, although there's technically no forced cut-off for retailers. Some will pull their discounts at 11:59pm that evening, while others will keep the offers running into early December.

Last year, for example, Lookfantastic continued its promotions until 3 December, and several retailers ran extended Cyber Week sales. However, I wouldn't count on every deal sticking around. Popular products can sell out long before the advertised end date and plenty of discounts are only available for a limited time. If you've spotted something at a jaw-droppingly good price, it's worth checking when that particular offer expires rather than relying on the retailer's wider sale dates.

When is Cyber Monday?

Cyber Monday is on 30 November 2026.

Cyber Monday is the online shopping event that follows Black Friday. It takes place on the Monday after Thanksgiving weekend in the US. It was originally created to encourage shoppers to buy online. But given that everyone shops on the internet, the concept of Cyber Monday is slightly redundant. It’s now just an extension of Black Friday, giving you a final chance to save before Christmas.

Some brands and retailers have tried to popularise other shopping events, but most have had about as much success as Gretchen Wieners trying to make “fetch” happen. There’s Travel Tuesday, for example, which takes place on the day after Cyber Monday and focuses on deals for flights, hotels and package holidays, and Small Business Saturday, which encourages shoppers to support independent retailers instead of the big chains.

How can I tell if a Black Friday deal is genuine?

The easiest way is to check a product’s price history. If it’s been the same price for weeks before Black Friday, or the discount is only a few pounds, it probably isn’t as impressive as it looks. Make sure to write a list of everything you want and need, noting down the current price so you can check the discount in November. I also recommend comparing prices across multiple retailers. Just because something has a big percentage off doesn’t automatically make it a good deal. Having covered sales for more than a decade, I’ve written a detailed guide to my top shopping tips for Black Friday.

News.title: Spanish club Tenerife pays tribute to Jesús de Miguel in its first match since soccer player's death
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Spanish soccer club Tenerife on Sunday paid tribute to Jesús de Miguel in its first game since the striker's shocking death, with midfielder Nacho Gil holding up De Miguel's jersey after scoring his team's opening goal shortly before halftime.

Before the second-division match, players from both Tenerife and Ceuta wore jerseys reading “Siempre en nuestro recuerdo” (Always in our memory). They gathered at midfield for a moment of silence. The shirts all had De Miguel's name and his No. 9 on the back.

After the warmup, Tenerife captain Enric Gallego placed De Miguel’s jersey on the field, and his teammates gathered around it.

Play stopped in the ninth minute, marking De Miguel's shirt number. Players, coaches and fans applauded.

Gil appeared overcome with emotion when he was given De Miguel's jersey after scoring in the 40th. Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife's 2-0 win over Ceuta, its first league victory since September.

A mural depicting De Miguel had been painted outside Gate 9 at Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium, where fans had left flowers, scarves and candles following his death.

De Miguel died on Nov. 3. He was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, who rushed far outside his area near the end of the Nov. 2 match in Tenerife. The 30-year-old De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest following the collision.

Owono on Friday was suspended for 12 games after he received a red card for the on-field collision with De Miguel. The Spanish soccer federation’s disciplinary committee said Owono used “excessive force” in the collision.

Owono had issued a statement through his club expressing his remorse and offering his condolences to De Miguel’s family.

Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings were unlikely.

Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday that it would be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again.

News.title: Teddy Riner: The judo star taking on Macron Le Pen to be France’s next president
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

French judo icon Teddy Riner suggests he would get the better of Donald Trump in a handshake contest if the pair were ever to meet as presidents of their respective nations—an assertion that is hardly a stretch.

Yet that scenario remains a major "if".

Even with five Olympic gold medals under his belt and more than 3.3 million followers across his social media platforms, Riner’s newly announced bid for the presidency of France promises to be a far tougher contest than many of the opponents he defeated.

History and rules stand in his way

The list of celebrities who have successfully built political power from screen or sporting fame is notably shorter in France than in the United States, where Trump, Ronald Reagan, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jesse Ventura, two-time NBA champion Bill Bradley, and former Buffalo Bills quarterback Jack Kemp converted stardom into high office.

Retiring sporting icons such as two-time Olympic judo champion David Douillet, fencing champion Jean-François Lamour, and Guy Drut, the 110-metre hurdles champion at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, did win seats in France's parliament and served as sports ministers.

However, Riner is targeting France's top office, seeking to become the first famous figure to achieve this since World War II hero Gen. Charles de Gaulle.

open image in gallery A thicket of cameras that greeted the 37-year-old on Friday, when he made his first campaign stop at a hospital in the northern suburbs of Paris, testified to the star power that Riner brings to the race ( AFP/Getty )

To feature on the ballot for April’s first round of voting, Riner must gain endorsements from a minimum of 500 elected officials—a requirement purposefully designed to prove challenging.

The measure, intended to limit the size of the field and filter out fanciful candidacies, is an indication of how France has traditionally regarded running the country as a serious business. It has been in place since the 1981 election and was one of the barriers that foiled a presidential bid by comedian and actor Coluche that year.

“In France, there are complex hurdles to entry for people who don’t come from the establishment,” said François Hourmant, a professor of political science at Angers University who has studied celebrity culture in French and North American politics.

“Moving from the tatamis to the political arena isn’t that simple, and isn’t something everyone can do,” he said in a phone interview with The Associated Press.

Riner's first campaign stop

A thicket of cameras that greeted the 37-year-old on Friday, when he made his first campaign stop at a hospital in the northern suburbs of Paris, testified to the star power that Riner brings to the race.

Looking fighting fit in a dark suit and open-neck shirt, he towers over everyone from the height of his 2.04-meter (6-foot, 8-inch) frame. His imposing physicality and easy charisma translate readily to television.

But the policy proposals Riner plans to bring to the campaign remain unclear. He describes himself as neither left nor right on the political spectrum and says France “needs common sense” and not “a professional politician who recites lessons and squabbles all day long.”

open image in gallery Teddy Riner collected two gold medals for France ( PA Wire )

In a two-minute, 37-second video that launched his campaign Monday and in an interview with the newspaper Le Parisien, Riner spoke of problems that he sees in France, among them “fear,” “anger,” a “social divide” and people unable “to envisage a future.” But he offered few solutions or blueprints for building what he called “the France that we want.”

Outside the hospital after meeting staff members, Riner said he is still working on his campaign platform and didn't answer questions, responding with a “have a good rest of the day, au revoir” before heading back to his car.

Far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, widely seen for now as the favorite to succeed President Emmanuel Macron in May, took a gentle swipe during a campaign stop of her own on Friday, saying she couldn't form an opinion about Riner's bid without knowing anything about his platform.

As a dominant judoka whose mantra was “Never let anyone steal your beefsteak,” Riner told the AP in 2013 that he would sometimes wrestle up to five people at once in training to make it more challenging. As a fledgling politician, he says he is steeled for more rough-and-tumble.

“When you know how to take punches, you also know how to throw them,” he told Le Parisien.

An electorate hungry for change but also experience

The rise of Le Pen and the challenge she faces from the other end of French politics from far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon together suggest a swath of French voters want deep and disruptive change.

But analysts believe many also want a seasoned hand to deal with the multitude of domestic and international challenges that France faces, including its record public debt and the threat to European security posed by Russian President Vladimir Putin and his war in Ukraine.

open image in gallery To appear on the ballot for the first round of voting in April, Riner needs a minimum of 500 elected officials to sponsor his candidacy, a requirement designed to not be easy ( Reuters )

“Teddy Riner certainly embodies renewal, but he doesn’t necessarily embody experience. So that is probably one of his main disadvantages,” said Mathieu Gallard, research director at the Ipsos polling institute.

Riner, who is Black, was born on the French Caribbean island of Guadeloupe and grew up in Paris. Both Gallard and Hourmant said the potential that Riner is more likely to understand and combat discrimination could attract people of color in an election where Le Pen's party and others on the far right are again seeking to focus on immigration.

“But again, is that enough to translate into votes,” Gallard asked.

“Teddy Riner’s skin color will be a political issue for some people,” Hourmant said. For some, “it may be a reason to support him, seeing a racialized candidate from the overseas territories. For others, it will be a deterrent.”

News.title: I’ve found the best PS5 Black Friday deals on consoles, games and more
News.content:
November is here, which means Black Friday 2026 is just around the corner. With Christmas creeping closer, there’s bargain-hunting to be had, and high up on many a wishlist is the PlayStation 5, which often drops in price every November.

The 2025 PS5 deals were the best I’d seen. The PS5 and PlayStation accessories, including gaming headsets and Sony’s PSVR2, crashed to all-time low prices. But will those prices be beaten for Black Friday 2026? It may be a tough ask, given that Sony hiked the price of all its consoles by nearly £100 in April. Even with a hefty saving, you might still pay more than the old RRP.

While Black Friday doesn’t officially take place until 27 November, Sony has already kicked off its PlayStation Store sale, with savings of up to 75 per cent on games. And while we’re still waiting for those PS5 deals to drop, I’ll be keeping a keen eye on PlayStation Direct in anticipation of offers on PS5 Slim, PS5 Pro and DualSense controllers. Here’s everything to know.



When will PS5 Black Friday deals begin in 2026?

For the past three years, PlayStation Direct has kicked off its official Black Friday sale a week before the eponymous day itself, which takes place on 27 November this year. While I’m still waiting for Sony to announce its PlayStation Direct sale, when it’s expected to drop deals on the console and other peripherals, the gaming giant has already kicked off its PlayStation Store sale.

Launching its savings on 4 November, you can now find discounts of up to 75 per cent on thousands of PS5, PS4 and PS VR2 games, expansions, and DLC.

As for the PS5 Slim and PS5 Pro itself? In 2025, Argos, Currys and EE were already discounting the PS5 Pro a fortnight before Black Friday began. While Argos, Currys and Very have already launched their 2026 Black Friday sales, only the latter is currently offering discounts on PS5 bundles. That could very well change in the coming weeks. Keep up to date with your favourite brands’ sales with our Black Friday tracker.



What are the best PS5 Black Friday deals to expect in 2026?

Last year’s Black Friday sale was the biggest and best when it came to the PS5, with record-low prices on almost every console in the gaming giant’s arsenal. Will the deals be just as good this year? I’d temper your expectations.

As mentioned, in April 2026, Sony hiked the price of all three PS5 consoles by a whopping £90, blaming global RAM shortages and higher manufacturing costs due to global tariffs. The PS5 slim with the disc drive was increased to £569.99, the PS5 Slim digital edition saw an increase to £519.99, and the PS5 Pro rose from £699.99 to an eye-watering £789.99. It’s also out of stock at several retailers.

That means even with a hefty Black Friday discount, we might not see prices fall quite as low as they have done in previous years.

Still, to give you a flavour of the kind of discounts we saw in 2025, Argos slashed the PS5 Slim digital edition console to just £289.99 – a huge £140 saving. The retailer even threw in a free copy of EA Sports FC 26. The PS5 Pro also fell to just £569.99 at Amazon and Argos, saving you £130.

There were loads of savings to be found at PlayStation Direct, too. Last year, £90 was sliced off the PS VR2 headset, while you could nab a £20 saving on the PlayStation Portal and get £20 off all of its DualSense controllers. I think games and accessories might get the heftiest discounts this year, with PS5 console prices being so sky-high right now.

News.title: Milburn warns Neets crisis will take a decade and billions of pounds to be solved: ‘No such thing as a free lunch’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Alan Milburn has said “there is no such thing as a free lunch” as he warned the government’s mission to tackle the youth unemployment crisis will take ten years and billions of pounds.

The former health secretary is set to unveil his review of the so-called Neets – under-25s not in employment, education or training – on Tuesday, which is expected to recommend radical changes to reduce welfare dependency.

Mr Milburn has said some young people will receive less financial support under his proposals, and called for young people to have a “legal guarantee” of work, training or employment support.

He said it will take 10 years to get to a “reasonable level” of youth unemployment in the UK, and also said GPs should be the people who sign fit notes, calling them a “route into the welfare system”.

He told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg show: “We’ve got to change how the current amount of money is spent and yes, of course, there will be a need for additional investment and that will run into billions I think, over a 10-year period.

open image in gallery Former health secretary Alan Milburn (Jeff Moore/PA) ( PA Wire )

“But what you get back is you get welfare savings back, and then you get the so-called fiscal benefits of young people not being reliant on a benefit but being paid a wage.”

Asked how long it would take to get the benefits bill down, he said: “This is a 10-year plan and you just got to be candid with people about this.”

Asked what his response was to people who argue he could be much tougher, he said: “I say that there’s no such thing as a free lunch.

“If you are going to will the ends, you’ve got to will the means. I don’t think there’s a single person in this country who believes that it’s tolerable to have one million young people aged 16 to 24 who are not in education, employment or training.”

He added it was not possible to “wave a magic wand” and do it within a few years without “crude cuts”.

“You can if you just do crude cuts, OK – if you do crude cuts, absolutely fine. But if you do crude cuts in benefits, all that happens is that young people show up somewhere else on the government ledger.”

He said: “It’s a 10-year programme for a reason because that’s the amount of time that we think it will take to get to a reasonable level of young people in this country being Neet.”

open image in gallery ( PA Graphics )

Work and pensions secretary Pat McFadden confirmed on Sunday that “there will be people in the future who will not get what they would get today”, as he urged Labour MPs to support the changes.

Asked whether he agreed that some people should lose the welfare they currently receive, Mr McFadden told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg show: “There will be people in the future who will not get what they would get today.

“When people come up for reassessment, they go on to a new system but, as I say, people are reassessed today under the current system.”

Amid questions about whether government will be able to win the backing of its MPs over any changes it adopts, Mr McFadden argued ministers must make reforms not “in spite of being Labour people”, but “because we’re Labour people”.

“If you’re 20 right now and you sign on to long-term sickness benefits, you’ve got more chance of marking your 30th birthday and still being on them than having a steady job in between,” he said.

“And the reason we have to change that isn’t in spite of being Labour people, it’s because we are Labour people.”

News.title: Trio give England fitness boost ahead of New Zealand showdown
News.content:

England have been reinforced for Saturday’s blockbuster fixture against New Zealand after George Furbank, Seb Atkinson and Ollie Chessum were given the green light to resume training.

All three were injured in the mauling of Australia that opened the autumn, forcing them to miss Saturday’s 78-15 rout of Japan, but have been restored to the 36-man squad that is preparing for the All Blacks’ visit to Allianz Stadium.

Furbank is expected to oust Freddie Steward at full-back and Atkinson is likely to replace Max Ojomoh at inside centre, while the return of Chessum could force a reshuffle in the back five of the pack.

open image in gallery New Zealand arrive at Twickenham on the back of a stunning upset by Wales on Saturday (Joe Giddens/PA) ( PA Wire )

The trio were influential performers as Australia were crushed 45-22 and, barring any setbacks in training, they are sure to feature in the starting XV named by head coach Steve Borthwick on Thursday.

Borthwick made 10 changes against Japan to give fringe players the chance to impress as the countdown to next year’s World continues, but he will revert to his strongest team for England’s bid to claim a place in the Nations Championship final on November 29.

Sports.title: Non-league game abandoned after seven minutes as star suffers serious injury days after team-mate’s tragic death
Sports.content:

NON-LEAGUE side Hendon were forced to cancel their game against Bedfont Sports after just seven minutes following defender Ethan Creary’s horror injury.

Play was stopped early on in the Isthmian League South Central Division clash after Creary suffered a nasty blow to his head.



A stretcher was brought on for the stricken star as a lengthy delay followed while medics were on the pitch assisting Creary.

Both sets of players were then taken off the pitch while Creary continued receiving treatment.



Eventually the referee decided to call off proceedings due to the serious nature of the injury and Creary was taken to hospital.

Hendon went on to report the player was “conscious and talking” in his hospital bed after a double collarbrone break and concussion.



The issue is likely to require surgery and he has also suffered possible ligament damage in his shoulder.

A club statement read: “We are pleased to be able to report that Ethan Creary is conscious, talking, and feeling better than earlier.

“Early signs are that he’s suffered a double break to the collarbone, possible shoulder ligament damage and concussion.

“We are hopeful he will be released home tonight ahead of surgery in the next few days and then a lengthy rehabilitation.



“The club will, of course, support Ethan in the coming days, weeks, and months ahead.”

Hendon also posted a picture of the defender sitting in his hospital bed while wearing a cast.

Creary’s blow comes just days after his friend and team-mate Ezekiel Williams was killed after a “serious assault” in Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire.



Williams, 26, had only joined Hendon in September and had scored his first goal for the club just days before his death.

Creary paid tribute to Williams in his own message posted by Hendon on his behalf amid a traumatic period off the pitch.

It said: “Yes boys, thank you for all the messages, sorry for not getting back to you all individually, I thought it would be easier to put a message in the group for now.

“I have a double break to the collar bone, will find out sometime this week whether it requires surgery.

“I have to be in the ward for 24hrs to assess any potential bleed in the brain, it’s just protocol and I woke up feeling okay.

“Hoping to come back to playoff positions at the absolute minimum, but my personal aim was always the title. See you lot soon.”

LIONEL MESSI left Juventus wonderkid Kenan Yildiz speechless after gifting him the custom-made boots he wore during his final appearance for Argentina.

The Turkish international, 21, received the extraordinary present from his footballing idol during a visit to Adidas’ headquarters in Germany, with the emotional moment captured on camera.



Yildiz was accompanied by his father as he toured the sportswear giant’s facilities before being presented with a mysterious golden box containing the priceless piece of football memorabilia.

And the youngster could barely believe his eyes when he discovered the personalised Adidas boots, which were accompanied by a handwritten card signed by the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner.



Yildiz said: “I think this is the craziest gift I’ve ever got. If I was an emotional guy, I would cry right now.”

The boots were worn by Messi during his Argentina farewell against Benin in Buenos Aires on October 7, when the 39-year-old scored a penalty and provided two assists in a 3-0 victory.

Messi brought the curtain down on his remarkable 21-year international career with 208 appearances and 126 goals for his country.

The Inter Miami superstar captained Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022 and also won two Copa America titles.

And Adidas ensured his final international appearance was suitably special, designing a unique version of the F50 ‘El Ultimo Tango’ boots featuring Argentina’s famous blue and white colours and stunning gold detailing.

The customised footwear included a gold No10 and the Argentine sun emblem surrounded by a laurel wreath.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Yildiz has long idolised Messi and was previously selected by the Barcelona legend as one of ten rising stars for Adidas’ Messi+10 project.

The initiative celebrates some of football’s most exciting young talents, with Arsenal youngster Max Dowman and Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal also among those involved.

The Turkey star has already established himself as one of European football’s brightest prospects since joining Juventus from Bayern Munich’s academy in 2022.

Sports.title: Dani Alves’ model wife Joana Sanz confirms breakup with former footie star, 43, after he took up new life as preacher

Next

MODEL Joana Sanz has confirmed her split from former Barcelona star Dani Alves.

The 34-year-old beauty, who stood by the retired footballer during his 2024 rape trial, blamed their separation after nine years of marriage on the Brazilian’s devotion to God.



Alves, 43, îs currently travelling the world on a speaking tour after transitioning into an evangelical preacher following a religious conversion in prison after his January 2023 rape arrest.

Alves was acquitted of sexual assault in a Barcelona nightclub after winning his appeal against his conviction last year.



The couple have a one-year-old daughter called Julieta.

Asked by a fan if she accompanied Alves to the religious services he has been attending since his conversion, Tenerife-born Joana said in a reply on Instagram: “I’m not a believer.

“The more I see what he does, the more I distance myself from all of this.”

She added: “I’d like to take this opportunity to clarify that we have been separated for some time now, precisely for that very reason.”

Spanish TV presenter Javi Hoyos went on to claim the couple were divorcing, saying: “The way in which Dani Alves has dedicated his life to the evangelical faith has driven them apart.”

Claiming he had spoken to Joana, he added: “They have launched divorce proceedings.



“After hearing about the news I contacted Joana and she has explained the reasons why to me.

“We’ve all seen the videos in recent times of Dani Alves as a preacher and right now he’s touring the world as an evangelical preacher and public speaker.

“Joana has told me this has led to him distancing himself from her and their daughter and she feels alone.



“She says she understand’s Dani Alves’ faith but the way in which he is dedicating his life to religion is forcing them apart and she reached a point where she decided enough was enough.

“Right now they’re no longer together and are divorcing.”

Joana reacted to Javi Hoyos’ Instagram post about the split by writing in a reply: “Always the most respectful one” and adding in a heart emoticon.

Alves, who has two teenage children from his first marriage, has yet to comment on the split but is posting footage showing him preaching in Guatemala which has been the latest stop on his tour.

After the break-up was made public, he shared a photo of himself sitting on an airplane in near-total darkness reading from a Bible.



Joana and Dani, who spent 14 months on remand in prison ahead of his February 2024 trial, married in 2017 in Ibiza two years after meeting.

The former Barcelona, Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain star had been arrested in January 2023 after flying to Spain from Mexico where he was playing his club football at the time to attend his mother-in-law’s funeral.

Joana gave him a second chance despite admitting she was seeking a divorce following his detention.



The ex-footballer was initially found guilty of raping a woman in a Barcelona in a city nightclub in December 2022 and sentenced to four and a half years in prison before the conviction and prison sentence was overturned by appeal court judges in March last year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alves had claimed at his trial he had consensual sex with his female accuser in a toilet at upmarket Sutton nightclub after initially denying knowing her.

Joana announced she was pregnant with their first child three days after the former footballer had his rape conviction overturned on appeal.

Sports.title: Man Utd's January offer to Mauricio Pochettino is needed - but also a recipe for disaster
Sports.content:
So Mauricio Pochettino is set to be backed in January as he bids to turn Manchester United's season around and get his tenure off to a positive start.

Is that needed? Undoubtedly. Is it still a recipe for disaster? Absolutely.

United's recruitment post Sir Alex Ferguson has, on the whole, been pretty poor. Their January dealings have been even worse and, were it not for a certain Bruno Fernandes, then their midseason transfer business would be looked upon woefully.

The senior figures at Old Trafford missed out on a number of their targets in the summer, and the team are now feeling the impact of that. A left-back and a No 9 would be most welcome right now, but any success is dependant on quality actually being landed in those positions.

‌



As we know, that is never easy in January. And it will probably prove even harder for a club whose talent identification and scouting has not proved a strength over the past decade or so.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Fernandes is an example of what can go right with a January arrival, inspiring the team in his opening six months and, largely, continuing to do so ever since.

‌



But that capture in January 2020 is an outlier. Every football executive up and down the country will tell you signing players in the New Year is a tough gig. Clubs don't want to sell, so as a result they'll hike any prices. Players that are available are often making the step up from the, so called, lesser clubs. Take a look at Patrick Dorgu from Leece as an example.

In January you'll tend to sign one of four things.

Genuine quality, unlikely. Overpriced stars, Alexis Sanchez. Young stars for the future, Ayden Heaven. Or players jumping up a level or two, which is a decision you take at your risk, Dorgu.

View 3 Images Ineos have made a number of underwhelming moves in the transfer market (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

‌



It was only last weekend that a former United player remarked that a back four containing Dorgu and Heaven would get the team relegated. They both are January signings.

In fact, since 2013 and the ending of United's dominance, the club have signed seven players permanently in January. Juan Mata, Victor Valdez, Sanchez, Fernandes , Amad, Dorgu and Heaven.

Bar Fernandes none of those could be classed as a 'hit'. That is the challenge that faces Pochettino and the Ineos hierarchy. It must be said, for all Pochettino's managerial quality, signing players hasn't actually been his greatest strength. Enter the likes of Vincent Janssen and Moussa Sissoko.

So here we have a concoction of Pochettino, an Ineos hierarchy who have shown themselves to be among England's worst decision makers and a United team whose transfer market history suggests they overpay for players who underdeliver.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes is Man Utd's most successful January signing but others, like Patrick Dorgu, have not totally convinced

Whilst Pochettino may look at this United team and think 'I need players' - of which he is right by the way - there is also a school of thought that says bringing in two or three players who don't cut the mustard and pen two or three years deals will only set the whole project back even further.

The irony, and frustration for those sitting in the Old Trafford stands, is that their rivals have constantly shown that value and quality very much exists in the New Year's market. Virgil van Dijk heading to Liverpool, Luis Diaz's move to Anfield, Newcastle signing Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal's capture of Martin Odegaard. To name a few.

United's neglect in the summer, which means their defence is now more than two years without a major arrival, leaves the club with little option but to go into the market in around 7 weeks time.

‌



The danger of course, as the latest new era begins, is that the fanbase watch the club and their hugely unpopular owners undertake business that will only set the club back even further.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard gives honest Arsenal contract update as major rival waits in the wings
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard gives honest Arsenal contract update as major rival waits in the wings

Martin Odegaard will soon enter the final 18 months of his contract at Arsenal and talks of not yet begun about extension - with rivals circling for the Norwegian

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard is yet to sit down with Arsenal to discuss a new deal (Image: Getty Images)

Martin Odegaard is hopeful he can remain at Arsenal beyond his current contract - but Bayern Munich are waiting in the wings.

‌



‌



The Norwegian has been at the Emirates for the bulk of Mikel Arteta's reign and for a long time was the team's first choice No 10, but the increase in competition and his recent injury record has cast doubt over his next move.

‌



Odegaard has confessed that he wants to stay in north London, but has equally conceded there has been no date set for the two parties to sit down around the negotiation table to discuss an extension.

‌



The former Real Madrid man has been among Arsenal's outstanding performers this season, reigniting the form of several years ago, and has made Arsenal tick in the opening weeks. His quality has seen admirers circle with Bayern among those keen on having him if Arsenal did want to move on from Odegaard.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Gunners are wise to the fact they may have to sell, reports Sky in Germany, and that scenario could come to pass if a deal has not been agreed soon. Arsenal ultimately do not want to lose Odegaard on a free.

The player himself recently said on his future: "I’m happy and hope I can stay there [at Arsenal] for a long time to come, but we haven’t started on that yet."

‌



Since Odegaard arrived at Arsenal the team have gone from top four challengers to a European powerhouse. Now Premier League champions, the Gunners boast a squad that also includes Kai Havertz, Bruno Guimaraes, Eberechi Eze and the blossoming Max Dowman.

View 2 Images The Norwegian has rediscovered top form this term (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

‌



It all leads to an increase in competition and Arteta has shown a ruthless side when it comes to selection and moving players on. He praised Odegaard for his early season form but confessed that the Norwegian needs to ensure he is fit, first and foremost.

“First of all, he needs to be available," he said. "And last year he missed so many games through injuries. He’s got that edge and he’s got different relationships around him as well. That helps."

Article continues below

Odegaard has started all ten of Arsenal's Premier League games and his five goals in all competitions is more than any of his teammates.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Declan Rice makes honest confession over England struggles
Sports.content:
Declan Rice has admitted he had “an average World Cup” by his own standards.

The midfielder went into the tournament with major fitness issues on the back of a gruelling season when he helped Arsenal win the Premier League title but ended up playing 69 games for club and country. His marathon year left him exhausted and in need of a break but also somewhat frustrated because he clearly felt he was not at his best even though England reached the semi-finals in the summer.

But Rice, who will win his 82nd cap against Spain, clearly feels there is unfinished business for him in an England shirt and he is determined to put that right.

England midfielder Rice, 27, said: “I think by my standards it was an average World Cup. I think some games I played well in, I applied myself well and did what I needed to do in terms of my standards and my level.

‌



“France was probably my best game, DR Congo I played really well, some of the other games I didn't play too well but it's one of those things, you reflect and look back at it - a 69-game season at the end of a title-winning season, a Champions League loss into a World Cup.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“It's annoying because at the World Cup you want to be totally at your best, you want to be fresh, you want to be ready. It's annoying that I couldn't perform how I did at Arsenal at the back end of the season.

‌



“But knowing I'm not going to be at my best, you give 100 percent for the badge. I loved it, I enjoyed it. Congo was probably one of my best games, having to go right-back for the last 15-20 minutes was out of the ordinary but I applied myself in the right way.

“The France game like I say, we had the disappointment of the Argentina game, the second game against Ghana - it's games you look back on and think 'Could I have done better?'

“But that's football. I'm now at an age where I've realised sometimes you're going to play well, sometimes you're not. I'm ready for the next set of games and to apply myself in the right way.”

Rice says a well earned rest in the summer has helped him but he also missed last month’s England camp and the first encounter with Spain after Thomas Tuchel agreed he should sit it out.

‌



View 3 Images Rice admits he wasn't at his best during the World Cup (Image: Julian Finney - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

“I had an honest conversation with the boss who was really understanding,” said Rice. “I still feel like I am building up to being a 100 per cent. But I feel like I am closer to that than what I was a few weeks ago, for sure.

“I think in coming up to 82 caps, I've probably missed three camps in my time with England over an eight, nine-year period now.

“So, I know the importance of playing for England, I know the importance of showing up, being available. It's one of the biggest things to me as well.

‌



“Like Harry Kane speaks about, playing for England is one of the biggest things. You never know when that's going to end, so every time you're here you cannot take that for granted.

“It's one of them things that I'm now here, I'm playing, we had a really good World Cup, we're having a really good Nations League campaign. The lads are young, the lads are fresh. It's something you want to be a part of going forward.”

Rice acknowledged that Spain - the current world and European champions - are the barometer by which everyone else is judged. They are on the back of a 43 game unbeaten run.

View 3 Images Rice sat out England's last meeting with Spain after talking with Thomas Tuchel

‌



The Arsenal midfielder sat out the Spain game at Wembley but watched on from the stands. He believes Spain’s success is built on strong defensive foundations.

Rice said: “It was weird. Weird, watching it as a fan, in a way. I went to the first one with my son which was an unbelievable experience, just me and him. And as for the other games, you obviously watch on the TV.

“Knowing what the lads are trying to build and how the manager works, performances were excellent. When you are watching those games as a fan, you have been around the set-up and you know you want to get straight back in. I am happy I am back in, to be honest with you.

“I'm extremely lucky to play with the back four I'm playing with at Arsenal. If you look at Spain's statistics at the World Cup in conceding goals I think they were the best in defending. Defence wins you titles. Obviously the attack, the flair wins you games.

‌



“Everyone talks about the attacking talent Spain has but look at their centre-backs and how well they play, their full-backs, their midfield helps out their defence. They're one of the best in the world at the minute. You have to credit them for that.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino has very easy choice to make on Bruno Fernandes' Man Utd future
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has very easy choice to make on Bruno Fernandes' Man Utd future

New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino has a laundry list of problems to solve when he arrives at Carrington next week - none more so than the future of his captain

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes remains Man Utd's best and most important player

Perhaps with the odd exception, successful football teams at the highest level of competition have at least one world-class player.

‌



‌



Leicester City, Premier League champions of 2015-16, might be one of those exceptions, although you could possibly claim that Jamie Vardy was, for a period, truly elite.

‌



The current champions are dull to watch but Arsenal have, arguably, a few world-class operators, Declan Rice leading the way.

‌



For all their faults, Manchester United have a world-class player. Bruno Fernandes. And that is why Mauricio Pochettino will position the captain at the heart of his plans to revitalise the club’s fortunes.

It goes without saying that Pochettino has quite a task on his hands. The truth is that Michael Carrick overachieved with the personnel available in the second half of last season and underachieved this season. Simple as that.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The true level of this United squad is somewhere between the one that won 12 of its last 17 Premier League games in the 2025-26 season and the one that has won one of ten in this campaign.

‌



It is not a squad equipped to challenge for the title any time soon, that is for sure. For a start, evidence of the naked eye suggests they are simply not fit enough. That is probably a result of the complacency that comes when you think you have made it when signing for such a grand institution.

And when the principal owner tells you success on the field is not needed for commercial power - as Avram Glazer did - then complacency is hard to get rid of.

‌



Getting the squad physically fit for purpose will be a long haul. It cannot be done mid-season. And while there will surely be some transfer activity after Christmas, the necessary changes in personnel cannot be completed in one window.

View 3 Images His histrionics are unpalatable, but his talent is unquestionable (Image: Getty Images)

‌



That will also be a long haul. The fundamental flaw in United’s recruitment policy has been that they have not pursued the best in class for some time.

Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba. Good players, decent value, but not amongst the best in class. The same applies to so many United signings over the last decade or so.

‌



Which is why Pochettino will lean heavily on Fernandes. There are some who believe the captain is part of the problem.

While there is no doubt his form has not reached the heights of last season, this is nonsense. Fernandes remains United’s best player. His histrionics are not particularly palatable, that is for sure, but he remains United’s best player.

‌



He will be the most creative option at Pochettino’s disposal - by a mile. Of all the signings in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era, he has been the best - by a mile.

There have been some vague mumblings that Fernandes might not fit into Pochettino’s team ethic. What evidence is there for that?

‌



Like everyone else at United, Fernandes could probably be fitter but his commitment on the field has never been questionable.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino will look to build his Man Utd team around the skipper (Image: Luke Hales/Getty Images)

‌



Fernandes’ contract is up at the end of the season but United have an option to extend the agreement by a year - an option they will surely trigger before January 1.

Fernandes, 32, has rejected a couple of new contract offers from United but that is standard negotiating procedure. He might well wait to see the impact made by the new manager before agreeing an extension.

‌



But he will be impressed by Pochettino, that is for certain. Almost as certain as Pochettino being impressed by Fernandes.

You might see a more youthful, vibrant United under Pochettino. For the sake of United fans, let’s hope so.

‌



But Fernandes will still be its leader.

Sports.title: Jordan Pickford discovers where he stands as James Trafford gets Spain nod AGAIN
Sports.content:
Jordan Pickford discovers where he stands as James Trafford gets Spain nod AGAIN

Thomas Tuchel has confirmed James Trafford will start in England's crucial showdown with Spain on Sunday - but insists Jordan Pickford remains his No 1 goalkeeper

View 2 Images James Trafford will start England's game with Spain on Sunday, not Jordan Pickford (Image: Getty)

James Trafford has been told he will start against Spain - and that puts a major doubt over Jordan Pickford’s status as No1.

‌



England boss Thomas Tuchel also revealed fit-again Ezri Konsa will go straight back into the starting line-up against the world champions in the Metropolitano Stadium.

It is a winner-takes-all showdown in the Nations League and that is why it is a surprise that Tuchel has decided to go with Trafford over his established first choice keeper which must raise questions over Pickford’s long-term future.

Tuchel said: “We want to try and see how far Traff is. That hasn't changed. So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match, so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers. And Traff gets the match tomorrow.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“It's only a football match, so hopefully he's not too over-excited or overly nervous, because there's no need to. We trust him.

“But it is different to play for England than to play for your club. And to have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way of course to show up, and to show that you're ready, and for us also to see where he is.

“We know what Jordan can do for us. Jordan is at the moment our No1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments. He played in tournaments and played for me in the World Cup. It's a good goalkeeping group that we built there and they’re pushing themselves.”

England will make changes in defence to try and defeat Spain and end their 43-game unbeaten record with Konsa coming back to steady the ship.

Tuchel says Konsa’s performances this season have been “amazing” and he is set to rerun after a knee issue ruled him out of the win over Croatia. He added: “I saw him when he played his first match for Arsenal after William Saliba’s injury. It just looked like he's always been there. It was seamless.

View 2 Images Pickford has been England's long-term No 1 but his position now appears to be under serious threat

“For us, it’s amazing that he plays on the highest level, competes for every title, is in an atmosphere and in a situation where it really matters that you stay focused and you show up every three days. It's only positives for us.

“He did very well and we gave him the chance to take care of his little niggle. He took it seriously and he showed that we can trust him. He showed up yesterday for individual work, he showed up today for training and he's ready to play.

“I think it's in itself a big match, Spain against England. I think Spain, since years, on an incredible run. They seem impossible to beat. I think we are in a very good moment. And in the best moment also to try and make the seemingly-impossible possible.

"Because we are here to win. We wanted this match desperately. We thought we were very close to beating them in the first match with a good performance. It's an achievement in itself that we already have 12 points. I think it was a tricky group, when we saw the draw.

“So we have 12, and have a final. It's exactly what we want. And I think it's two powerful teams, two teams in a very good place at the moment. Two teams who like to dominate the ball and create chances. We feel in a good place. It's the moment to show up and try to win.”

Sports.title: Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after Arsenal star accused of 'cheating'
Sports.content:
Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after Arsenal star accused of 'cheating'

Liverpool legend Graeme Souness was highly critical of Arsenal star Declan Rice, with the England midfielder now offering a strong response

View 3 Images Declan Rice will win England cap number 82 when he lines up against Spain

Declan Rice has hit back after Graeme Souness claimed the England midfielder is “cheating” and playing “old man’s football.”

‌



‌



Rice is regarded as one of the best midfielders in world football but Liverpool legend Souness claims the Arsenal star plays more like a centre half.

‌



Souness, now a respected TV pundit, said: “A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield. I think he may be a centre-half. He’s back there all the time. It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield.”

‌



Rice, who helped Arsenal to win their first title in 22 years and England to the World Cup semi final in July, said: “For a centre-back, I think my numbers are not bad!

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. I think I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals and to be a top-class centre-back getting those numbers I’m delighted with that!

“Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion probably since my West Ham days, if I’m being honest with you. But it’s one of them things. As an ex-pro you’re going to have an opinion on something.

‌



“I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise. I can’t really say much because he was way before my time … I didn’t really get to see Graeme as a player.

View 3 Images Graeme Souness gave a scathing assessment of Declan Rice (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“Obviously I know him as a pundit. So I’m sure if I met him in person there would be no disrespect there. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. Yeah, it doesn’t matter. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.

“Look, if you speak about, as you said, the positioning and old man’s football, look at Harry Kane. We played him the other week against Bayern Munich, he dropped next to the centre-backs 20-30 times in the game to pick up the ball. The game's different now.”

‌



Rice will be key to England’s hopes of beating Spain in their winner-takes-all Nations League clash in Madrid on Sunday night.

View 3 Images Rice has six goals and 16 assists for Arsenal since the start of last season (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

‌



Rice, who will win his 82nd cap, said: “This is massive. You are going away to the Metropolitano, playing the world champions in a game to see who can top the group. I don’t think it can get any bigger than that.

“We have a massive motive to win the group, to beat Spain, as the away team would be a massive thing for us. Already, the mindset is in a really good place, the manager’s messaging has been really good so we need to go there and put on a performance.”

Sports.title: BBC legend slams 'discipline' after broadcast axe and admits he tunes into rival
Sports.content:
BBC legend slams 'discipline' after broadcast axe and admits he tunes into rival

A BBC icon has explained that he listens to a rival of the broadcaster as a result of the "comprehensive service" it provides

View 2 Images The BBC cut 5 Live's classified results section in 2022 (Image: Leila Coker - WSL, WSL Football via Getty Images)

Mike Ingham has argued that BBC Radio 5 Live has surrendered much of its "discipline" following the controversial choice to scrap its classified football results segment back in 2022. The broadcasting legend has also revealed that he now listens to talkSPORT, which he considers a "comprehensive service."

‌



‌



The 76-year-old formed a partnership with Alan Green for nearly a quarter of a century between 1990 and 2014, commentating on the most significant matches in Britain and across the globe. Ingham and Green provided coverage of FA Cup finals, World Cup tournaments and European competitions, with the former renowned for his articulate style and presentation.

‌



In 2004, Ingham was promoted to the position of 5 Live's chief football correspondent. He stepped away from his position following the 2014 World Cup, bringing an illustrious career to a close, though he has remained an avid listener of the output from his former colleagues and those who followed.

‌



Jesus Owono given maximum ban for tackle that resulted in Jesus de Miguel's tragic death READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford causes issue as Man Utd set to trigger his team-mate's contract clause READ MORE :

Yet the iconic commentator doesn't always support the decisions taken by the BBC, as shown by his disapproval of 5 Live axing their classified segment four years ago. Discussing the decision, Ingham told the Telegraph: "It's like building a house without the bricks.

"Those two-and-a-half minutes were like taking stock at the end of a hurly-burly afternoon. It was a great bit of broadcasting when it was done by James Alexander Gordon, like the shipping forecast.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"I think 5 Live has lost a lot of, not professionalism, but discipline. I was reared on hitting the pips. My family gets so exasperated with me now because I'm such a stickler for time. A lot of that has been lost, it has become much more easy come, easy go."

He added: "I just think the BBC has spread itself too thinly. It's just trying to do everything, as opposed to trying to concentrate on the things it does best.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"For me, the programme should always come before the podcast. That's me though, not being able to move with the times."

‌



A BBC statement issued when they chose to axe 5 Live's results segment said: "We appreciate the strength of feeling towards the classified football results within Sports Report. It's always difficult when a programme with a special history changes, but there are good reasons for the change.

"With the addition of the 5.30pm live Premier League match to our coverage, Sports Report has been condensed into a shorter programme - cut from 1 hour to 25 minutes. The classifieds were taking around 5-7 minutes to read, which would have taken up around a third of the programme - constraining the range of sport we could cover.

‌



View 2 Images Mike Ingham (left) has spoken about the BBC (Image: Getty)

"We'd like to assure our listeners that results from across the football leagues will still be shared during the programme and through the afternoon. Results are also available in full on the BBC Sport website and during Final Score on BBC One. Having a live match at 5.30 is a great addition to the 5 Live schedule."

‌



Ingham has also made the striking admission that he now tunes into BBC Sport's long-standing rival talkSPORT, owing to the network's capacity to deliver a "comprehensive service" to its audience. He said: "I think they [BBC Sport] were complacent about talkSPORT.

"When it began it was a bit blokey, now I think it's a more comprehensive service and the range of presenters they have really makes it work. Simon Jordan is brilliant, Jeff Stelling's there and they do the results at 5 o'clock on a Saturday."
