Mr Anenechukwu said he chose to support the programme because educational resources could create a more lasting impact than a personal celebration.

“This partnership is not charity alone. It is strategy. It is nation-building,” he said.

He urged individuals, businesses, religious organisations and other institutions to support the programme by sponsoring pupils, schools or learning materials.

CTYEEF said achieving its 2040 target would depend on partnerships with governments, corporate organisations, development agencies, educational institutions and private donors.

World.title: 2027: Abiodun unveils 50,400 Renewed Hope Apostles, launches grassroots campaign across Ogun
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has inaugurated 50,400 grassroots political canvassers, christened Renewed Hope Apostles, across the state as part of an aggressive mobilisation strategy to secure electoral victory for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections.

The initiative, which will see the canvassers embark on a coordinated door-to-door campaign across the state’s 236 wards, is designed to deepen grassroots engagement, strengthen the party’s support base and educate voters on the achievements of the APC-led governments at the federal, state and local government levels.

Governor Abiodun disclosed this during a series of strategic meetings with party leaders and stakeholders across the 20 local government areas of the state, attended by local government and ward executives, council chairmen, councillors, governorship and other party candidates, Apex leaders, Governor’s Liaison Officers and political appointees.

The governor explained that the Renewed Hope Apostles would serve as the party’s grassroots communication and mobilisation network, taking verifiable information about government policies, programmes and achievements directly to the electorate.

He said the initiative was particularly important in countering misinformation and ensuring that voters were adequately informed about the impact of government policies on their lives.

“We have called them the Renewed Hope Apostles. They will now begin to propagate so that the people can be better informed because when there is no information, there is misinformation, and that is what we are addressing.

“In the first instance, in Ogun East, we have 15,000 of them, and across the state, we have 50,400. We expect them to multiply and spread the gospel of the party’s performance,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Abiodun said the canvassers had been carefully selected across the local government areas and organised around polling units to ensure that the mobilisation exercise reached voters at the most immediate level of their communities.

According to him, the recruitment and verification process had taken about three months, with the necessary details of the canvassers compiled and verified to ensure an effective and accountable grassroots mobilisation structure.

He said the exercise would provide an opportunity to properly equip the canvassers with information about the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration and the Ogun State Government, enabling them to communicate the benefits of the APC’s policies with clarity and conviction.

Highlighting the impact of the Tinubu administration on Ogun State, Abiodun listed the reconstruction of the Sagamu-Ijebu-Ode-Ore Road, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the facilitation of the Gateway Deep Sea Port, the revival of the Ogun LNG project and the establishment of a major Customs facility in the state.

He noted that these projects, alongside other federal interventions, were strengthening Ogun’s economic prospects, attracting investments, creating employment opportunities and consolidating its position as one of Nigeria’s leading industrial destinations.

The governor described the economic and policy decisions taken by President Tinubu as necessary interventions that had helped stabilise the nation’s economy and set it on the path of sustainable growth.

On the achievements of his administration, Abiodun said Ogun State had witnessed significant improvements in infrastructure, housing, education, healthcare, agriculture, energy and economic empowerment.

He disclosed that his administration had constructed more than 1,700 kilometres of roads across the three senatorial districts, rehabilitated and constructed over 1,600 schools, and provided more than 7,000 housing units now occupied by residents.

In the health sector, he said his administration had equipped and upgraded 160 Primary Healthcare Centres as part of its commitment to providing at least one functional primary healthcare facility in each of the state’s 236 wards.

He added that contracts had recently been awarded for the construction of new hospitals at Odogbolu, Isara and Itori, while the Olabisi Onabanjo University Teaching Hospital had been repositioned to improve healthcare delivery.

The governor also announced the completion of the 250-bed Gateway Medical Centre of Excellence in Abeokuta, which he said had been abandoned by previous administrations.

On power infrastructure, Abiodun said his government had established two independent power plants in Abeokuta to support industrial and social activities, while more than 20,000 farmers had benefited from the distribution of agricultural inputs, including pesticides, fertilisers, seedlings and tractors.

He further disclosed that over 60,000 women had been empowered through the Oko Owo Dapo initiative, while cooperative societies and artisans had received more than N1 billion in financial support to expand their businesses.

In the education sector, the governor said over 7,000 teaching personnel had been recruited and deployed to address manpower shortages in public primary and secondary schools.

Abiodun also highlighted his administration’s aviation initiative, noting that beyond the development of a world-class airport, the state had established an airline whose aircraft had commenced international operations from Lagos to Bangui.

The governor charged the Renewed Hope Apostles to approach their assignment with commitment, discipline and a clear understanding of the party’s achievements, stressing that their responsibility was to communicate with voters, address concerns and mobilise support for the APC.

He also called on party leaders and members to close ranks, put aside personal differences and work collectively towards the success of the party in the forthcoming elections.

According to him, political unity and effective coordination at the grassroots remain indispensable to electoral success.

“A divided party cannot win an election. We must work together as a team, strengthen our relationships and ensure that every member understands the importance of this assignment,” he said.

The governor explained that the stakeholder meetings were also intended to strengthen internal party cohesion, review mobilisation strategies and establish a common direction for the party ahead of the elections.

Prominent party leaders, including the State APC Chairman, Chief Yemi Sanusi; Director-General of the Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council, Senator Lekan Mustapha; Deputy Director-General, Dr. Apaye; Ogun East Senatorial Chairman, Chief Adeleke Adedotun; and APC Chairman in Odeda Local Government, Hon. Musulumi Saka, pledged their commitment to the party’s success.

They assured the governor of their readiness to mobilise members and supporters across their respective constituencies in support of President Tinubu, Governor Abiodun and all APC candidates.

The inauguration and stakeholder engagements have so far covered Remo North, Sagamu, Ikenne, Ijebu North East, Ijebu-Ode, Odogbolu, Ijebu East, Ijebu North, Ifo, Ewekoro, Abeokuta North, Abeokuta South, Odeda and Obafemi-Owode local government areas.

The engagements are part of a broader political outreach programme by Governor Abiodun, who has also held consultations with religious organisations, traders, artisans, traditional worshippers, labour leaders and cooperative societies to build wider support for the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections.

World.title: Police rescue three-year-old girl, 19 other abducted persons in Zamfara
World.content:
The police in Zamfara State have rescued 19 people held captive by suspected bandits for 22 days and a three-year-old girl abducted in a separate incident in the state.

The 19 people, described by the police as women and children, were rescued on Saturday from a suspected bandits’ camp near Kungurmi village, while the girl was freed earlier in the week following the arrest of her 26-year-old paternal aunt.

The police spokesperson in Zamfara, Yazid Abubakar, disclosed the operations in separate statements issued on Friday and Saturday.

Nineteen rescued after 22 days

Mr Abubakar said the 19 victims were abducted from Tungar Haki village, near Wanke, in Gusau Local Government Area, and taken to a camp around Kungurmi.

Acting on intelligence about their location, operatives of the police Anti-Kidnapping Unit, personnel attached to Government House, the State Security Service (SSS) and local hunters carried out a rescue operation at about 10 a.m. on Saturday.

The victims were found unharmed and have since been reunited with their families, according to the police.

However, the command did not disclose whether any suspects were arrested during the operation or whether the kidnappers had demanded or received a ransom.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also provided no breakdown of the victims by age and sex or details of any medical examinations conducted after their rescue.

The Commissioner of Police, Ahmad Muhammad Bello, commended those involved in the operation and urged residents to continue providing information to security agencies.

Aunt arrested over girl’s abduction

In the other incident, police arrested a 26-year-old woman, Saadiya Sahabi, over the alleged abduction of her three-year-old niece in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area.

A man, Abdulganiyu Sahabi, reported to the police on 30 October that his daughter had been abducted two days earlier.

He told investigators that an unidentified caller contacted him on 29 October, claiming to have the child and demanding ₦10 million for her release.

Following investigations, detectives from the State Intelligence Department arrested Ms Sahabi on 10 November in Bela District, Bungudu Local Government Area.

The child was rescued the same day.

The police identified the suspect as the younger sister of the child’s father and alleged that she admitted involvement in the abduction during interrogation.

They did not explain her suspected role in the ransom demand or disclose whether any money was paid.

The girl underwent a medical examination before being reunited with her parents on 12 November.

Investigators are still trying to establish whether other people participated in the abduction. The police have not announced any charges against the suspect.

The two incidents occurred in different parts of Zamfara, and the police have not reported any connection between them.

World.title: Police arrest 12 suspects over theft, political thuggery in Niger State
World.content:
The Niger State Police Command says it has arrested 12 suspects over housebreaking, shop burglary, theft, political thuggery and destruction of property across the state.

The command also said dangerous weapons and several stolen items were recovered during the operations.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Wasiu Abiodun, disclosed this in a crime bulletin issued on Sunday.

According to the statement, Alhassan Abdullahi, 32, and Zahradeen Aliyu, 22, were arrested over alleged housebreaking and theft in the Maje Flyover area of Suleja.

The police said unidentified persons broke into a house on 28 October and stole about 120 litres of diesel stored in three jerrycans, a mobile phone and an undisclosed sum of money.

Following an investigation, Mr Abdullahi was arrested and allegedly identified Mr Aliyu as the receiver of the stolen items.

A search of Mr Aliyu’s residence reportedly led to the recovery of three empty jerrycans, housebreaking tools, including a bolt cutter, a 42-inch television and some clothes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police said both suspects had been charged to court.

In a separate incident, the command arrested a 32-year-old shop caretaker, Victor Peter, over the alleged burglary of five shops along KFF Street, Gidan-Kwano, Minna.

The incident reportedly occurred in the early hours of 5 November, when items valued at more than N2 million were stolen.

The stolen items included two power banks, four traditional outfits, other clothing materials, four pairs of shoes, chargers and a music box.

The police said Mr Peter allegedly confessed to committing the crime alone at about 3:30 a.m., adding that he moved the stolen items to an uncompleted building with the intention of selling them to raise money for betting activities.

READ ALSO: IGP urges hospitals to treat gunshot victims without police reports

Police subsequently took the recovered exhibits into custody, and the suspect was charged in court.

The command also announced the arrest of seven suspects in connection with alleged political thuggery and violence during campaign activities in Minna.

It said six suspects were arrested on November 12 at the Trade Fair Complex, Shango, for allegedly engaging in thuggery during political campaign activities.

The suspects were reportedly found with two cutlasses, four knives, scissors and other dangerous weapons.

Similarly, an alleged notorious thug identified as Anasho was arrested around Tunga on November 13.

The police alleged that he attacked a political campaign team, damaging vehicles, banners and other campaign materials. A cutlass was reportedly recovered from him.

The suspect remains in police custody for further investigation.

In another development, the command arrested two suspects in separate cases involving theft, thuggery and malicious damage to property.

One of them, Lawal Mohammed, 35, was arrested following a complaint that he allegedly broke into a room in a compound at Angwan-Dakoko, Chanchaga, on November 10 and stole 11 wrappers and a power bank.

The police said four of the wrappers and the power bank were recovered from him. He is expected to be charged and brought to court.

Meanwhile, police operatives attached to Maitumbi Division, working with local vigilante members, arrested an 18-year-old suspect, Kabiru Mikailu, following an attack on a residence in Angwan-Kadara.

The incident reportedly occurred at about 11:30 p.m. on November 13, when suspected miscreants attacked a house, damaged a vehicle’s windscreen and broke about four crates of soft drinks.

The police said Mikailu was identified as one of the alleged masterminds of the attack.

During interrogation, he reportedly mentioned six other suspects, identified as Khalifa Usman, Abba Usman, Nafiu, Ali Zagam, Abubakar and others who are currently at large.

Four sticks and two cutlasses were recovered from him, while investigations into the incident are ongoing.

The police command reiterated its commitment to tackling criminal activities and maintaining public order across Niger State.

World.title: AKK gas pipeline set for commissioning amid protest by Kano manufacturers
World.content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd.) says the mainline section of the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline is nearing completion, just as a company demands compensation for its land acquired for the project.

NNPCL said the facility will significantly improve gas availability and boost Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) supply across Northern Nigeria.

The Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Ltd., Bashir Ojulari, disclosed this during an interview in Abuja on Friday.

​According to Mr Ojulari, the AKK Gas Pipeline project is currently 95 per cent complete, with the remaining five per cent covering auxiliary stations and end-user connections.

He noted that expanding gas linkages to additional locations will substantially increase CNG availability across the region.

​Mr Ojulari expects gas delivery to Abuja to begin before the end of 2026 to support power generation, factories, data centres, and industrial hubs, while Kaduna and Kano are scheduled to receive supplies by 2027.

He added that NNPCL successfully raised $1.5 billion for the project based solely on projected pipeline throughput.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

​“The main pipeline of the AKK gas project, running all the way from Ajaokuta through Kaduna to Kano, has been completed,” Mr Ojulari said.

“The remaining five per cent involves completing some of the stations needed to link offtakes from the main pipeline to end-users.

​“We are hoping that before the end of the year, we will deliver gas to Abuja as the first phase, and by 2027, we will extend supply to Kaduna and Kano. However, keep in mind that this is just the main line. From there, we will build more connections to other areas.

​“We have already addressed the initial phase because we now have the Abuja power plant. As we move further north and establish those connections, CNG availability will increase phenomenally.

“We still need to extend the network toward Maiduguri and Sokoto, so there is more work to be done—but it is now much easier than transporting gas all the way from Port Harcourt to those locations.”

​He explained that the infrastructure creates a far more accessible supply network, simplifying regional gas distribution.

While acknowledging that further extensions are necessary to reach cities like Maiduguri and Sokoto, Mr Ojulari emphasised that the AKK pipeline provides a vital backbone that makes future expansions considerably easier.

​The AKK Gas Pipeline is a 40-inch, 614-kilometre pipeline system running from Ajaokuta in Kogi State to Kano, complete with intermediate and terminal gas facilities designed to transport natural gas to commercial and industrial off-takers across Northern Nigeria.

Protest

Meanwhile, A.B. Janruwa Enterprises has demanded compensation for more than four hectares of land allegedly taken over in Kano State for a development corridor linked to the AKK Gas Pipeline Project.

The Kano-based manufacturing company said the disputed land, located in the Chalawa Industrial Area of Kumbotso Local Government Area, was acquired over several years from local farmers and earmarked for a multi-billion-naira factory expansion project expected to create more than 2,000 jobs.

According to the company, contractors working on behalf of government authorities recently began fencing the property, which the company later discovered had been incorporated into a proposed industrial layout associated with the AKK gas pipeline development corridor.

Development must not come at the expense of justice

Speaking on the matter, the company’s manager, Abdullahi Hashim, said it supports industrial development and strategic investments such as the AKK pipeline but believes that affected businesses should not bear the costs alone.

According to him, the company was shocked to discover physical activities taking place on the land despite what it describes as the absence of formal notification or compensation arrangements.

The dispute highlights a broader concern around large-scale infrastructure projects in Nigeria: whether landowners’ rights are being adequately protected during acquisition processes.

For A.B. Janruwa Enterprises, the issue is not opposition to development but a demand for fairness, due process and lawful compensation.

Lawyer questions due process

The company’s legal representative, Umar Ahmad-Umar, said it was never served with a revocation notice and only learned of the developments after physical activities had already begun on the land.

The lawyer argued that compensation is not merely a financial obligation. “It is a fundamental safeguard designed to balance public interest with private rights and to ensure that citizens and businesses do not unfairly shoulder the burden of national development projects.”

Government assures landowners of compensation

Responding to the allegations, Murtala Shehu, Director of Public Enlightenment at the Kano State Ministry of Lands and Physical Planning, stated that all affected landowners would be compensated and urged the company to remain calm.

The official assured that no land would be forcibly taken over and described the project as intended to advance Kano State’s economic prosperity.

Mr Shehu appealed for patience while government processes continue.

Hussaini Bukar, a development expert, argues that paying prompt and adequate compensation protects constitutional property rights, prevents costly disputes and litigation, and encourages investor confidence.

He added that while development is key for national growth, it cannot be done at the expense of investors.

‘’Paying compensation demonstrates respect for affected communities and businesses, and enhances public support for strategic national projects, Mr Bukar said.

He argued that if land is acquired in the public interest, compensation must follow under the law.

That principle, he added, is not only a legal obligation but an essential foundation for sustainable development and investor confidence in Nigeria

World.title: From 51 Iweka Road to Ebinpejo Lane, Idumota, these marketers powered Nollywood’s home-video boom
World.content:
Long before Netflix, Prime Video, and other streaming platforms courted Nigerian filmmakers, the country’s movie industry ran on videocassettes, Video CDs (VCDs) and, later, DVDs, sold from cramped shops in Lagos and Onitsha.

Between the late 1990s and the 2000s, the era now remembered as the home-video period, a network of marketers financed, packaged and distributed the films that gave Nollywood its first mass audience. Copies moved from Idumota in Lagos and Onitsha in Anambra State to the markets of Aba, Abia State, and Accra, Ghana, reaching viewers hungry for stories in which they recognised themselves.

For many Nigerians, their legacy lives on in a single sound. Every trailer of the era closed with a fast-talking, booming voiceover:

“Marketed and distributed by [Marketer Name] Films, No. 1/3 Pound Road, Aba; 51 Iweka Road, Onitsha; and 7 Ebinpejo Lane, Idumota, Lagos. Grab your copy NOW!”

Shop numbers varied by marketer, but the routine became one of the most nostalgic tropes in Nigerian pop culture.

PREMIUM TIMES profiles the figures whose capital and commercial instinct, often exercised from small offices in Idumota and Onitsha, put Nigerian films before their first mass audience.

Kenneth Nnebue (NEK Video Links)

An electronics and video-cassette dealer, Kenneth Nnebue began in Onitsha before moving to Idumota, then the centre of the cassette trade. His company, NEK Video Links, released ‘Living in Bondage’ in 1992, directed by Chris Obi Rapu. The two-part Igbo-language drama about money rituals and moral ruin is widely credited with igniting the home-video boom. Mr Nnebue was no filmmaker by training, but he had a trader’s feel for what the market wanted. He hired Mr Rapu for the first part and Christian Onu for the second, yet insisted on being present at shoots and controlling how scripts were interpreted. The film’s success pushed him further. In 1994, he produced Glamour Girls, one of the earliest major English-language home videos, which carried Nigerian film beyond Igbo speakers to a wider national and West African audience.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Chukwuka Emelionwu (Kas-Vid)

Known across the industry as Kas-Vid, Mr Emelionwu produced ‘Aki na Ukwa’, the film that made Osita Iheme and Chinedu Ikedieze household names. His reputation rested on spotting talent: Kas-Vid gave Genevieve Nnaji her breakout role in the 1998 drama ‘Most Wanted’, launching her into nationwide stardom. He also executive produced ‘Osuofia in London’ (2003), among the best-selling Nollywood comedies of all time, and produced ‘Mr. Ibu in London’, ‘The Last Burial’ and ‘Isakaba’, creating character brands that outlived their creator. Mr Emelionwu died in January 2018 in a road accident on the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway while travelling to his home state, Anambra.

Ojiofor Ezeanyaeche (OJ Productions)

Mr Ezeanyaeche operated under the business name, OJ Productions. His younger brother, Arinze Ezeanyaeche of A.2.Z. Productions and Uzochukwu of Solid Movies International also became prominent Nollywood producers and marketers under his mentorship

Some of his most popular classic films include Blood Money (1997), Diamond Ring (1998), Igodo (1999), 2 Rats (2003), Abuja Connections (2003), Police Recruit (2003), and Behind a Smile (2009). After dominating the early home video market, he temporarily stepped away from film production to focus on his other business ventures. In 2020, after years away from the scene, he staged a highly publicised comeback with his passion project, Our Jesus Story.

Gabriel Okoye (Gabosky Films)

Better known as Igwe, the founder of Gabosky Films produced classics such as Nneka the Pretty Serpent and Battle of Musanga. His most consequential bet came in 2013, when he secured over N1 billion from the Bank of Industry to build G-Media, a nationwide distribution network meant to formalise the industry and curb piracy. The plan envisaged 25 stores, 30 regional distributors and 4,000 community distribution points. However, the plan collapsed. Mr Okoye alleged that pirates colluded with cinema operators and officials to frustrate the platform, leaving him bankrupt with his collateral still held by the bank.

Ikechukwu Nnadi (Andy Best)

Also known as Andy Best, Mr Nnadi began producing in the 1980s, making him one of the trade’s older hands. His titles included ‘My Sweet Sister’, ‘Pretty Angels’ and ‘Ikuku’, a 1995 release starring Pete Edochie that became one of his biggest successes. His films circulated widely through the southeast’s distribution networks. He died in March 2024 after a prolonged illness, prompting tributes from across the industry.

The Amaco Brothers

Gabriel and Damian Moses ran Amaco Investments from the Iweka Road commercial hub in Onitsha, alongside a presence in Lagos’s Alaba International Market. The company was known for financing large ensemble casts, comedies and high-stakes ritual dramas, including 1 Dollar (starring Nkem Owoh), ‘Standing Order’ (2005), ‘When God Says Yes’, ‘Romantic Attraction’, ‘Old School’ and ‘Holy Cross ‘.

Sunny Nwatu (Great Sunny Collins Production)

Mr Nwatu operated under the business name of Great Sunny Collins Production. He conceived and executive-produced the 2004 blockbuster drama ‘World Apart’ (directed by Tchidi Chikere). The film starred Ini Edo (in her star-making role as Uli), Kenneth Okonkwo, Liz Benson, and Prof. Laz Ekwueme. It became one of the highest-selling and most celebrated Nollywood royal romance movies of the 2000s. He was also known for movies like ‘Billionaires Club’ (2003), ‘Onye Eze’ (2001), ‘Scores to Settle’ (1998), ‘Witches’ (1998), ‘Little Angels’ (2004), and ‘GSM Wahala’(2014).

Osita Okeke (Ossy Affason)

Known as Ossy Affason, he frequently worked alongside prominent names like Bimbo Manuel, Ejike Asiegbu, Rachael Oniga, and Teco Benson. His face became familiar to fans who watched the classic VCD and VHS movies distributed from major Nigerian commercial hubs. He produced ‘State of Emergency’, ‘ The Corridors of Power’ (2005), and ‘Be My Val’

Gbenga Adewusi (Bayowa Films)

Trading as Bayowa Films and Records, Mr Adewusi helped launch major gospel music and drama stars. Notably, he produced and distributed projects for figures like Evang. Ebenezer Obey and Yinka Ayefele in the gospel industry, and Babatunde Omidina (“Baba Suwe”) and Yomi Fabiyi in Nollywood. Some of the movies he is known for include ‘Orefunmi’, ‘Aditu’, and ‘Eye Owiwi’ (2017).

Rasaq Abdullahi (Corporate Pictures Nigeria Limited)

Alhaji Abdullahi Abdulrasaq, popularly known as Sheikh Movie and the man behind Corporate Pictures Nigeria Limited, is a veteran Yoruba Nollywood film marketer, producer, and investor whose career spans nearly three decades. He established the company after starting with a video-rental club in Lagos, turning his passion for collecting films into a business that expanded into film production, marketing, and distribution. His early industry collaborations included actor-producers Akeem Alimi, popularly known as Ajala Jalingo, Taiwo Hassan (Ogogo), and the late Muyideen Alade Aromire. His first marketed film was ‘Adegbesan’, produced by Ajala Jalingo, while Corporate Pictures later became known for distributing Yoruba films through physical video formats, television, and digital platforms, including YouTube.

The End of an Era

Today, that once-thriving Marketing business that brought Nollywood to the spotlight is fading.

The rise of smartphones, faster internet, and streaming platforms has changed how audiences consume not just films but music too.

Services such as YouTube, Netflix, and Spotify offer instant access to content without buying physical copies or owning disc players. As manufacturers phase out optical drives and consumers embrace digital convenience, even improved formats such as DVDs and Blu-ray have struggled to maintain their former appeal.

Piracy further weakened legitimate disc sales, reducing earnings for filmmakers and distributors who once depended on physical copies.

For Nollywood, the transition has opened new avenues for reaching global audiences through streaming services and cinema releases. Still, it has also disrupted the traditional distribution networks that once helped build the industry. Challenges such as online piracy and the difficulty of converting digital views into sustainable revenue persist.

Meanwhile, some of these marketers have created YouTube channels; others have moved into new ventures outside film marketing.

World.title: Bandits attack Zamfara mosque, kill APC e-registration supervisor, abduct worshippers
World.content:
A supervisor of the All Progressives Congress (APC) e-registration exercise, Nasiru Sani, has been killed by suspected bandits during an early-morning attack on a mosque in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area of Zamfara State.

According to a statement issued by the Zamfara State APC E-Registration Coordinator, Yusuf Idris, the attackers stormed the Lowcost Mosque in Kaura Namoda town on Sunday while congregants were observing the early-morning Subhi (Fajr) prayers.

The statement said Mr Sani was fatally shot during the attack, while an unconfirmed number of other worshippers were abducted by the assailants before they fled the area.

In his condolence statement released on Sunday, Mr Idris expressed deep shock over the killing, describing the deceased as a dedicated member of the party’s registration team.

“I received with deep shock and sadness the news of the passing away of one of my Supervisors of the APC E-Registration in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area, Hon. Nasiru Sani Kaura,” Mr Idris stated.

“Hon. Nasiru Sani lost his life as a result of a bandits’ attack while performing the Subhi prayer at the Lowcost Mosque in Kaura Namoda, where he was shot dead”, he added.

Residents told PREMIUM TIMES that the gunmen targeted the Low Cost residential area of Kaura Namoda town at dawn, taking advantage of the quiet morning hours to strike the mosque during prayers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Several worshippers were taken captive, sparking renewed panic among residents.

Communities in Kaura Namoda LGA have experienced repeated security breaches in recent months

Bandits had, in October, attacked Kaura Namoda town for over three hours after bypassing local vigilante fortifications via a riverine route, killing seven members of the local Joint Task Force (JTF) and abducting 38 residents.

Also, in August, suspected bandits killed six soldiers and abducted over 70 residents in the Kasuwar Daji community of the LGA. However, troops later foiled another mass abduction attempt along the Unguwar Rogo axis.

READ ALSO: Gov Lawal appoints 282 new aides to strengthen inclusive governance

The bandits in June attacked an off-campus student residence in the same Low Cost area of Kaura Namoda, abducting seven students of the Federal Polytechnic, Kaura Namoda, who were later rescued by security operatives.

World.title: Rebecca Omokamo Godwin-Isaac receives The Sun Real Estate Icon Award 2026 in Lagos
World.content:
Dr (Mrs) Rebecca Omokamo Godwin-Isaac, Chief Executive Officer of Homadil Realty Limited and Summit Estate Global Limited, has received The Sun Real Estate Icon Award 2026 in recognition of her contributions to Nigeria’s property sector. Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, founder of The Sun Newspaper and The Sun Publishing Limited, personally presented the award to her at the Expo Convention Centre, Eko Hotels and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Friday, 13 November 2026.

The ceremony, themed Nation Builders, celebrated Nigerians recognised for leadership, enterprise and service across several fields. In its “post-event report” (https://thesun.ng/night-of-bliss-splendour-razzmatazz/), The Sun confirmed Godwin-Isaac as a recipient of the Real Estate Icon distinction. For her, the occasion was a national acknowledgement of an entrepreneurial journey and the property-development work associated with the businesses she leads.

The recognition had been set in motion before the Lagos ceremony. The Sun’s Managing Director and Editor-in-Chief, Onuoha Ukeh, led a delegation that formally notified Godwin-Isaac of her selection during a visit in Abuja. She welcomed the decision and thanked the newspaper’s Board of Editors, describing the honour as a source of encouragement to continue contributing to the industry.

In its “published profile” (https://thesun.ng/rebecca-omokamo-godwin-isaac-a-reputation-for-long-term-value-creation/), The Sun highlighted her experience in business development, market research and contract negotiation. Her education, as reported by the newspaper, includes degrees from the University of Maiduguri, the National Open University of Nigeria and the University of South Wales, alongside Harvard Business School’s General Management Programme and a doctorate in Real Estate Economics and Finance from American Management University.

The recognition places her among Nigerian women whose professional lives challenge the assumption that property development and large-scale business leadership are predominantly male pursuits. Her emphasis on entrepreneurship, learning and long-term planning also provides a wider context for an award centred on real estate.

Much of her professional work centres on Homadil Realty Limited, which operates in Abuja’s property sector with activities spanning residential development, construction coordination, brokerage and project management.

For homebuyers and investors, those demands extend beyond attractive designs and locations. Title verification, construction standards, transparent terms and delivery timelines are central to responsible real estate development. In an expanding city such as Abuja, developers must align commercial ambition with the practical needs of future residents.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Godwin-Isaac also heads Summit Estate Global Limited, whose residential development at Apo-Dutse has become a visible part of her property-development portfolio. The project illustrates the scale of the planning and coordination involved in creating a new residential community.

The project’s plans moved into the public spotlight when Summit Estate Global held its groundbreaking on 14 February 2026 at Cadastral Zone B14, Apo-Dutse, Abuja. The development is planned to comprise approximately 180 residential units, including detached homes, semi-detached homes and flats, together with supporting facilities. These are proposed development figures, not a statement that the homes have already been completed.

The “News Agency of Nigeria reported” (https://nannews.ng/shettima-urges-estate-developers-to-uphold-standards-professionalism/) that Vice President Kashim Shettima was represented at the groundbreaking by his Senior Special Assistant on Legal and Compliance, Bashir Maidugu. The representative encouraged developers to prioritise proper title documentation, construction quality and professional estate management.

The same report identified JI Construct Limited among the construction firms represented at the event. Rebecca’s husband, Engineer Isaac Ishaku Yusuf, is the Chief Executive Officer of JI Construct Limited, bringing construction and project-management expertise to residential development.

The significance of the Apo-Dutse project ultimately rests on the translation of its plans into a well-managed residential environment, supported by clear documentation, effective construction and reliable communication with purchasers.

Beyond her work in property development, Godwin-Isaac has advocated opportunities for girls and women to gain education, confidence and greater economic independence. Earlier coverage by “The Guardian” (https://guardian.ng/specials/nigerias-most-impactful-women-in-leadership-2/) identified her with The Girl Yesterday, The Woman Today, an initiative associated with mentoring and support for girls and women.

Her advocacy reflects a broader view of success: that commercial enterprise can sit alongside efforts to equip others to pursue their ambitions. The Sun’s recognition brings renewed attention to these interests as well as to her role in Abuja’s real estate industry.

For Rebecca Omokamo Godwin-Isaac, the 2026 award marks an important professional milestone. For Homadil Realty Limited and Summit Estate Global Limited, the enduring measure will be progress that can be independently assessed through responsible development and completed projects. The Lagos ceremony celebrated recognition already earned; the lasting legacy will depend on the communities built and opportunities created in the years ahead.

World.title: Adeleke demotes Osun traditional rulers over pro APC stance
World.content:
Gov Ademola Adeleke of Osun State

By Shina Abubakar Osogbo

The Governor Ademola Adeleke-led administration in Osun State has demoted two traditional rulers, the Alagunbeelewo of Agunbeelewo and the Olu of Irepodun, in Osogbo, the State capital.

The demotion of the part 2 traditional rulers was contained in a letter by the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, dated November 5, signed for the Permanent Secretary by one Wale Alliyu and copied the Ataoja of Osogbo.

The two separate letters addressed to the affected monarchs, stated that the State Executive Council presided over by the Governor on October 23rd has approved their de-recognise their stools as part 2 traditional rulers back to that minor chieftaincy.

“I am directed to inform you that the State Executive Council ably led by His Excellency Senator Ademola Jackson Nurudeen Adeleke has approved the de-recognition of your stool as Part II (Recognized) stool under the Chief’s Law (Cap, 25) Laws of Osun State, 2002 with effect from 23rd October, 2026.

“By this de-recognition, your stool now reverts to a Minor Chieftaincy to which Part III of the Chief’s Law applies and consequently, all the rights, privileges and allowances being enjoyed as a recognized Chief will by this development cease.

Although the letter did not state any reason for the demotion but the Alagunbeelewo of Agunbeelewo, Chief Maruf Olayiwola disclosed that they were both alleged of associating with the APC instead of the Accord party in the state.

“It is unfortunate that till now, no one disclosed our offence but we were told that we are not associating with Accord party and we did not collect money from anyone. We have friends in the APC and cannot deny our relationship with them. I believe that is not enough reason to sack us from the stool.

“Governor Adeleke should not allow some persons to reduce the office of the Governor to that of settling personal grudges for the sake of posterity”, he said.

Meanwhile, a civil society organisation, Local Government Development Initiative (LGDI), berated the State Government for acting lawless over the matter.

Its Spokesperson Adeniyi Faith while addressing newsmen in Osogbo on Sunday, counselled the State Government not to politicise traditional institutions in the state to ensure its sanctity.

“We wish to remind Governor Adeleke that the power of a state government over traditional institutions is not unlimited. Such powers must be exercised strictly in accordance with the applicable laws, established procedures, principles of natural justice and the constitutional guarantee of fair hearing.

“The government must demonstrate the legal authority, procedural compliance and legitimate grounds for every decision it takes concerning the appointment, suspension or removal of a traditional ruler. Political authority must never be mistaken for unlimited authority.

“We are not suggesting that traditional rulers are above the law or cannot be removed under any circumstances. However, where the law prescribes procedures for such removal, those procedures must be followed without manipulation, political intimidation or selective application.

“Governor Adeleke must understand that traditional rulership is not a toy that he can pick up, throw away or manipulate whenever he feels like doing so. The traditional institution is bigger than any political administration, and its dignity must be preserved beyond the tenure of any governor”, he said.

World.title: Nasarawa 2027: Adamu unveils plans for security, jobs, roads, electricity
World.content:
The Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has unveiled plans to improve security, agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment if elected governor in 2027.

Adamu outlined his priorities in a five-minute campaign video, saying his experience as a police officer and former Inspector-General of Police had prepared him to serve the state.

He said he would bring the same commitment to protecting lives that guided his over three decades in the Nigeria Police Force to governing Nasarawa.

“For over three decades, I served Nigeria as a police officer and as your Inspector-General of Police. My duty was to protect lives. Today, I bring that same duty to Nasarawa State to serve as your governor,” he said.

The former police chief said he had travelled across the state’s local government areas and wards, where he observed challenges facing farmers, rural communities and public institutions.

He listed poor roads, inadequate hospital and school facilities, limited access to clean water and unreliable electricity among the problems requiring urgent attention.

Outlining his security plans, Adamu said an SDP administration would build security structures from the ward level to strengthen protection across communities.

On agriculture, he promised to provide farmers with tractors and other support, while prioritising the construction and maintenance of roads, particularly in rural areas.

“We will put tractors in the hands of our farmers, and this time we will not just promise roads; we will build them and maintain them, reaching the rural communities that have been left behind for too long,” he said.

Adamu also pledged to improve education through investment in teachers, modern classrooms and digital learning tools. He said his administration would work with communities at the ward level to improve academic performance.

On youth employment, the SDP candidate said existing skill acquisition centres would be linked to employers and start-up support to ensure that graduates could secure jobs or establish businesses.

“So, training turns into livelihood, not just a certificate,” he said.

He also promised to strengthen the state water board and expand existing water infrastructure to connect more homes and farms to reliable supplies.

Adamu promises to complete Farin-Ruwa dam

The former IGP identified the completion of the Farin-Ruwa dam in Wamba Local Government Area as a priority, lamenting that the project had remained unfinished for more than 20 years.

He said completing the dam would help generate electricity for homes, schools and industries across the state.

Adamu further promised to deploy digital technology to monitor government projects and public spending, saying the approach would promote transparency and accountability.

On solid minerals, he said Nasarawa’s deposits of lithium, tin, columbite, limestone and marble should translate into tangible benefits for residents.

He pledged to ensure that mining companies operating in the state created jobs for local youths, protected host communities and paid their statutory obligations transparently.

“Our lithium, our tin, our solid minerals will no longer simply leave Nasarawa State. They will build the state,” he said.

Adamu said his development agenda would be implemented ward by ward and local government by local government, urging residents to support his ambition to build what he described as a secure, prosperous and modern Nasarawa.

World.title: Meet African countries home to some of the world’s oldest universities
World.content:
Africa is home to some of the world’s oldest centres of higher learning, with educational institutions that began centuries before many of the universities commonly associated with Europe’s academic history.

From Islamic centres of scholarship in North Africa to historic institutions in West Africa, the continent has a long tradition of organised education, research and intellectual development.

Some of these institutions started as mosques and religious schools before evolving into universities, while others emerged as

colleges during the 19th century.

Here are six African countries home to some of the world’s oldest universities and higher-learning institutions.

1. Tunisia – Ez-Zitouna University (737 AD)

Tunisia is home to Ez-Zitouna University, one of the oldest centres of higher learning in the world, with an educational history dating back to the eighth century.

Located in Tunis, the institution traces its origins to the Great Mosque of Ez-Zitouna, founded in 734 AD. According to the university’s official historical account, the teaching of Islamic sciences began there around 737 AD.

Over the centuries, the institution became an important centre for Islamic scholarship, teaching subjects including Islamic jurisprudence, philosophy, mathematics, medicine and astronomy.

It also attracted prominent scholars, including the renowned North African historian Ibn Khaldun, who studied at the institution.

Ez-Zitouna remains an important institution for Islamic studies and is widely regarded as one of the oldest continuously operating educational traditions in the Arab and Islamic world.

2. Morocco – University of Al-Qarawiyyin (859 AD)

Morocco is home to the University of Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, an institution widely recognised as the world’s oldest existing and continually operating educational institution.

Founded in 859 AD, Al-Qarawiyyin was established as a mosque and centre of learning by Fatima al-Fihri, a Muslim woman who reportedly used her inheritance to finance its construction.

The institution gradually developed into a major centre of Islamic scholarship, attracting students and scholars from different parts of Africa and beyond.

Its academic activities historically covered Islamic theology, law, Arabic grammar, mathematics and astronomy, among other subjects.

Al-Qarawiyyin’s historical significance extends beyond its age. Its establishment demonstrates the important role African women played in supporting education and intellectual development centuries ago.

Today, the institution remains part of Morocco’s higher education system and continues to preserve its long-standing tradition of Islamic learning.

3. Egypt – Al-Azhar University (970 AD)

Egypt is home to Al-Azhar University, another historic African institution that has played a significant role in global education and Islamic scholarship for more than 1,000 years.

Located in Cairo, Al-Azhar traces its origins to 970 AD, when construction of the Al-Azhar Mosque began under the Fatimid dynasty. The mosque was inaugurated in 972 AD, and educational activities developed shortly afterwards.

It became a major centre for Islamic learning, attracting scholars and students from across the Muslim world.

Over the centuries, Al-Azhar expanded its academic influence, becoming particularly renowned for Islamic theology, jurisprudence and Arabic studies.

The institution underwent significant reforms in the modern era. In 1961, legislation formally established Al-Azhar as a university, expanding its academic structure to include several faculties.

Today, it remains one of the world’s most influential Islamic educational institutions, offering programmes in religious studies, medicine, engineering and other disciplines.

4. Mali – University of Sankore (14th century)

Mali is home to one of Africa’s most celebrated historical centres of learning, the University of Sankore in Timbuktu.

Sankore formed part of Timbuktu’s remarkable intellectual history, particularly during the 15th and 16th centuries, when the city became a major centre of Islamic scholarship and trans-Saharan trade.

According to UNESCO, Timbuktu was home to the prestigious Koranic University of Sankore, alongside numerous other religious schools.

At the height of its intellectual influence, the city reportedly had about 180 Koranic schools and 25,000 students.

Scholars studied subjects including Islamic theology, law, literature and other areas of knowledge, while the city also became famous for its manuscripts and libraries.

The Sankore Mosque, which dates to the 14th century, remains an important historical monument in Timbuktu.

Although Sankore does not operate today as a conventional modern university, its historical contribution makes Mali an important part of the story of Africa’s early higher education system. UNESCO World Heritage Centre+1

5. Sierra Leone – Fourah Bay College (1827)

Sierra Leone is home to Fourah Bay College, one of the oldest Western-style institutions of higher learning in sub-Saharan Africa.

Established in Freetown in 1827 by Anglican missionaries, the college was created to provide higher education and train teachers and clergy.

Its establishment marked an important development in the history of Western education in the region, attracting students from different parts of West Africa.

The institution later became affiliated with Durham University in England in 1876, allowing its students to obtain degrees through the British university.

Fourah Bay College played a significant role in producing some of West Africa’s earliest educated professionals and political and religious leaders.

Among its notable historical students was Samuel Ajayi Crowther, who became the first African Anglican bishop.

The college is now part of the University of Sierra Leone and remains an important institution in the country’s educational history.

6. South Africa – University of Cape Town (1829)

South Africa is home to the University of Cape Town (UCT), the country’s oldest university and one of the oldest higher-education institutions in Africa.

UCT traces its origins to 1829, when it was established as the South African College, initially operating as a school for boys with a small higher-education component.

The institution gradually expanded its academic activities during the 19th century, particularly following the discovery of gold and diamonds in South Africa, which increased demand for skilled professionals.

Between 1880 and 1900, it developed into a fully fledged university, expanding its academic departments, research facilities and student population.

It also made progress in women’s education, admitting four women to its chemistry class on a trial basis in 1886.

Today, UCT is one of Africa’s leading research universities, with a strong international reputation across disciplines including medicine, engineering, business, law and the sciences.

Its long history makes it one of the continent’s most significant institutions of higher learning.

Vanguard News

World.title: List of African countries that have their own unique calendars
World.content:
Several African countries have calendars that are distinct from the Gregorian calendar, either because they maintain traditional systems of dating or because their religious and cultural communities follow their own calendars.

The most notable example is Ethiopia, which has a separate calendar system used for official civil purposes.

Other countries have indigenous or religious calendars that remain culturally significant, although they are not necessarily used for government administration.

African countries with unique calendar systems

1. Ethiopia – Ethiopian (Ge’ez) Calendar

Ethiopia operates a calendar that is approximately seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar. It has 13 months: 12 months of 30 days and a final month called Pagume, which has five or six days. Its New Year usually falls on September 11.

2. Egypt – Coptic Calendar

The Coptic calendar descends from the ancient Egyptian calendar and is still used by the Coptic Orthodox Church. It has 13 months, with 12 months of 30 days and a short 13th month. Its New Year is known as Nayrouz.

3. Eritrea – Ge’ez Calendar

Eritrean Orthodox Christians follow the Ge’ez calendar, which is closely related to Ethiopia’s calendar. Its New Year is called Kidus Yohannes and is celebrated around September 11. Eritrea uses the Gregorian calendar for official administration.

4. Morocco – Amazigh (Berber) Calendar

The Amazigh calendar is used traditionally by Berber communities. It follows an agricultural year and marks its New Year, Yennayer, around January 12–14. Morocco recognises Yennayer as a public holiday.

5. Algeria – Amazigh Calendar

Algeria also observes the Amazigh agricultural calendar. Yennayer marks the beginning of the traditional year and is celebrated as an important cultural occasion.

6. Nigeria – Igbo Traditional Calendar

The Igbo calendar, known as Ọgụ́àfọ̀ Ị̀gbò, has 13 months in its traditional structure. Its week consists of four market days: Eke, Orie, Afọ and Nkwọ. It is used in traditional religious, cultural and market activities, although different Igbo communities may calculate it differently.

7. Ghana – Akan Calendar

The Akan people use a traditional 42-day cycle known as Adaduanan, combining a six-day week and a seven-day week. It helps determine traditional festivals, ceremonies and important cultural events. Similar practices are found among Akan communities in Côte d’Ivoire.
