World.title: More than 900 US flights cancelled Sunday after Friday’s ground stop
World.content:
…FAA expects flight schedules to recover by late Sunday

By Juliet Umeh

More than 900 flights scheduled for Sunday in the United States had been cancelled by late Saturday as airlines continued to recover from a nationwide ground stop imposed by the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA.

FlightAware, a flight-tracking service, recorded 910 cancellations for Sunday, with the figure rising. More than 6,400 flights were cancelled on Saturday, following about 9,200 on Friday.

The FAA order halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours on Friday. Although it was lifted that evening, passengers continued to face cancellations and delays as airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crews.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said, “I do think the worst is behind us,” but added that “a significant amount of recovery work” remained. He apologised to travellers, saying: “I’m sorry that we put you through this, but we did it for the right reasons.”

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption began during work to replace old copper telecommunications lines with fibre-optic cables at an FAA facility. A router involved in the upgrade overloaded parts of the network, affecting air traffic communications and radar systems.

“We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,” Duffy said, adding that the surge caused “issues with our communication with airplanes” and disrupted radar feeds.

Officials are investigating whether the problem resulted from an installation error or faulty equipment. “We haven’t determined what the fault was,” Duffy said.

Bedford said airlines expected to restore their schedules by late Sunday. “Based on everything that we’re hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they’ll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday,” he said.

The FAA said it ordered the ground stop as a safety measure after communications problems affected 17 of its 22 en-route air traffic control centres. Bedford said, “No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost.”

He also said there was “zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related.”

World.title: NDLEA arrests American basketballer over 34kg cannabis consignment
World.content:
Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) have intercepted a 25.05 kilograms consignment of methamphetamine at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos.

The agency’s Director, Media and Advocacy, Mr Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday in Abuja.

Babafemi said that the drugs were concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals imported from South Africa.

He said that the NDLEA operatives arrested the 56-year-old trafficker who had lived in South Africa for over two decades under a stolen identity.

He added that the meth suspect was arrested on Wednesday at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa.

“A thorough search of his two travelling boxes led to the recovery of twenty-five parcels of a white crystalline substance, which tested positive for methamphetamine with a total weight of 25.05kg.

“The parcels had been carefully concealed inside packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products in a bid to beat security screening.

“The 56-year-old suspect holds both Nigerian and South African passports and has been resident in South Africa for over 24 years.

“During preliminary interview, he confessed that he adopted the fake Nigerian name after using forged documents to gain entry into South Africa and had continued to use that identity ever since.

“He further stated that he was contracted by a South Africa-based man to deliver the illicit consignment in Nigeria for a fee of R20,000,”he said.

Babafemi further disclosed that the agency’s operatives at the same airport, arrested an American professional basketball player over a 33.95kg shipment of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, from Thailand.

Babafemi said that on Wednesday, acting on credible intelligence, NDLEA operatives at the MMIA intercepted a 28-year-old American citizen who arrived in Lagos aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand via Dubai.

He said that the suspect, who was placed under discreet surveillance upon arrival, was observed abandoning his two checked-in bags before attempting to exit the airport with only his carry-on luggage.

“He was promptly apprehended at the airport car park.

“A search of the two abandoned bags, both bearing his name tag, revealed sixteen parcels of Loud in each, totalling thirty-two parcels with a combined weight of 33.95 kilograms.

“A tracking device was also recovered from the bags. The suspect, a native of Savannah, Georgia, USA, claimed he has lived in Thailand since October 2025 where he plays professional basketball.

“The suspect said he came to Nigeria on holiday to build networks for his basketball career.

“A forensic examination of his mobile phone revealed information pointing to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity,”he said

World.title: Revenue leakages: FG to deploy export automation system as non-oil sector hits over $6b
World.content:
By Daniel Abia

P/Harcourt

The Federal Government has concluded the process to deploy an automated export processing system to strengthen regulatory compliance and curb revenue leakages in the exports sector.

This was disclosed by, Mr Tola Fakolade, the Project Director, National Single Window (NSW), at the Phase Two Export Sensitization Joint Stakeholders Engagement in Port Harcourt on Thursday.

The event had as its theme, “Unlocking Endless Possibilities: A Comprehensive Outlook on the NSW Project”.

Fakolade described the NSW as a Federal Government initiative designed to streamline international trade through a unified digital platform for trade documentation, permits and approvals.

“The second phase of the project, scheduled to commence on Dec. 14, is expected to eliminate the multiple bottlenecks, delays and revenue leakages that have long frustrated exporters,” he said.

He said the first batch of the phase would cover the issuance of export permit issuance by agencies, including the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), NAFDAC and Federal Produce Inspection Service.

According to him, the second batch, involving processes handled by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), would commence in the first quarter of 2027.

Fakolade explained that the first phase had streamlined the submission of licences and permits by integrating the digital systems of various regulatory agencies.

He said the platform had also strengthened compliance by ensuring that users met regulatory requirements before accessing relevant services.

“One of the testimonials we received from agencies during the first phase was that enforced compliance on the platform helped users comply with regulations.

“When there is compliance, there is also a reduction in revenue leakages,” he said.

The NSW project director said the project team was engaging exporters and other stakeholders nationwide to ensure adequate awareness ahead of the second phase.

He listed Enugu, Akure, Jos, Lagos and Port Harcourt among the cities already visited, adding that sensitisation would continue in Kano and Abuja.

He said the NSW team was collaborating with the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), which maintains the database of registered exporters.

“The partnership would provide access to relevant information and insights required for effective implementation of the export phase,” he said.

Fakolade said the project had completed its User Acceptance Testing and would commence end-user training on Monday.

He urged exporters and other stakeholders to register for the training to familiarise themselves with the platform ahead of its implementation.

Meanwhile,Mrs Nonye Ayeni, the Executive Director of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), said Nigeria’s non-oil export earnings rose by 11.5 per cent to 6.1 billion dollars (N875.4 billion) in 2025.

Ayeni, who was represented by Mr Ndubueze Okeke, the Director of Trade Information at NEPC, said the figure rose from 5.46 billion dollars (N783.5 billion) in 2024.

She said export volumes also increased by 10 per cent to 8.02 million metric tonnes, while the country exported 281 non-oil products to 120 countries during the period.

“This reflects the country’s growing export potential,” she said.

The NEPC chief executive, however, said sustained growth required efficient systems to move products from local markets to international destinations with minimal delays and reduced costs.

She expressed confidence that the NSW would improve inter-agency coordination, eliminate duplication, enhance transparency and reduce administrative burdens on businesses.

Ayeni said the council had commenced engagement and onboarding processes to integrate relevant export services into the platform.

She said it was important for exporters to understand the relationship between the NSW, Trade Monitoring System (TRMS), Forms NXP and NCX, as well as applicable registration, permit and certification requirements.

“Our objective is to ensure a seamless transition that simplifies processes rather than creates additional burdens for businesses,” she said.

Mr Aondona Fanyam, the Controller in charge of Modernisation, Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), said the service was working with relevant government agencies to digitise and integrate export documentation into the NSW platform.

Fanyam said the project, which had been tested through import processes, was now being extended to exports through a phased implementation approach.

“The agencies are ready, but the stakeholders need to be aware of what is happening. That is why we are here to sensitise them and provide avenues for training,” he said.

World.title: Stop weaponising public for political relevance – Obi’s media office to Wike, Keyamo
World.content:
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo and NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA- THE Media Office of the Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC ahead of January 16 2027 election, Peter Obi has taken a swipe at the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory Administration, FCTA, Nyesom Wike and the Minister Nigeria’s Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, over attacks on the Presidential candidate over National anthem.

In a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Reach, POMR, Idris Zekeri, he described them as rabble rousers, warning them to stop weaponising public for political relevance.

According to Zekeri, a government minister is not a political warlord and public office is neither a private arsenal nor are Nigeria’s state institutions extensions of any politician’s personal political organisation, urging Wike and Keyamo to recognise that they hold their offices in trust for Nigerians, not to serve political egos or protect partisan interests, adding that even more concerning is the attempt to portray partisan conduct as patriotism.

The statement read, ” the Peter Obi Media Office strongly condemns the disturbing conduct of Ministers Nyesom Wike and Festus Keyamo, who appear to be exploiting their official positions for partisan political confrontation, treating the authority entrusted to them by Nigerians as though it were personal property to be deployed against political opponents. Their conduct raises a fundamental question: when did public service become an instrument for political intimidation, personal vendettas and the pursuit of narrow partisan interests?

” A government minister is not a political warlord. Public office is neither a private arsenal nor are Nigeria’s state institutions extensions of any politician’s personal political organisation. Wike and Keyamo must recognise that they hold their offices in trust for Nigerians, not to serve political egos or protect partisan interests. Even more concerning is the attempt to portray partisan conduct as patriotism.

“Patriotism is not measured by the forcefulness of political rhetoric, the harshness of attacks on opponents or the unconditional defence of a government. It is demonstrated by service, integrity, respect for the rule of law and an unwavering commitment to the welfare of citizens. Claims of patriotism should be subjected to careful scrutiny rather than accepted without question. Nigerians must differentiate political antagonism from genuine patriotism and understand that loyalty to a political establishment is not equivalent to commitment to the nation.

“No individual or political organisation has an exclusive monopoly on patriotism. At a time when Nigerians are contending with poverty, insecurity, unemployment and a deepening cost-of-living crisis, senior public officials must not appear more concerned with political disputes than with the urgent responsibilities of governance.

“The Nigerian people did not entrust public institutions to these officials for use as instruments of political conflict. Those institutions were placed in their care to serve the nation. Wike and Keyamo must understand that public office is temporary, whereas the effects of its abuse can endure for years. They owe Nigerians accountability, restraint and respect for democratic institutions. Nigeria needs public servants, not political combatants; nation-builders, not political enforcers. Patriotism must be demonstrated through service to the people, not manufactured through partisan propaganda.”

World.title: ICPC Pledges Transparency, Periodic Publication of Recovered Assets
World.content:
* As 52 African countries storm Abuja for Asset Recovery Assembly

* Says recovery now integral part of fight against corruption across Africa

Alex Enumah and Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has assured Nigerians that all recovered assets will be periodically published, with their status and owners made public.

The assurance was given during a media briefing Saturday in Abuja ahead of the General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners Forum (AARPF), holding under the auspices of the African Union (AU).

Responding to questions from journalists on whether the commission is committed to periodically publishing recovered assets, the Director, Special Services, ICPC, Mohammed Hassan, disclosed that the commission will definitely do that, stressing that nothing is hidden.

Mohammed, who doubled as the Chairman, Local Organising Committee of the forthcoming programme, stated: “Anything recovered is for the public and so ICPC will definitely declare anything and whatever has been recovered. It’s a public document.”

He dismissed suggestions that practitioners are scared of developments in the sector, explaining that asset recovery has become an integral part in the fight against corruption all over the world.

According to him, it is not just about recovering assets, but ensuring that what was recovered is put to use for the benefit of the generality of the masses.

“It is an aspect of the fight against corruption which the African Union is advancing,” he said.

On whether any other African country is leading Nigeria in asset recovery, he said some countries recover their assets without public knowledge, making comparison difficult.

“Some of these countries recover their assets and you don’t know what they have recovered. We don’t know whether they are doing their recoveries or not. But however, when we meet like this we have the opportunity to discuss in forums like this what has been recovered,” he explained.

He added that delegates will be taken to some places to see what Nigeria is doing with some recovered assets in the country.

On measures to ensure proper implementation of recoveries, especially where foreign countries may be reluctant, he said such questions would be better addressed when the programme starts properly by officials of the AU and the Local Organising Committee.

He however stressed that the purpose of the programme is to harmonize the fight against corruption, especially now that asset recovery has become an integral part of what anti-corruption agencies do all over the world.

“The purpose of the programme, like I said, is to harmonize, synergise, emphasise, come up with strategies, common ways to deal with this menace. Essentially, that’s what we are doing,” he said.

He disclosed that literally all African countries, about 52 to 54 – will be attending the assembly.

World.title: Lagos Denies N700m Billboard Permit Fee
World.content:
* Says most expensive outdoor advert costs N10m monthly

Ayodeji Ake

The Lagos State Government has dismissed reports that it has increased billboard permit fees to N700 million, describing the claim as false and misleading.

The government, in a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Gbenga Omotoso, said the allegation circulating on social media was intended to misrepresent the state’s outdoor advertising regulations.

The controversy followed a social media post suggesting that the alleged high billboard fees were responsible for the absence of the New Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign materials on Lagos roads.

However, the government maintained that billboard structures were owned and operated by private advertising companies, adding that the most expensive billboard placement in the state costs about N10 million monthly.

It explained that the Lagos State Signage and  Agency (LASAA) was a regulatory body and did not own or operate billboards.

“Billboards are owned by private operators. The most expensive billboard is about N10 million monthly. The government does not run billboards,” the statement said.

Clarifying the regulatory requirements, the government said individuals and companies seeking to operate as outdoor advertising practitioners in Lagos must obtain a non-refundable, one-off registration form costing N7 million, register with the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) and meet other statutory requirements.

It stressed that the N7 million registration requirement was distinct from the statutory permit fees payable for individual advertising structures and the commercial costs of media placement, production and other advertising services.

According to the government, LASAA does not determine the commercial rates charged by billboard owners, as such charges are determined by private operators.

It added that regulatory fees applicable to billboard structures vary according to factors such as size, format and location, with different rates applying across designated zones.

The government also clarified that political campaign s must be displayed on approved advertising structures operated by registered outdoor advertising practitioners with valid LASAA permits.

It said the structures must also satisfy established requirements relating to their locations, structural safety and environmental standards.

As political activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather momentum, the government said LASAA had recently embarked on public sensitisation on election campaign advertising guidelines to educate political parties, candidates, advertising practitioners and members of the public on the applicable regulations.

It reiterated that the agency’s responsibility was to regulate outdoor advertising, administer permits and ensure compliance with relevant laws.

The government further disclosed that LASAA would remove campaign communication materials after election activities to restore the city’s visual appeal, at no cost to the public.

Reaffirming its position on political participation, the state government said Lagos remained open to all political parties and candidates, insisting that its advertising regulations applied to everyone.

“Lagos will continue to be the bastion of democracy and equal opportunities for all politicians and their parties,” the statement added.

World.title: Sundiata Post Launches Founding 100 Club for New Intellectual Platform
World.content:
Sundiata Post has unveiled the Founding 100 Club, an exclusive pre-subscription initiative for its forthcoming flagship intellectual publication, Sovereignty Call, with membership limited to 100 subscribers.

The five-week pre-subscription campaign will open on Monday, November 16, and close on Friday, December 18, 2026, ahead of the platform’s maiden edition scheduled for January 25, 2027.

The initiative offers founding members discounted annual subscription rates of ₦40,000 for Nigerians and Nigerian residents, and $50 for international subscribers.

According to a statement released on Friday by Vivian Daniel, Manager of the Sundiata Post Knowledge Lab (SPKL), the initiative provides the first 100 subscribers an opportunity to become part of the platform’s inaugural subscriber community.

Operating under the tagline, Ideas That Govern, Sovereignty Call is a premium, subscription-based intellectual publication dedicated to examining sovereignty, statehood, institutional capacity and political order in Nigeria, Africa and the Global South.

The publication will feature 12 original, fully researched contributions annually, released monthly, focusing on ideas, research and perspectives beyond the immediacy of conventional news.

Founding members will enjoy seven principal privileges, including permanent founding subscriber status, preferential subscription rates, personalised digital membership certificates, public recognition on the platform’s official webpage and access to exclusive publications and subscriber archives.

They will also enjoy priority access to special editions, research publications and selected intellectual engagements organised or offered through the platform.

The preferential subscription rate will remain available to founding members for renewals through the third year, irrespective of prevailing subscription rates.

The initiative, according to the statement, represents more than a discounted subscription arrangement, describing it as a founding membership distinction within a new intellectual publishing institution.

Commenting on the initiative, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Sundiata Post, Dr Max Nwabueze Amuchie, described Sovereignty Call as a deliberate investment in the production and distribution of enduring knowledge.

He said: “Sovereignty Call reflects our conviction that societies need more than a continuous supply of news. They need ideas, research and intellectual contributions that help explain the forces shaping their political and institutional realities.

“We are building a platform where serious ideas can find a permanent audience and where knowledge is treated not merely as commentary but as an instrument for understanding and improving the conditions of statehood and sovereignty.

“The Founding 100 Club gives our earliest subscribers an opportunity to participate in this institutional undertaking from the beginning. We want them to be recognised not simply as our first customers, but as the inaugural community of a platform committed to ideas that matter and knowledge that endures.”

The launch marks a significant milestone in Sundiata Post’s evolution from a conventional digital news platform into what it describes as a media, intelligence and knowledge institution.

The organisation said the new publication would form part of its evolving dual-engine architecture, combining research, knowledge production and intellectual infrastructure with premium knowledge products and sustainable commercial publishing.

Unlike conventional news platforms driven largely by immediacy, Sovereignty Call is designed to create enduring intellectual value through original analysis, research-informed arguments and contributions from individuals with relevant expertise and experience.

The publication will also pursue institutional subscription and media syndication arrangements, providing opportunities for organisations, research institutions, professional bodies and media outlets to access and republish selected contributions under agreed commercial and licensing terms.

Details of institutional subscription and syndication rates will be communicated separately.

Thw statment said interested individuals and institutions can obtain further information about the Founding 100 Club through Sundiata Post’s official communication channels, https://sundiatapost.com/sovereignty-call

or by calling +234(0)8053069436.

World.title: Tinubu Seeks Forgiveness from Plateau, Promises Decisive Action Against Insecurity
World.content:
•Vows to return IDPs to their ancestral homes

• Gov Mutfwang: Tinubu met Nigeria in intensive care unit

• Massive turnout reflects North-Central’s confidence in Tinubu’s leadership, says information minister

Deji Elumoye, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Yemi Kosoko in Jos



President Bola Tinubu yesterday asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba in Jos North Local Government Area (LGA) of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities.

He stated that his administration was taking stern security measures against those carrying out the dastardly acts in the state.

This is just as Governor Caleb Mutfwang of Plateau State said President Tinubu met Nigeria in an intensive care unit when he assumed office but has gradually moved the country into recovery through his administration’s policies.

Meanwhile, the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has attributed the large turnout of party faithful and supporters at yesterday’s rally of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jos to what he described as growing public appreciation of the achievements of President Tinubu’s administration by the North-Central over the past three years.

Speaking at the ruling APC presidential campaign rally in Jos, Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001.

“When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.

“But since then, that has changed; we are forging together,” he explained.

He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home.

Tinubu pledged the reconstruction of conflict-ravaged communities, the return of internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes and accelerated economic development across the region.

Recalling his previous visits to the state, the president said the state had suffered years of violent attacks that resulted in loss of lives, destruction of homes and displacement of thousands of residents.

He expressed sympathy to victims of violence and IDPs, pledging that the federal government would rebuild affected communities and support their safe return to their ancestral homes.

He said the government had intensified security measures to tackle insecurity, including training 1,000 forest guards and deploying surveillance technology to strengthen intelligence gathering and rapid response capabilities.

“Crises and attacks have inflicted deep wounds on Plateau. Too many lives have been lost, homes destroyed, communities displaced.

“To every bereaved family, every survivor and everyone unable to return home, I offer my heartfelt condolences for your loss and pray that only God will console you.

“We are one single family created by the same God Almighty. We are just living in different rooms, speaking different languages and behaving in different ways, but living in different rooms and speaking different languages does not make us enemies of one another.

“We have to live together. We have to farm together. We have to build this Plateau and this country together. It is our responsibility to behave as brothers and sisters”, he further said.

The president promised that the 2027 general election would be peaceful, warning individuals and groups plotting to unleash violence or intimidate voters that his administration would not tolerate any attempt to undermine the democratic process.

He also appealed for electoral support for APC candidates at all levels, encouraging voters to support the party in the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and state House of Assembly elections.

Tinubu said he had directed security agencies to intensify operations against those responsible for violent attacks and ensure lasting peace across Plateau State.

“What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people from adversity to prosperity”, he added.

The president said the security arrangements would target threats facing rural communities, where farmers and other residents had been forced to abandon their homes and livelihoods.

“Crises and attacks have inflicted deep wounds on the state. Too many lives have been lost, homes destroyed, communities displaced.

“To every bereaved family, every survivor and everyone unable to return home, I offer my heartfelt condolences for your loss and pray that only God will console you”, he said.

He urged Plateau residents to embrace peaceful coexistence and resist attempts to exploit their ethnic, religious or political differences.

“We are one single family created by the same God Almighty. We are just living in different rooms, speaking different languages and behaving in different ways, but living in different rooms and speaking different languages do not make us enemies of one another.

“We have to live together. We have to farm together. We have to build this Plateau and this country together. It is our responsibility to behave as brothers and sisters”, he declared.

On economic development, Tinubu announced plans to collaborate with the Plateau State Government to transform the Jos airport into an agro-cargo hub that can facilitate the direct export of agricultural produce to international markets.

He said the proposed project would enable farmers in Plateau and surrounding states to export vegetables, potatoes, and other agricultural commodities, expanding market access, creating economic opportunities, and improving farmers’ incomes.

“From that, you will be able to export vegetables and potatoes abroad directly. The economy will improve. Development and prosperity will grow this economy”, he said.

He urged Nigerians to obtain and safeguard their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 elections, describing the PVC as a vital instrument for democratic participation and prosperity.

Gov Mutfwang: Tinubu Met Nigeria in Intensive Care Unit

In his welcome address, Governor Mutfwang said President Tinubu met Nigeria in an intensive care unit when he assumed office but had moved the country into recovery through his administration’s policies.

The governor pledged Plateau State’s support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The governor said, “You met Nigeria in the intensive care unit, and through the policies you have administered, like a drug, you have been able to bring Nigeria out of the intensive care unit. We are now in recovery.”

“We are confident that if you continue, we will not only recover but prosper as well. That is why we are determined that in the 2027 election, there is no alternative for us. We will stick with you and go with you.”

He described Tinubu as a friend of Plateau State and the North-Central region, citing the federal government’s interventions in road infrastructure, education and healthcare.

According to him, students in tertiary institutions across the state had benefited from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund scheme, while strategic federal road projects had improved connectivity and economic prospects.

The governor pledged overwhelming support for Tinubu in the 2027 election, insisting that the people of Plateau had resolved to reciprocate what he described as the President’s goodwill towards the state.

Earlier, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari Abubakar, declared that Plateau and the North-central zone remained firmly behind Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Yari said the administration’s achievements in security, infrastructure and economic management had strengthened public confidence in the APC government, adding that the President had demonstrated commitment to fulfilling the party’s manifesto.

Yilwatda Charges North-central Governors, Candidates to Unite for Tinubu’s Victory

Speaking at the event, the National Chairman of APC, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, urged the party’s governors and governorship candidates in the North-central to unite all stakeholders in their states and mobilise massive support for President Tinubu.

He also urged Plateau people to translate the rally’s enthusiasm into votes, insisting the state must deliver a record-breaking victory for Tinubu.

The chairman described Tinubu as a promise-keeper who has fulfilled his commitments to Plateau State, saying the administration’s record of delivery provides a strong basis for renewed public confidence.

“All political leaders in Plateau State are now united, 100 per cent, behind the President,” Yilwatda said, assuring Tinubu that the ballot box would reflect the people’s overwhelming support.

Yilwatda specifically charged governors, candidates and leaders across the region to close ranks, bring every stakeholder on board and establish a united front behind Tinubu.

The chairman emphasised that the North-Central must approach the elections with a common purpose, stressing that personal interests and political differences must give way to the collective objective of securing victory for the APC.

Massive Turnout Reflects North-Central’s Confidence in Tinubu’s Leadership, Says Information Minister

Meanwhile, the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Idris, has attributed the large turnout of party faithful to what he described as growing public appreciation of the achievements of President Tinubu’s administration by the North-Central over the past three years.

Speaking at the rally, the minister said the enthusiastic participation of party faithful and supporters reflected, in his assessment, confidence in the administration’s reform agenda and its efforts to reposition the country for sustainable economic growth and development.

“The turnout we are witnessing here today is a clear demonstration of the confidence Nigerians have in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the direction his administration is taking the country. The people can see the efforts being made to address longstanding challenges, strengthen the economy and create a better future for our country,” Idris said.

Idris said the administration remained focused on consolidating the gains of its reforms and ensuring that their benefits translated into tangible improvements in the lives of citizens across the country.

“President Tinubu remains committed to staying the course and ensuring that the decisions being taken today deliver lasting benefits for Nigerians. What is important is that we continue to build on the progress made and work towards a stronger, more prosperous nation,” he said.

The minister also urged opposition political parties to embrace issue-based campaigns and demonstrate greater organisational preparedness rather than relying on political rhetoric and criticism of the government.

He maintained that Nigeria’s democratic process would be better served by constructive political engagement, credible alternatives and robust debates on policies and programmes that directly affect the welfare of Nigerians.

Idris further emphasised the importance of responsible political conduct as the country approaches the 2027 general elections, noting that political parties have a collective responsibility to promote peaceful participation and strengthen public confidence in the democratic process.

Also speaking at the rally, the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, underscored the strategic importance of the North-Central geopolitical zone to Nigeria’s political stability, economic growth and national development.

He highlighted the region’s enormous potential, particularly in solid minerals and other productive sectors, and stressed its significance to the country’s broader economic transformation.

World.title: Amaechi: 13 North-east, North-west States Backing ADC in 2027 Elections
World.content:
• I’ll restore fuel subsidy, tackle insecurity if elected, Atiku vows

•Promises to continue Kolmani oil exploration in Bauchi

Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Mr. Rotimi Amaechi, has claimed that 13 states in the North-east and North-west backed the opposition party in the forthcoming 2027 elections, and expressed confidence that the party would defeat President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC).

This comes as the ADC presidential candidate and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has reiterated his determination to restore fuel subsidy and tackle insecurity if elected president.

Atiku also promised to continue oil exploration activities at the Kolmani Oil Field in Bauchi State

Speaking yesterday during the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State, Amaechi said the ADC would also challenge the APC in the South-south and North-central regions, predicting victories for the opposition party in Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states.

The former Rivers State governor vowed that the party would not accept a repeat of what he alleged happened during the 2023 general election.

“Because these people will do what they did in 2023. This time, we shall not agree. Do you understand? We will not do what?” he said.

Amaechi argued that the ADC had a stronger regional presence, citing the 13 states in the North-east and North-west.

“We are the only party that comes with 13 states. The whole of North-east, the whole of North-west, that is 13, right? Let the president tell us how many states he comes with. He comes with only five in the South-West,” he added.

He further claimed that the APC would lose a sixth state in the South-west to the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

“And the sixth state in the South-west will vote APM, whether he likes it or not,” he added.

Amaechi said the ADC would also compete strongly against the ruling party in the South-South and North-Central, expressing confidence that Atiku would secure Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states.

“We will fight with him in South-South. We will fight with him in North-Central. And be sure, be rest assured, Niger, Kogi, Nasarawa will be in ours easily,” he said.

Amaechi also predicted that Tinubu would not make significant electoral gains in the South-east, insisting that the ADC would win the presidential election.

“He will not go to South-east at all. Be assured, we will win. We will win. Things will get better,” he said.

I’ll Restore Fuel Subsidy, Tackle Insecurity If Elected, Atiku Vows

Speaking at the rally, Atiku reiterated his determination to restore the fuel subsidy and tackle insecurity and urged voters to vote for the party’s candidates in all elective positions.

“I have already promised all Nigerians that I will restore petroleum subsidy. Not only that, but I will also restore subsidy in electricity,” he said.

Atiku also pledged to address insecurity in the North-east and other parts of the country, while promising to expand petroleum exploration in the Kolmani area to generate additional revenue.

He called on Nigerians to support the ADC, urging voters in Bauchi to elect the party’s candidates from the presidency to the councillorship positions.

The former vice-president thanked the people of the state for their previous support, saying Bauchi had consistently given him substantial votes in past elections.

He urged residents to turn out in large numbers during the 2027 polls and ensure their votes were protected and counted.

“I want you to make sure you come out in your thousands. You vote for ADC. You defend the vote. You ensure that the votes are counted, and results are transmitted before you leave the polling booth,” Atiku said.

President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023.

Tinubu said the funds would instead be redirected to infrastructure, education, healthcare and job creation.

The subsidy removal has inflicted hardship on Nigerians, and Atiku repeatedly promised to restore it if elected in 2027.

The former vice president had questioned how the savings from its removal had been spent.

Uncertainty has surrounded the ADC’s leadership following a November 5 judgment by the Federal High Court in Abuja, which sacked the Senator Mark-led National Working Committee (NWC) and invalidated decisions taken under it, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate.

Justice Peter Lifu also ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) not to recognise decisions taken at the party’s 99th National Executive Committee meeting held on July 27, 2025.

But the ADC rejected the judgment and said it would challenge the decision in court.

The party also continued its activities and preparations for the 2027 elections.

World.title: Tegbe: Over 15,000 MVA Capacity Added to Grid in Three Years, Eyes N19bn Private Investments
World.content:
•FG spends over N10tn on power supply in 13 years, says Anuwe

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Tegbe, has disclosed that more than 15,000 megavolt-amperes (MVA) of additional transmission capacity was added to the national electricity grid between 2023 and 2026.

This is just as the Managing Director of FGN Power Company Limited, Mr. Kenny Anuwe, revealed that the federal government invested more than N10trillion in Nigeria’s Electricity Supply Industry (NESI) since the privatisation of the sector in 2013.

FGN Power is the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) set up by the Nigerian government to implement the Presidential Power Initiative (PPI), the flagship programme conceived in 2018 to tackle Nigeria’s long-standing electricity challenges.

Speaking at the Sixth Edition of the Power Correspondents Association of Nigeria (PCAN) Conference in Abuja, Tegbe added that the federal government had taken steps to address longstanding financial and infrastructure challenges in the electricity sector as part of efforts to support President Bola Tinubu’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy.

The minister said the president had approved a plan to settle verified legacy debts owed to generating companies, reiterating that the initiative had raised N1.2 trillion to ease financial pressure on the companies and improve their capacity to pay for gas and maintain their plants.

He disclosed that more than 2.8 million customers had been metered under the Presidential Metering Initiative (PMI).

At the same time, the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) had continued to connect universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power.

Tegbe also said construction had commenced on a new National Grid Control Centre in Osogbo to replace the existing facility built more than 60 years ago.

He added that more than 15,000MVA of additional transmission capacity had been added to the national grid between 2023 and 2026.

According to him, newly installed substation equipment commissioned across several locations in the country had added more than 1,300 MVA to Nigeria’s transmission capacity, making additional electricity available to distribution companies.

The minister, represented by his Special Adviser on Administration and Projects, Martins Olajide, identified grid stabilisation, sector liquidity and sustainability, asset optimisation, and grid expansion and enhancement as the four priorities of the government’s roadmap for addressing the sector’s challenges.

He said the plan would adopt a corridor-based approach to prioritise major economic centres for reliable, round-the-clock electricity supply.

FG Spends over N10tn on Power Supply in 13 years

Meanwhile, delivering a keynote address at the PCAN conference, themed: “$1tn Economy: Nigeria’s Roadmap to Reliable and Affordable Power Supply,” the Managing Director of FGN Power Company Limited, Mr. Anuwe, revealed that the federal government invested more than N10 trillion on power supply since 2013.

Anuwe said that government funding had helped sustain the electricity industry despite its challenges.

He pointed out that public funding has remained insufficient to meet the country’s power needs, stressing that the company had secured a $1 billion commitment from the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC). In comparison, other financiers were expected to commit $18 billion to the sector.

Anuwe, however, argued that the scale of investment required to support Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy could not be achieved through public funding alone.

“The government has invested over N10 trillion in the electricity sector since the advent of privatisation. But is it enough? How much money is enough?” he asked.

According to him, the industry would not have remained operational without the government’s financial interventions.

He stated the country must adopt new investment models capable of attracting substantial private capital.

Anuwe said the federal government accounted for more than 95 per cent of new infrastructure investment in the sector, a development he described as inconsistent with the objectives of privatisation.

“That’s not why we privatised,” he said, urging stakeholders to move beyond excuses and develop practical solutions to the sector’s financing and infrastructure challenges.

He maintained that the government should focus on providing the policy, regulatory and infrastructure conditions that would enable public and private capital to operate effectively.

“The government can provide the enablers, provide infrastructure, delivery, and market conditions under which public and private capital can perform effectively,” he argued.

The FGN Power chief said Nigeria needed between 10,000 megawatts and 30,000 megawatts of electricity to support the growth of a $1trillion economy, stressing that achieving the target would require a different approach to power sector planning and implementation.

He identified integrated resource planning, coordinated policy interventions, reliable technology, financial discipline and stronger private sector participation as essential to expanding electricity supply.

Anuwe also called for simpler institutional and regulatory arrangements, noting that the complexity of the electricity market, involving generation and distribution companies, transmission operators, regulators, government agencies, financiers and gas suppliers, could discourage potential investors.

He said clearer responsibilities, predictable regulation, bankable projects, faster decisions and measurable delivery would improve investor confidence and accelerate infrastructure development.

Anuwe disclosed that the company had structured commercial arrangements with original equipment manufacturers and engineering, procurement and construction firms, with the federal government providing 15 per cent equity in the financing arrangements.

According to him, the company’s transmission substation and line projects were progressing, with most of the ongoing Phase One projects expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

He added that the second batch of Siemens substations, comprising 12 facilities, was being prepared for implementation, subject to the necessary financing approvals, with commencement targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Anuwe said the projects, alongside the Omotosho substation project, were expected to deliver a combined capacity of just under 3,400 megawatts.

The company, he said, was targeting an additional 5,540 megawatts by 2029, alongside an improvement of at least 60 per cent in grid reliability.

Anuwe said the planned improvements could also enable at least 2,000 industries to return to the national grid, with households and businesses expected to benefit from more reliable electricity supply.

He said FGN Power Company was working toward a $2.3 billion project financing package, comprising $1.3 billion from Europe and $1 billion from China.

On his part, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Electricity Management Services Agency (NEMSA), Olusegun Adesayo, restated the organisation’s commitment to ensuring that electrical installations, equipment and networks across the country comply with prescribed technical standards and regulations.

Adesayo explained that beyond infrastructure, safety remains critical, since unsafe installations that do not comply with regulations cannot serve the people effectively.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Chairman of PCAN, Obas Esiedesa, said the association’s annual conference had evolved into an important platform for engagement among policymakers, regulators, operators, investors, industry experts and journalists since its inaugural edition in November 2021.

Esiedesa called for urgent attention to the recurring seasonal decline in electricity generation, particularly between November and March, when reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations and gas supply constraints to thermal plants often affected electricity output.

World.title: Decline in Loan Impairment Charges of Eight Banks By  46.9% Lifts Profit Before Tax to N4.8tn
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Eight Nigerian banks reported a 46.9 per cent decline in loan impairment charges to N1.01 trillion in the nine months ended September 2026, compared with N1.91 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025.

Loan impairment charges, often referred to as credit losses, are provisions banks make to cover potential defaults and deterioration in the value of their financial assets.

The substantial decline in impairment charges helped lift the eight banks’ combined profit before tax (PBT) by 12.2 per cent to N4.8 trillion, from N4.3 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025.

The eight banks are Jaiz Bank Plc, Zenith Bank Plc, Ecobank Transnational Incorporated, First HoldCo Plc, Guaranty Trust Holding Company (GTCO) Plc, Access Holdings Plc, Wema Bank Plc and Sterling Financial Holdings Plc.

THISDAY gathered that lower impairment charges at GTCO, Access Holdings, Zenith Bank and First HoldCo supported their combined profitability, although earnings growth sources varied across the groups.

Access Holdings recorded the largest percentage reduction in impairment charges, which fell by 73.5 per cent to N92.91 billion in the nine months ended September 2026, from N349.99 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Its PBT rose by 8.3 per cent to N667.36 billion.

Zenith Bank recorded the second-largest percentage reduction, with impairment charges declining by 70.5 per cent to N230.77 billion, from N782.76 billion.

Its PBT rose 1.2 per cent to N928.80 billion, from N917.41 billion, suggesting lower credit-loss provisions helped offset weaker income from other activities.

Together, Zenith Bank and Access Holdings accounted for approximately N809 billion of the reported N906 billion reductions in impairment charges across the eight groups.

GTCO also benefited from approximately N39.6 billion in lower impairment charges, although its PBT declined by 2.3 per cent to N879.90 billion.

The results show that lower impairment charges can materially support earnings but do not automatically translate into higher profits when other income sources weaken or expenses rise.

While Zenith Bank and Access Holdings benefited significantly from lower credit losses, First HoldCo’s performance was substantially supported by trading and other non-interest income.

The banks’ statements on the nine-month results also highlighted different sources of earnings growth, with executives emphasising lower credit costs, diversified income and operating efficiency.

The Group Managing Director of Zenith Bank, Adaora Umeoji, said growth in lending, transaction volumes and deposits supported the bank’s performance, while “lower funding and credit costs contributed to profitability and improved earnings quality.”

Similarly, Access Holdings Group Chief Executive Officer Innocent Ike described the reduction in impairment charges and growth in income after impairment as evidence of the group’s stronger earnings base. He said the improvement “demonstrates the resilience of our core earnings base.”

First HoldCo recorded PBT of N911.24 billion, up 60.8 per cent, despite a 16 per cent decline in net interest income. Trading and fair-value income increased by about N190 billion, while higher fees and other operating income also supported profitability.

First HoldCo’s management highlighted the contribution of transaction-led revenues, with non-interest income growing by more than 143 per cent, helping to offset weaker net interest income.

Wema Bank’s net interest income increased by 38.3 per cent to N325.88 billion, supporting a 76.6 per cent rise in PBT to N258.64 billion.

Sterling Financial Holdings recorded a 43.9 per cent increase in net interest income to N205.90 billion, while PBT rose by 37.1 per cent to N97.28 billion. However, higher impairment charges and operating expenses absorbed part of the improvement.

Ecobank’s naira-denominated PBT declined marginally to N1.01 trillion as operating income weakened. GTCO’s PBT fell by 2.3 per cent as higher funding costs and operating expenses weighed on earnings.

Ecobank Group Chief Executive Officer Jeremy Awori identified deposit growth and operating efficiency as sources of resilience, while acknowledging risks from inflation, energy prices and foreign exchange volatility.

Jaiz Bank reported a 21.07 per cent increase in impairment charges to N1.28 billion, from N1.05 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Its PBT rose by 1.7 per cent to N23.69 billion, from N23.29 billion.

World.title: NDC, Keyamo in War of Words over Singing of Old National Anthem at Lagos Meeting
World.content:
•Minister accuses Obi of planning secession

• Ex-Anambra gov didn’t stop new National Anthem, NDC fights back

. Accuses APC of sponsoring political attacks

Chinedu Eze in Lagos and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, yesterday engaged in war of words over the minister’s allegation that the presidential candidate of the opposition party, Mr. Peter Obi and the members of the party, sang the old National Anthem at the recent town hall meeting held by the party in Lagos.

Keyamo had in his verified Twitter (X) account said that by defying to sing the new national anthem, Obi and his group might be planning to break away from Nigeria.

But in a swift response, the NDC dismissed allegations against its presidential candidate, describing them as unfounded, baseless and politically-motivated.

The party accused Keyamo of exhibiting selective amnesia in his assessment of the Lagos incident, insisting that Obi neither instructed supporters not to sing the national anthem nor attempted to undermine the country’s national symbols.

In a response to the minister’s allegations, through its National Publicity Secretary Osa Director, the NDC maintained that the incident was a spontaneous expression of defiance by some supporters against what it described as the poor governance of the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration and the alleged deployment of political thugs to attack its members during the gathering.

The party argued that Keyamo deliberately ignored the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the reported attack on the NDC supporters, while attempting to portray Obi in a negative light.

It stated, “Keyamo’s allegations are hair-splitting, unfounded and baseless. As characteristic of the APC, he exhibited selective amnesia in his assessment.

“He forgot to state that Obi did not ask the crowd not to sing the national anthem. What happened was a spontaneous act of defiance to the ruinous reign of the APC and the hired thugs they sent to attack the NDC members,” the party added.

The opposition party further disclosed that while some supporters expressed their displeasure through the rendition of the old national anthem, other participants at the same venue continued to recite the current national anthem.

According to the party, the development contradicted any suggestion that Obi or the NDC leadership deliberately organised an action to disrespect the country’s national anthem.

It said, “At another end of the same hall, people recited the national anthem.”

The NDC also questioned the significance of the controversy, arguing that the mere public rendition of the national anthem by members of the ruling party had not translated into improved governance or better living conditions for Nigerians.

Taking a swipe at Keyamo and the APC, the party declared that displaying outward loyalty to national symbols should not be confused with the capacity to provide effective leadership.

“In any case, he should realise that the hood does not make the monk. Since the APC has been reciting the national anthem, where has it led Nigeria?” the party queried.

The opposition party accused the minister and the ruling party of deliberately shifting public attention from the alleged attack on its supporters and the country’s worsening political and economic challenges to what it described as unnecessary personality attacks against Obi.

It argued that the controversy reflected the APC’s inability to engage the opposition candidate on substantive issues of governance, national development and the welfare of Nigerians.

The NDC maintained that its presidential candidate remained committed to national unity, democratic values and peaceful political engagement, while accusing the APC of using the controversy to distract Nigerians from pressing national concerns.

Keyamo had described the act of singing the old national anthem as one of the ingredients of secession.

He insisted that by approving the singing of a different national anthem, Obi was allegedly officially leading a secessionist group.

“National Anthem is one of a country’s national symbols. It represents a country’s history, values and sovereignty. It is meant to unite citizens.

“When a group of people decide to defy it and sing something different from what others are signing as prescribed by law, that group is preparing grounds to break away from the country. It is one of the ingredients of secession. And once the leader of such a group endorses the action, it means the group is then officially a secessionist movement.

“I am therefore, officially calling on the original ‘countryman’, my classmate, my friend and a man of considerable courage from our school days, Senator Seriake Dickson, the official leader of the NDC, to within 48 hours speak up as to whether the NDC officially endorses a proscribed anthem as its own national symbol. The world is waiting,” he said.

World.title: South Africa’s cheapest national parks for a summer getaway
World.content:
A summer getaway in South Africa doesn’t have to involve expensive accommodation or luxury safari lodges. The country’s national parks offer affordable opportunities to explore beautiful natural landscapes, spot wildlife and enjoy outdoor activities.

South African National Parks (SANParks) introduced its latest conservation fees on 1 November 2026, with the rates applying until 31 October 2027.

For South African citizens and residents, daily entrance fees start at just R54 per adult. Here are some of the cheapest national parks to visit this summer.



The cheapest national parks in South Africa

The following are daily conservation fees for South African citizens and residents with valid identification.

National park or section Adult Child Garden Route – Knysna R54 R27 Agulhas R63 R32 Bontebok R63 R32 Camdeboo R63 R32 Garden Route – Wilderness R63 R32 Tankwa-Karoo R63 R32 Namaqua R65 R33 Mokala R66 R33 Augrabies Falls R73 R37 Golden Gate Highlands R76 R38 Karoo R76 R38 Mapungubwe R76 R38 Marakele R76 R38 Mountain Zebra R76 R38

Children are aged between two and 11. Fees cover park entry only.

1. Garden Route National Park – Knysna

Entrance: R54 per adult



The Knysna section of Garden Route National Park is the cheapest option on this list. It’s known for its indigenous forests, estuaries and beautiful coastal scenery.

Visitors can enjoy nature walks, birdwatching and exploring the surrounding environment.

2. Bontebok National Park

Entrance: R63 per adult



Located near Swellendam in the Western Cape, Bontebok National Park was established to protect the endangered bontebok.

Visitors can spot these antelope alongside other wildlife while enjoying the park’s mountain scenery. Activities include hiking, birdwatching and picnicking.

3. Camdeboo National Park

Entrance: R63 per adult



Surrounding Graaff-Reinet in the Eastern Cape, Camdeboo National Park is best known for the spectacular Valley of Desolation.

Visitors can enjoy scenic drives, hiking, wildlife viewing and impressive viewpoints overlooking the Karoo landscape.

4. Tankwa-Karoo National Park

Entrance: R63 per adult



Tankwa-Karoo offers a very different experience, with vast open landscapes, rocky mountains and remarkable night skies.

It’s particularly popular with photographers and stargazers. Wildlife includes gemsbok, springbok and red hartebeest.

5. Mokala National Park

Entrance: R66 per adult



Situated south-west of Kimberley, Mokala is a great option for visitors interested in wildlife.

The park is home to black and white rhinos, buffalo, giraffes, roan antelope and sable antelope. Visitors can enjoy self-drive game viewing and guided activities.

6. Augrabies Falls National Park

Entrance: R73 per adult



Augrabies Falls National Park is home to one of South Africa’s most spectacular waterfalls.

The Orange River plunges approximately 56 metres into a rocky gorge, creating an impressive natural attraction. Visitors can explore viewpoints, hiking trails and the surrounding landscape.

7. Mountain Zebra National Park

Entrance: R76 per adult



Located near Cradock in the Eastern Cape, Mountain Zebra National Park was established to protect the endangered Cape mountain zebra.

Other wildlife includes cheetahs, black rhinos, buffalo and various antelope species. Visitors can enjoy self-drive game viewing, guided activities and hiking.

8. Golden Gate Highlands National Park

Entrance: R76 per adult



Golden Gate Highlands National Park is known for its dramatic sandstone formations, green grasslands and mountain scenery.

Situated near Clarens in the Free State, it is particularly popular with hikers, photographers and outdoor enthusiasts. Visitors can enjoy scenic drives, hiking trails and wildlife viewing.

How much does a family visit cost?

For a family of two adults and two children aged between two and 11, entrance fees at some of these parks remain relatively affordable.



National park Family entrance fee Garden Route – Knysna R162 Bontebok R190 Camdeboo R190 Tankwa-Karoo R190 Mokala R198 Augrabies Falls R220 Mountain Zebra R228 Golden Gate Highlands R228

These amounts cover daily conservation fees only, excluding accommodation and other activities.

What about Kruger National Park?

Kruger is more expensive than the parks listed above, but remains one of South Africa’s most popular safari destinations.

South African citizens and residents pay R140 per adult and R70 per child per day for the 2026/27 season. A family of two adults and two children would therefore pay R420 in daily conservation fees.



There are a few ways to keep the cost of a national park getaway down:

Choose camping: Campsites can be cheaper than chalets and bungalows.

Campsites can be cheaper than chalets and bungalows. Pack your own food: Self-catering helps reduce restaurant expenses.

Self-catering helps reduce restaurant expenses. Consider a day trip: Avoid accommodation costs if you live nearby.

Avoid accommodation costs if you live nearby. Look into a Wild Card: Frequent visitors may save through annual access to participating parks, depending on their membership category.

Visitors should check SANParks’ website for the latest entrance fees, accommodation availability and park-specific conditions before travelling.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs warned on new signing
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs recently confirmed Mokwana’s arrival. The KwaMhlanga-born star joined the Soweto giants are leaving Tunisian giants Esperance.

The Bafana Bafana international has had quite a journey since then, moving abroad to play for Esperance before also spending time in Saudi Arabia.

MNTAMBO EXPLAINS WHAT Kaizer CHIEFS ARE GETTING

Elias Mntambo knows the player from their days together at Sekhukhune, where he was captain and had the chance to watch Mokwana develop.



Speaking on The CARWASH Podcast, the former midfielder believes the winger has the right qualities to do well at Chiefs. However, he wants the club’s supporters to give him time instead of putting too much pressure on him from the beginning.

“No individual will solve the team’s problems. Let’s not put Elias Mokwana under immense pressure. Yes, football in itself is a pressure game. And pressure is a privilege. It means something is expected of you,” Mntambo said.

Mntambo recalled that Mokwana was not the finished product when he arrived at Sekhukhune. He already had pace and could take on defenders, but there were parts of his game that needed attention.

What impressed Mntambo most was the winger’s attitude towards learning.

“And I’ve seen him grow at Sekhukhune. You know, [he] came in rough, you know, that rough diamond, you know, speed, dribble, but he’d lose so many balls. But one thing about him is that he’s coachable. He’s a sponge. He can absorb, he can listen. And that’s what’s going to take him far.”

The former Sekhukhune captain also believes Mokwana must keep his feet on the ground at Naturena.



“I think one thing with Kaizer Chiefs, they found a player that is hardworking, a player that is humble. I think where he comes from, he comes from humble beginnings. He knows to be the lowest of the lowest of life. So I hope that he still has that within him.

ELIAS MOKWANA CAN ALSO CREATE FOR OTHERS

Mntambo also spoke about an aspect of Mokwana’s game that he believes Chiefs supporters should appreciate.

The winger is not only interested in scoring goals or taking the attention away from his teammates. He can also provide opportunities for other players.

“When I was at Sekhukhune, I would never make the box and not get a cutback from a Mokwana. So more than him getting the shine, he is a player that can also serve. And I think Kaizer Chiefs have found themselves a gem in that position.”

Mokwana will have competition for a place in the wide attacking positions, with Mduduzi Shabalala, Mfundo Vilakazi and Langelihle Phili also available.

World.title: ‘Blue dragons’ with painful, venomous sting continue to wash up on Cape beaches
World.content:
Blue dragons were recently photographed on a beach in the Overstrand area. Image: Supplied

Blue dragons (glaucus atlanticus) are still being spotted on Cape beaches, including recent sightings at Pringle Bay in the Overstrand.

The striking little creatures, also known as blue sea slugs, usually occur alongside washed-up bluebottles, and also pack a painful sting.

Beachgoers have been urged to keep their distance from the blue dragons, and not to handle or harm them.



A series of sightings

Several blue dragons were reported washed up on Muizenberg beach in January this year, prompting warnings from ocean scientists.

At the time, Heather Wares, communications manager at the Two Oceans Aquarium, described the sightings as rare, but not unprecedented.

“The blue dragon slugs seen washed up on Cape Town’s beaches are an unusual sight,” Wares said.

“This stranding event is an uncommon occurrence but is known to happen globally from time to time, often together with bluebottles.”

The striking blue dragon (glaucus atlanticus), also commonly known as a blue sea slug. Image: Supplied

After the Muizenberg sightings, Cape Town deputy mayor Eddie Andrews warned that shores to the east of Cape Town could experience similar strandings.

“Given the current oceanographic and climatic conditions, it’s highly likely,” Andrews noted.



Andrews confirmed that City teams had also identified several blue dragons and numerous bluebottles during an inspection at Muizenberg in late January.

He also explained that the occurrence of blue dragons can be driven by warmer summer water temperatures and prevailing south-easterly winds.

More recently (7 November 2026), the dazzling little creatures were photographed by a beachgoer in Pringle Bay, on a beach roughly 80kms east of Muizenberg.

This adds another location to a series of blue dragon sightings reported along the Western Cape coastline this year.

How venomous are blue dragons?

Despite rarely exceeding 3cm in length, glaucus atlanticus delivers a surprisingly powerful sting.

These colourful nudibranchs usually live in the pelagic zone (open ocean). They float upside down at the sea’s surface, drifting wherever winds and currents take them.

They feed on venomous creatures, including the Portuguese man-o’-war, known in South Africa as bluebottles.

Blue dragons then ‘steal’ and store the stinging cells of their prey in specialised structures on their bodies. This allows them to deliver a painful sting, even after they have died.

Because it concentrates these stinging cells, a sting from a blue sea slug can be more potent and painful than a sting from a bluebottle.

This remarkable adaptation makes blue dragons deceptively dangerous, despite their tiny size and stunning blue-and-white appearance.

“While beachgoers should be aware of the risks associated with being stung by one of these highly venomous nudibranchs, this is also an opportunity to learn about these extraordinary marine animals,” Wares added.

The underside of glaucus atlanticus. Image: Supplied

What should you do if you are stung by a blue dragon?

With the festive season approaching, thousands of visitors are expected to flock to Cape beaches. Blue dragons could easily attract the attention of curious holidaymakers, particularly children.

Beachgoers are advised not to touch blue dragons or bluebottles, even if they appear dead.

If stung, rinse the affected area with seawater to remove any remaining stinging cells. Do not use fresh water.

Apply heat by immersing the affected area in hot water – about 45°C, or as warm as tolerable – for 20 to 90 minutes to help reduce pain.

Seek medical help if symptoms worsen, become severe, or if there are signs of an allergic reaction.

World.title: The best South African national parks to visit this summer
World.content:
Winter is traditionally considered the best time for wildlife viewing in South Africa, but that doesn’t mean summer is a bad time to go on safari.

Between October and March, the country’s national parks transform with lush green landscapes, seasonal birdlife and opportunities to spot newborn animals.

Although thicker vegetation can make some wildlife harder to find, summer offers a different safari experience, particularly for birdwatchers and nature lovers.



Here are five South African national parks worth visiting this summer.

1. Kruger National Park

Kruger National Park remains one of South Africa’s best safari destinations throughout the year.

During summer, the park’s dry bushveld transforms into a lush green landscape as seasonal rains fill rivers and waterholes.

The warmer months are particularly good for birdwatching, with migratory species arriving from elsewhere in Africa and beyond.

Visitors may also spot newborn animals, while the park’s famous predators remain active throughout the year.

Best for: Birdwatching, young wildlife and self-drive safaris.



Keep in mind: Thick vegetation can make animals harder to spot, while summer temperatures and afternoon thunderstorms can affect game-viewing conditions.

2. Addo Elephant National Park

Located near Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape, Addo Elephant National Park is an excellent option for a summer wildlife getaway.

The park is particularly famous for its elephant population, but visitors can also encounter lions, buffalo, leopards and rhinos.

Its varied habitats support hundreds of bird species, making it an appealing destination for birdwatchers. Visitors can explore the park on self-drive routes or book guided game drives.

Best for: Elephant sightings, family safaris and self-drive game viewing.

Keep in mind: Summer can be hot, so plan wildlife-viewing activities for the cooler morning and late-afternoon hours.

3. Marakele National Park

Situated in Limpopo’s Waterberg region, Marakele National Park combines mountain scenery, grasslands and bushveld.

The park is home to elephants, rhinos, buffalo and several antelope species.

It is also a particularly interesting destination for birdwatchers, with more than 270 recorded bird species and an impressive Cape vulture colony.

Its varied landscape offers a different experience from the traditional Lowveld safari.

Best for: Birdwatching, mountain scenery and varied wildlife.

Keep in mind: Summer thunderstorms are possible, and temperatures can become particularly high in lower-lying areas.

4. Mapungubwe National Park

Mapungubwe National Park offers a combination of wildlife, natural scenery and fascinating history.

Situated near South Africa’s borders with Botswana and Zimbabwe, the park is known for its riverine forests, rocky landscapes and the meeting point of the Limpopo and Shashe rivers.

It’s home to elephants, leopards and a variety of other wildlife. Summer is also a rewarding time for birdwatching, with migratory species adding to the park’s impressive birdlife.

Visitors can enjoy guided game drives, walking activities and scenic viewpoints.

Best for: Birdwatching, history and unusual landscapes.

Keep in mind: Summer temperatures can exceed 40°C, so plan activities around the cooler parts of the day.

5. Mokala National Park

For a quieter safari experience, Mokala National Park in the Northern Cape is worth considering.

Situated south-west of Kimberley, the park is known for its camelthorn trees, open plains and rocky hills.

Wildlife includes black and white rhinos, buffalo, giraffes, roan antelope and sable antelope. Visitors can enjoy self-drive game viewing, guided activities and birdwatching.

Its smaller size also makes it an appealing option for travellers looking for a less conventional safari destination.

Best for: Antelope sightings, conservation and quieter game viewing.

Keep in mind: The Northern Cape can become extremely hot during summer, so visitors should carry plenty of water.

Is summer a good time for a safari THOUGH?

Summer offers a different experience from the traditional winter safari.

Although animals can be harder to spot in thicker vegetation, visitors benefit from greener landscapes, increased birdlife and the possibility of seeing newborn animals.

For the best experience, plan game drives for early morning or late afternoon, when temperatures are generally more comfortable, and wildlife is often more active.

Remember to pack sunscreen, hats, insect repellent and plenty of drinking water.

World.title: ‘She was fearless’: Ex-Joburg mayor mourns Nabeelah Shaikh
World.content:
Former City of Johannesburg mayor Dada Morero has expressed his sadness following the death of award-winning eNCA journalist Nabeelah Shaikh.

Shaikh who was pregnant died in hospital on Saturday, 14 November, following a short illness.

CONDOLENCES POUR IN FOR NABEELAH SHAIKH

According to eNCA, Shaikh was laid to rest on Saturday evening alongside her unborn child.



Taking to X, Morero described Shaikh as a fearless and familiar presence on the streets of Johannesburg who ensured that residents’ voices were heard.

“To Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Nabeelah Shaikh, eNCA’s award-winning investigative reporter, who was laid to rest last night together with her unborn child.

“Nabeelah was a fearless and familiar presence on the streets of Johannesburg. She went wherever the story was and made sure our residents’ voices were heard. At just 34, she leaves behind a body of work that held power to account, and a family who loved her dearly,” he wrote.



The former mayor also extended his condolences to Shaikh’s husband, daughter, family and loved ones.

“To her husband Waseem, her little girl Maahira, her parents Zafarullah and Rashida Bibi Shaikh, her brothers, and the eNCA family and the wider media fraternity, please accept my heartfelt condolences. May Allah grant her and her baby Jannatul Firdous, and grant her loved ones sabr in this painful time. Rest in peace, Nabeelah.”

Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. To Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Nabeelah Shaikh, eNCA's award-winning investigative reporter, who was laid to rest last night together with her unborn child.



Nabeelah was a fearless and… pic.twitter.com/zzzBTyZNoq  November 15, 2026

MEDIA FRATERNITY MOURNS RENOWNED JOURNALIST

Tributes have continued to pour in from colleagues and members of the media fraternity following the 34-year-old journalist’s passing.

The National Press Club and the South African National Editors’ Forum (SANEF) also expressed their condolences, remembering Shaikh as a dedicated journalist whose work reflected her commitment to the profession.

eNCA colleagues Manqoba Mchunu and Slindile Sebata also took to social media to pay tribute to their colleague.



“Rest well, Nabeelah Shaikh. We are heartbroken by your passing and that of our niece. May Allah grant you both Jannah and give your family strength. You were such a kind, sweet and caring soul. A true younger sister. Gone too soon. Rest in eternal peace,” Mchunu wrote.

“I can’t believe the news I woke up to. This is not how your story was meant to end. But you are no longer in pain. Rest in eternal glory. I’ll miss our chats and your beautiful energy. You are one of a kind,” Sebata wrote.
