World.title: From Sonia-Natwar row to Advani's Jinnah remarks: 5 political memoirs that stirred storm
World.content:
"I will write my own book and then you will come to know everything."

Sonia Gandhi's response to former external affairs minister Natwar Singh's explosive autobiography in 2014 was as much a promise as it was a rebuttal.

Singh's book had stirred a political storm with its account of why she declined the prime minister's post after the Congress-led UPA won the 2004 general elections.

More controversially, he claimed that Rahul Gandhi had strongly opposed his mother's elevation, fearing she could meet the same fate as her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, both of whom were assassinated. Sonia, who had publicly attributed her decision to her "inner voice", was now promising to tell her side of the story.



Twelve years later, that promise has come full circle. Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, was released on November 10, bringing her own account of her life, family and political journey into the public domain. The book has already triggered political reactions and renewed debate over some of the most contentious episodes involving the Gandhi family.

But Sonia is hardly the first political figure to find that putting personal recollections on paper can have consequences far beyond the pages of a book.





Over the years, memoirs by politicians have revisited ideological battles, exposed differences within parties, offered personal accounts of political turning points and reopened controversies that many thought had been settled.

From L K Advani's account of the Jinnah controversy to Jayaprakash Narayan's prison diary during the Emergency, these books have offered glimpses into the people and decisions behind some of India's defining political moments.

Here are five political memoirs that made headlines for what their authors chose to reveal.

Natwar Singh's One Life Is Not Enough

When Natwar Singh's autobiography was released in 2014, much of the attention centred on his account of Sonia Gandhi's decision not to become prime minister in 2004.

While Sonia had publicly described the decision as a call of her "inner voice", Singh offered a different explanation. He claimed that Rahul Gandhi had strongly opposed his mother's elevation, fearing that she could meet the same fate as her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, both of whom were assassinated.

Singh wrote that Rahul's opposition was so strong that he gave Sonia 24 hours to decide. He also claimed that he, Manmohan Singh, Suman Dubey and Priyanka Gandhi were present when Sonia struggled with the decision. According to him, Rahul's intervention ultimately led her to offer the post to Manmohan Singh.

The memoir went beyond the 2004 episode. Singh offered a sharply critical assessment of Sonia's leadership and her control over the Congress, describing her as increasingly authoritarian and secretive.

He also recounted conversations with former prime minister P V Narasimha Rao, who, according to Singh, was troubled by Sonia's attitude towards him.

The revelations triggered a political storm. Sonia rejected Singh's account and announced that she would write her own book. Former prime minister Manmohan Singh dismissed the claims as a "marketing gimmick", while the Congress accused Natwar Singh of distorting facts to promote his book.

The controversy deepened when Singh made remarks linking Sonia's alleged ruthlessness to her Italian origin, drawing further criticism.

Natwar Singh on Rahul Gandhiâs role in Soniaâs decision not to become PM

LK Advani's My Country, My Life

Released in New Delhi on March 19, 2008, by then President A P J Abdul Kalam, L K Advani's autobiography traced his journey from childhood in Karachi and Partition to his association with the RSS, the growth of the BJP, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and his years in the Union government.

One of its most discussed sections revisited the controversy surrounding Advani's June 2005 visit to Pakistan and his remarks on Muhammad Ali Jinnah. During the visit, Advani praised Jinnah's August 11, 1947, address to Pakistan's Constituent Assembly, in which the latter spoke about religious freedom and equal citizenship irrespective of religion.

The remarks triggered a backlash within the BJP and the Sangh Parivar.

Sections of the party viewed them as a departure from its ideological position, and Advani eventually resigned as BJP president.

Looking back at the episode, Advani described it as "simply the most agonising moment of my political life". He also recalled feeling let down by several party colleagues during the controversy, contrasting their response with the support he had received during the Hawala case in 1996.

Explaining the purpose of his Pakistan visit, he wrote: "I went to Pakistan as a messenger of peace, with an earnest desire to contribute to the normalisation of relations between our two long-estranged nations."

Advani maintained that he had not described Jinnah as secular but had referred to a particular speech as a "classic, a forceful espousal of a Secular State". He also argued that the media had reported his remarks without adequately explaining their historical context.

The autobiography also revisited the 1990 Rath Yatra and the demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992. Another section offered insights into his long association with former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. While acknowledging that the two sometimes differed in their approaches, Advani wrote that he had always regarded Vajpayee as his leader and generally deferred to his opinion.

Mamata Banerjee's My Unforgettable Memories

Published in January 2012 by Roli Books, Mamata Banerjee's My Unforgettable Memories offered a personal account of the relationships, disappointments and political rivalries that shaped her career.

The English book was a translation of excerpts from her earlier Bengali writings.

It appeared just months after Mamata led the Trinamool Congress to a historic victory in the 2011 West Bengal assembly elections, ending the Left Front's 34-year rule. Her observations about prominent political figures, particularly Sonia Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, attracted considerable attention.

Having spent years in the Congress before leaving the party to establish the Trinamool Congress in 1998, Mamata wrote about feeling repeatedly let down by its leadership.

She referred to Sonia Gandhi as the "Queen Mother" and criticised the party's treatment of regional leaders.

"The culture in Congress is that when a regional faction gets too active, it's immediately censored by the top leadership," she wrote.

Her account of Sonia, however, stood in contrast to the affection she expressed for Rajiv Gandhi, whom she described as "the leader of our hearts".

Mamata recalled that after she was attacked at a rally in Kolkata in 1991 by alleged CPM activists, Rajiv took responsibility for arranging and paying for her treatment.

He also sent people to ask whether she wanted to travel to the US for further medical care.

She wrote that she was devastated when she heard of Rajiv's assassination in May 1991. She said she could neither eat nor speak to anyone for a week and described the loss as being "orphaned all over again, for the second time in my life since my father's death".

The memoir also spoke warmly of former President Pranab Mukherjee, despite the changing political equations between the Congress and the Trinamool Congress.

"I have always respected him and my relationship with him is that of an elder brother and his kid sister," she wrote.

She recalled that when Mukherjee was sidelined by the Congress and formed the Rashtriya Samajwadi Congress in 1986, she had repeatedly requested Rajiv Gandhi to take him back into the party.

Jayaprakash Narayan's Prison Diary

Unlike the other books, Jayaprakash Narayan's Prison Diary was not a retrospective account written years after the events.

It was a record of his experiences during one of the most turbulent periods in India's democratic history: the Emergency.

Popularly known as JP, Narayan was among the most prominent leaders of the movement against Indira Gandhi's government in the 1970s. His call for Sampoorna Kranti (Total Revolution) had brought together students, opposition parties and civil society groups.

After the Allahabad high court set aside Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli on June 12, 1975, the movement gathered momentum.

On June 25, JP addressed a massive rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, calling for a peaceful struggle against the government. Hours later, the Emergency was proclaimed. In the early hours of June 26, opposition leaders, including JP, were arrested.

Written during his detention and published by Popular Prakashan in 1977, the diary documented his experiences in custody, his health, his reading and his reflections on the political crisis.

One of its most striking passages appeared in the opening entry, dated July 21, 1975, nearly a month after his arrest. JP wrote, "My world lies in a shambles all round me."

He went on to express disbelief that a democratically elected prime minister could use the law to undermine democracy and suppress political opposition. The diary also contained sharp criticism of the decision to impose the Emergency, arrest opposition leaders and curtail civil liberties.

Another deeply personal aspect of the book was its account of JP's deteriorating health. He was 72 when arrested and was already facing health problems. During his detention, his kidneys failed. He was released on November 12, 1975, on medical grounds and subsequently required regular dialysis for the remaining years of his life.

Published in the year the Emergency ended and the Janata Party came to power, Prison Diary offered a contemporary first-person account of the political crisis from one of its most prominent opponents.

Pranab Mukherjee's The Presidential Years

Former President Pranab Mukherjee's The Presidential Years (2012-2017) made headlines even before its release in December 2020. The book offered his assessment of the Congress's decline, his dealings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and some of the most consequential decisions taken during his presidency.

Looking back at the Congress's defeat in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, when the party won just 44 seats, Mukherjee attributed its performance to several factors, including its failure to recognise the end of its charismatic leadership.

He described the establishment as having been reduced to a "government of averages".

Why Pranab Mukherjee defended demonetisation without prior consultation

His observations also touched upon the Congress's leadership under Sonia Gandhi and Manmohan Singh.

The memoir was equally candid about his interactions with Modi during his five-year tenure as President. Mukherjee described their relationship as cordial and said he had regularly offered the prime minister advice on policy matters.

However, he criticised the NDA government's handling of Parliament between 2014 and 2019, blaming its "arrogance and inept handling" for the acrimonious exchanges between the treasury and opposition benches, while holding the opposition responsible too.

One of the most discussed revelations concerned demonetisation. Mukherjee disclosed that Modi had not consulted him before announcing the decision on November 8, 2016.

He said the lack of prior consultation did not surprise him, as the element of surprise was essential to such an announcement.

He recalled that Modi visited Rashtrapati Bhavan after announcing the decision and explained its rationale. Mukherjee described demonetisation as a bold step but warned that it could cause a temporary economic slowdown and that the government would have to be careful about easing the burden on the poor.

The memoir also became the subject of a family disagreement. Mukherjee's son, former Congress MP Abhijit Mukherjee, asked the publisher to halt publication until he had reviewed the final manuscript and given written consent. His daughter Sharmistha Mukherjee opposed the demand, saying their father had completed the manuscript before falling ill and that the final draft retained his handwritten notes and comments.

Pranab Mukherjee on the decline of charismatic leadership in Indian politics

Accusing her brother of creating "unnecessary hurdles", Sharmistha said preventing the book's release would be the "greatest disservice" to their departed father. The disagreement played out on social media, adding a family feud to the political conversations surrounding the memoir.

Political memoirs offer a rare window into the personal experiences and perspectives of those who have occupied positions of power.

They can reveal ideological differences, internal party dynamics and relationships that rarely find space in official accounts.

But they are also personal interpretations of history. The authors decide which episodes to revisit, which conversations to disclose and how to explain decisions made years earlier. And, as the controversies surrounding these books show, sometimes what a politician writes long after leaving office can reopen debates that their public life had never quite settled.

Here are top news stories of the day

Parliament's winter session likely in December; Centre plans Constitution amendment on women's quota

The winter session of Parliament is likely to commence in the first week of December, with the government looking to secure the passage of a Constitution amendment bill linking women's reservation to delimitation.

The proposed legislation seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats, enabling the implementation of 33% reservation for women before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. However, the NDA, with 320 MPs, will need opposition support to secure the two-thirds majority required to pass the bill. The session is also expected to witness fresh confrontations over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.



India beat New Zealand by 22 runs to clinch ODI series 3-1

India defeated New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth ODI to clinch the series 3-1, with an inexperienced bowling attack stepping up to defend a target of 210. Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan scored 46 runs each as India were bowled out for 209 in 42.1 overs. Arshdeep Singh led the bowling effort with three wickets for 30 runs, while Axar picked up the final wicket to bowl out New Zealand for 187 in 48.1 overs.

Biden accuses Netanyahu of breaking promises on civilian casualties in Gaza in upcoming memoir

Former US president Joe Biden has accused Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu of repeatedly promising to reduce civilian casualties in Gaza but following those assurances with military actions that killed more Palestinians.





In his forthcoming memoir, Promise Me, America, Biden describes a recurring pattern in his dealings with Netanyahu, saying the Israeli PM made promises he had no intention of keeping. He also questions Netanyahu's political judgement, accusing him of prioritising his short-term political interests over Israel's long-term security.

Indian student gets 30 years in UK jail for grooming 70 girls online, forcing them into sexual acts

An Indian student has been sentenced to 30 years in prison in the UK for grooming at least 70 girls online and coercing them into sexual acts.

Bilal Kazi (27), a student at the University of Chester, was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to 37 child sexual abuse offences, including blackmail and making indecent images of children. Kazi posed as a white British teenage boy named Reece on social media and gaming platforms, including Snapchat, Roblox and Wink, to gain the trust of girls aged 10 to 15.

Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail. Without Gyanesh Kumar, neither Narendra Modi would have become Prime Minister nor Amit Shah would have become home minister,â he said.

World.title: ‘Chats show no mention of Pulkit’: Convict’s father seeks action in Ankita Bhandari murder case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The father of Ankita Bhandari murder convict Pulkit Arya on Sunday demanded action against those who allegedly harassed her, specifically naming her parents.

Addressing a press conference in Haridwar, Vinod Arya presented what he described as chat logs spanning around 4,800 pages, claiming they showed no mention of his son Pulkit in Ankita's conversations.

He also claimed there was no VIP involved in the case and denied any attempt to influence the narrative or link the matter to elections.

"The chat consists of approximately 4,800 pages...to our knowledge, there is no VIP involved in this entire case. We have no connection to the elections, nor are we trying to steer the narrative. Our sole demand is that action be taken against those who harassed Ankita which is her father and mother.



Throughout the entire set of chats, Ankita never once mentioned Pulkit," he said.

"If the Chief Minister truly seeks justiceâif he genuinely wants to ensure justice for Ankita Bhandariâthen action must also be taken against those who harassed her," he said.

Ankita Bhandari, who worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Rishikesh, was killed on September 18, 2022. Her body was recovered from the Chilla canal four days later.





The parents of Ankita have been staging in New Delhi while protesting against the appointment of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor near India Gate on October 14.

Resort owner Pulkit Arya, son of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, and his two accomplices were sentenced to life imprisonment in the case. The case attracted political attention over allegations of the involvement of an unidentified VIP.

World.title: '100% pure' or just marketing? What the law says about misleading food labels
World.content:
A food packet promises "100% pure" fruit juice, authentic honey or whole-grain biscuits, yet in India it has become a normal understanding that such claims are over the top.

In a different scenario, the ingredients listed on an online grocery platform also differ from what arrives at the doorstep.

With the online grocery shopping trend growing, these discrepancies are becoming a serious food safety and consumer protection concern.

The

, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, lay down obligations for manufacturers, sellers and e-commerce platforms.

But it requires knowing what constitutes misleading labelling, understanding which authority to approach and preserving the right evidence.



Raids alone cannot ensure food safety

The latest

enforcement figures say that it suspended 1,133 licences, cancelled 52 and sealed 314 premises.

Ashwin Bhadri, a national resource person for FSSAI says the real challenge begins after the inspection team leaves. Inspections and punitive action are necessary because they remind businesses that authorities are watching, but temporary fixes do not address the reasons behind repeated violations.

"A crackdown is an event. Food safety is a habit," Bhadri explains. "A suspension is a pause. What I wonder about is what changed inside the business during the pause. Was the pest-control contract fixed, or was the kitchen simply cleaned for the visit? Was the cause of the failure found, or only the symptom?"

He says visible violations often point to deeper problems in raw material sourcing, supplier verification, cleaning practices and quality checks during manufacturing.





Parliamentary figures for 2025-26 show the same gap.

"The wider numbers show where the challenge lies. The government told Parliament that of 2,23,808 food samples analysed in 2025-26, 40,023 were found non-conforming, close to one in five. The figures are provisional, and non-conforming covers a wide range, from misbranding to genuine adulteration. Convictions over the same period stood at 1,918. I would not read those two numbers as a ratio.

But together they tell us something: the system is far better at finding problems than at seeing them through to a lasting fix," Bhadri observes.

What Indian law says about

misleading food labels

Three laws govern these responsibilities: the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.

1. Ingredients must be declared in the correct order

The Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020, framed under Section 23 of the FSSAI Act, set the basic requirements for food labels.

Ankita, senior associate, Chamber of Jain and Kumar, explains that ingredient disclosure remains a fundamental obligation:

"In Under Regulation 5 of the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020, food manufacturers are required to declare ingredients on pre-packaged food products, generally in descending order of their composition by weight or volume. The law also mandates disclosures concerning allergens, nutritional information and food additives, wherever applicable.

The 2026 amendments introduce additional labelling-related requirements, but do not remove the fundamental obligation to disclose ingredients," she says.

2. When does a food product become misbranded?

Section 3(f) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, defines misbranded food, i.e., when a product is sold under a deceptive name, presented as a substitute for another food, or carries a statement, design or representation about its ingredients or composition that is false or misleading.

For instance, a product marketed as "100% pure" that contains undeclared ingredients contradicting the claim could attract scrutiny under these provisions.

Penalties depend on the violation:

Section 52 (misbranded food): Manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing or importing misbranded food for human consumption can attract a penalty of up to Rs 3 lakh.

Manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing or importing misbranded food for human consumption can attract a penalty of up to Rs 3 lakh. Section 53 (misleading s): Publishing or participating in a misleading food  can attract a penalty of up to Rs 10 lakh.

Publishing or participating in a misleading food  can attract a penalty of up to Rs 10 lakh. Section 51 (sub-standard food): Food that fails prescribed compositional standards but is not necessarily unsafe can attract a penalty of up to Rs 5 lakh.

Under the licensing framework, including Regulation 2.1.8 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, authorities can also suspend or cancel a food business licence for non-compliance.

Can an online grocery platform be held responsible?

The manufacturer may argue the product was correctly labelled, while the platform may say the seller uploaded the description. But India's framework also covers online food businesses and e-commerce entities.

Product information must be displayed.

The Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations, 2018, which introduced provisions for e-commerce food business operators, require platforms to give consumers relevant product information before purchase.

They also provide for a minimum remaining shelf life of 30% or 45 days before expiry, whichever applies, at the time of delivery.

Misleading descriptions are prohibited.

The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, place obligations on marketplaces and inventory-based platforms.

Descriptions and s must be consistent with the actual characteristics of the goods, which matters most when a listing claims "pure", "natural", "sugar-free" or "whole-grain".

Consumers have a statutory right to accurate information.

Section 2(9) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, recognises the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods. Section 2(11) defines deficiency in service, and Section 2(47) deals with unfair trade practices.

If the delivered product differs materially from the description at the time of purchase, the consumer may invoke these provisions, depending on the facts.

The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) can investigate misleading s and issue directions under Section 21.

It can order their discontinuation or modification and impose penalties of up to Rs 10 lakh for a first contravention and up to Rs 50 lakh for subsequent ones.

Fine print is not a shield

Regulation 4 of the 2020 Labelling and Display Regulations requires mandatory declarations to be clear, prominent, indelible and readily legible under normal conditions of purchase and use, and prescribes minimum font heights based on the area of the principal display panel.

A manufacturer cannot rely on an inconspicuous disclaimer to avoid its labelling obligations.

"Fine print can sometimes be used to obscure material information and make important disclosures difficult for consumers to notice. However, statutory labelling requirements cannot be bypassed through disclaimers or inconspicuous disclosures,â says Ankita.

âMandatory declarations must comply with the prescribed requirements concerning visibility and legibility.

Consumers can challenge misleading or inadequate disclosures before the relevant regulatory authorities and Consumer Commissions," Ankita adds.

What should consumers do

For a Rs 150 or Rs 600 grocery order, a regulator or consumer court can seem excessive.

But consumers need not begin with litigation. India offers several administrative and pre-litigation routes.

Step 1: Keep the packaging and document the discrepancy

Do not throw away the packet or jar. Ankita says the packaging, invoice, batch details and photographs can become key evidence:

"A consumer can report the violation to FSSAI or the concerned State Food Safety Department.

They can also approach the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or file a complaint before the appropriate Consumer Commission. It is important to preserve the product packaging, purchase invoice, batch number and photographs of the label as evidence," she advises.

Preserve five categories of evidence:

The wrapper, carton, bottle or jar. If still sealed, keep it unopened. Full-screen screenshots of the product title, ingredient claims, nutritional information and photographs shown in the app when the order was placed. The invoice and order details downloaded from the platform. Photographs of the batch or lot number, manufacturing date, expiry or Use By date, MRP and the 14-digit FSSAI licence number on the packet. Emails, in-app chats and other communications with the platform or manufacturer.

Step 2: Approach the platform's grievance officer

Under Rule 4(4) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, every e-commerce entity must prominently display the name and contact details of its Grievance Officer.

The officer must acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and redress it within one month.

Step 3: Register a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline

If the platform does not resolve the issue, approach the National Consumer Helpline (NCH), run by the Department of Consumer Affairs. Call 1915, use the NCH mobile app, or visit

.

Step 4: Report the violation directly to FSSAI

For issues of ingredients, food safety, misbranding or misleading food claims, complaints can go through the Food Safety Connect mobile app or the Food Safety Compliance System portal at

.

Provide the product's 14-digit FSSAI licence number and upload photographs of the alleged violation. Unlike a routine refund request, a regulatory complaint can lead to scrutiny by the jurisdictional Designated Officer or Food Safety Officer, who may inspect the manufacturing facility, warehouse or dark store and initiate proceedings under the Act.

Step 5: Consider sending a legal notice

A written legal notice to the manufacturer and the platform can identify the discrepancy and cite provisions such as Regulation 5 of the 2020 Labelling and Display Regulations and Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

It puts the parties on formal notice of the allegations and potential consequences. Ankita says litigation need not come first:

When to approach the Consumer Commission

If the manufacturer or platform refuses to act, consumers can go to the appropriate Consumer Commission. Under Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction where the consideration paid does not exceed Rs 50 lakh.

Complaints can be filed on the e-Daakhil portal at edaakhil.nic.in, which allows submission of documents from home and virtual proceedings where permitted, without necessarily engaging a lawyer.

Under Section 38(2)(c) of the Act, a Commission can direct that a sample be sent to an appropriate laboratory. Consumers can also submit an independent test report from an NABL-accredited laboratory.

What compensation and action can consumers seek

Under Section 39(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Commissions can direct refunds, replacement of goods and compensation for loss or injury, including mental agony, plus litigation costs.

They can also order a business to discontinue an unfair trade practice, withdraw hazardous or misdescribed goods, and pay punitive damages into the Consumer Welfare Fund. A complaint about one purchase can therefore have wider implications if the same practice affects other consumers.

Why consumers still hesitate

Pursuing a complaint is not always straightforward. Proceedings take time, and it can be hard to establish exactly how a product's composition differs from its declared ingredients.

Manufacturers may call the discrepancy a technical or inadvertent labelling error, and actual composition disputes may need independent testing. The low cost of a single grocery purchase can also discourage complaints.

"The principal hurdles are procedural delays that sometimes take a toll on an average consumer. Sometimes, establishing the violation, proving the loss or injury suffered are some other common hurdles.

Companies may sometimes argue that a discrepancy is merely a technical or inadvertent labelling error. Therefore, proper documentation and demonstrating how the violation affects consumer rights become particularly important," notes Ankita.

The principal hurdles are procedural delays that sometimes take a toll on an average consumer. Anikita, senior associate, Chamber of Jain and Kumar

She further adds, "I strongly encourage consumers to call out companies engaging in misleading practices, provided their allegations are supported by facts and evidence.

Public accountability creates pressure on companies to follow statutory requirements. Consumer awareness is one of the strongest deterrents against unfair trade practices, and companies must understand that regulatory compliance is not optional.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

You might have also seen a surge of such cases in present times where FSSAI has suo moto taken actions against companies who are violating the norms.â

Food label more than a marketing claim

For food businesses, compliance cannot stop at correcting labels after an inspection or controversy.

For consumers, the key safeguard is to look beyond the claims shown prominently on a packet or app. Ankita says transparency is a legal obligation, not a voluntary promise:

"I would emphasise that consumers have a fundamental right to know what they are purchasing and consuming. Transparency in labelling is not a privilege offered by companies; it is a statutory obligation. With evolving FSSAI regulations and increasing consumer awareness, companies must prioritise transparency and compliance over marketing strategies. Ultimately, an informed consumer is the strongest safeguard against unfair trade practices," she concludes.

The next time a grocery order arrives, checking the back of the packet may be just as important as checking the price on the screen.

World.title: Chalakkayam-Pampa road reopens a day ahead of Sabarimala season
World.content:
With just a day to go for the annual pilgrimage season to begin, the Chalakkayam-Pampa road, the main access route to Sabarimala, has been reopened to traffic after a major upgrade.

Inaugurating the restored road here on Sunday, Public Works Minister P. K. Basheer described the completion of the project in just one month as a proud achievement of the department. He credited the coordination among various departments and thanked Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan for his support in expediting the work.

The 4.5-km stretch has been upgraded to modern standards, with the road widened to 12 metres.

According to Mr.Basheer, the decision to take up the renovation on a war footing was made at a review meeting chaired by the Chief Minister in Thiruvananthapuram as part of efforts to improve infrastructure ahead of the pilgrimage season. Administrative sanction was granted within 24 hours and Cabinet approval secured within an hour, paving the way for the work to begin. All necessary procedures were completed within the stipulated time.

The Minister also announced that the government had approved a special PWD package worth ₹553 crore for various development works linked to the Sabarimala pilgrimage. Nearly 80% of the works under the package have already been tendered. The initiative is expected to accelerate the development of pilgrimage routes and improve basic infrastructure.

According to PWD officials, the road has been laid with a 5-cm-thick bituminous macadam (BM) layer topped by a 3-cm-thick bituminous concrete (BC) layer. Its foundation has also been strengthened with a 20 to 30-cm-thick layer of metal aggregate to improve its load-bearing capacity and durability.The project also included ancillary works such as the laying of concrete interlocking blocks along both sides of the road from Thriveni to the U-turn. Protective structures have also been incorporated to ensure safer travel for pilgrims.

Health and Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan presided over the function.

World.title: Vijayapura co-op not involved in any financial irregularities, says Yatnal
World.content:
Vijayapura-based Siddhasiri Multi-state, Multi-purpose Cooperative Society is not involved in any irregularity or financial misconduct nor has it violated any law or rule, MLA and president of the society Basanagouda Patil Yatnal said in Vijayapura on Sunday.

He was responding to allegations that the Central Registrar of Cooperative Society earlier raised some questions about some of the society’s transactions.

“Any society that converts into a multi-state society has five years compliance time to follow the Central laws. All our transactions and audit processes are according to the State laws. We have ample time to follow the Central laws. We have uploaded some audit documents prepared as per State laws into the CRCS portal. Since these are slightly different from those prepared as per Central rules, we have received a letter, with certain observations and seeking clarifications,” he told reporters.

“This is not to be construed as a notice given to a wrongdoer,” he said.

He said that there is some misunderstanding about the ownership of Chincholi Sugar and Bio Industries Ltd., where his son Ramanagouda Patil is a director, and denied the charge that he diverted funds from Siddhasiri to his son’s factory.

He, his wife, his two sons or other family members do not own any land or assets in their names in Chincholi, he said.

“All the properties are in the names of either Siddhasiri or Chincholi Sugar,” he said.

The Central Registrar of Cooperative Society has questioned the society’s investment of ₹1,065,81,20,358.39 in Chincholi Sugar calling it “related-party transactions” and pointing out that it has not been disclosed in the audited accounts of the society.

The Central Registrar has also asked the society what measures are being taken to safeguard its investment and what return it has earned.

“We received the letter on August 14, 2026. We have given satisfactory answers to all the queries,” Mr. Yatnal said.

“The Central Registrar has objected to Siddhasiri running a chit fund. Hence, we have delinked the business, while the directors have formed a private company for the purpose. That has been communicated to the Central Registrar,” he said.

Mr. Yatnal said that the Central Registrar has “wrongly understood” some of the “easy loans” as unsecured loans.

“We convinced the Central Registrar that they are secured loans given after obtaining three guarantees and five cheques. The other observations are minor issues, including signatures of some officials missing from some documents. They have all been corrected and submitted,” he said.

World.title: Retired Havildar takes on veteran BJP leader in Rajamahendravaram mayoral battle
World.content:
The contest for the Mayor’s post in the Rajamahendravaram Municipal Corporation (RMC) has intensified after the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) fielded retired Havildar Daasi Venkata Rao against BJP’s long-standing party worker, Relangi Rani Sridevi. Enrolled in the Indian Army as a Jawan in 1969, Mr. Venkata Rao retired as a Havildar after serving for 15 years. He is currently a contractor based in Rajamahendravaram city. Proposed by YSRCP East Godavari district president Ch. Venugopala Krishna and former MP Margani Bharat, Mr. Venkata Rao filed his nomination papers for the Mayor’s post on Sunday. Speaking to the media later, Mr. Venkata Rao said; “Developmental projects would be his top priority and that transparency and discipline in administration would be guaranteed if he is voted to power”.

He recalled that the city had witnessed transformation and infrastructure development during the YSRCP rule. Bond with party

On Sunday, BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav announced Ms. Sridevi as the NDA alliance candidate. She is scheduled to file her nomination for the Mayor’s post on Monday. Ms. Sridevi has been associated with the BJP for many years.

Currently, Ms. Sridevi, is serving as the BJP In-Charge of West Godavari district. She served as the party’s former vice president of Andhra Pradesh (2021-25), and as the State president of BJP Mahila Morcha from 2009-12. In 2014, she was elected as a corporator in the Rajamahendravaram Municipal Corporation. The Mayor post is reserved for SC-General, posing a challenge for the YSRCP and the BJP in finding suitable candidates, as some of the key Mayor aspirants been associated with the parties were found to be ineligible to contest. Manifesto

The mayoral candidates of both the parties are yet to announce their manifestos, as they were fielded by their respective parties at the eleventh hour to meet the nomination deadline. Monday is the last date for filing nominations for the Mayor’s post. However, the new Mayor is likely to focus on the Godavari Pushkarams-2027 and infrastructure projects as the road map. The 2026 election will be the first election to the RMC after 11 villages, including Dowleswaram, Bommuru, Hukumpeta, were merged.

World.title: Karnataka seeks one year’s time to file submissions over Kasturirangan report, says Ramalinga Reddy
World.content:
Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy said on Sunday that the State government has sought one year’s time from the Union government to conduct a ground survey to identify the Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA), as mentioned by the Kasturirangan Committee report, and file submissions to oppose the recommendations of the committee.

Speaking to reporters at the Pilikula Nisargadhama in Mangaluru, Mr. Reddy said the State government had rejected the recommendations of the Kasturirangan Committee six times. For the seventh time, too, the State Cabinet decided to reject the recommendations. Before making the submission to the Centre, the government has to submit a ground report of the affected areas by doing a survey, he said.

When the ground survey done in the past was pointed out, the Minister said: “If the ground survey report done in the past was not submitted to the Centre, it will not serve any purpose. Like the way it was done by Keralam, we too will make our submission (to reject the recommendations) by enclosing the ground survey report. We have sought one year’s time; the Centre will grant time.”

A committee headed by the Deputy Commissioner would be formed at the district level, while a similar committee will be formed at the State level. Retired judges and domain experts would be involved in the ground survey. “A joint survey will be done at the panchayat level. This will give a permanent solution (to the issue of implementing the Kasturirangan Committee recommendations for the protection of the Western Ghats). It is a time-bound work, and there is no question of the government dragging its feet on the issue,” Mr. Reddy said.

On the deemed forest issue, the Minister said a joint survey of the deemed forest area would be completed in another three months. The joint survey would be conducted by the Forest and Revenue Departments across the State. After the demarcation of the deemed forest land, the remaining land would be handed over to the Revenue Department. “The joint survey will end the problem related to deemed forest land, which is across the State,” he said.

World.title: Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival 2026: Nelly, Khalid, and Swae Lee headline two days of music
World.content:
Shillong has always had an ear for music. Long before Spotify and YouTube, its musical tastes were shaped by worn-out cassettes, CDs and mixtapes. Hip-hop, R&B, pop and alternative rock gradually found a place in the city’s musical landscape, sharing space with its thriving local rock scene. This November, the Shillong Cherry Blossom Festival will celebrate this musical legacy with a lineup that cuts across generations and genres.

Scheduled for November 20 and 21, the 2026 edition features international acts including American rapper Nelly, pop-rock band Boys Like Girls, singer Khalid, rapper Swae Lee and retro-pop artist Elliot James Reay, alongside Indian singer Darshan Raval. While the lineup offers something for different generations of listeners, it also reflects the city’s taste for global sounds in music.

The festival takes its name from the wild Himalayan cherry trees, which burst into bloom every autumn, painting Shillong’s hills, streets and parks, along with the surrounding Khasi Hills, in shades of pink.

Back to school

Nelly’s early 2000s hits such as ‘Hot in Herre’, ‘Dilemma’ and ‘Ride with Me’ bring back an era when MTV became a core childhood memory; Boys Like Girls, with tracks such as ‘The Great Escape’ and ‘Love Drunk’, recall the pop-rock movement that resonates with young guitar enthusiasts, and for many Gen Zs, Darshan Raval was what Hindi pop sounded like.

Khalid’s ‘Location’, ‘Young Dumb & Broke’, and ‘Better’, along with Swae Lee’s ‘Sunflower’ and ‘Unforgettable’, represent the streaming-platform generation.

For Jason Manners, organiser of the festival says that creating an international-level music festival in Shillong, “is a dream for us, but also a nightmare because we are victims of geography.” He explains, “We are located in a hill station. We don’t have a proper international airport. We are not lucky to be near any big city that makes it easy for an international artist to tour and make the decision to tour. So it is very much organic.”

Jason traces the journey back to 2013, when he travelled to the US to accompany the Maharaja of Tripura Pradyot Bikram Manikya Deb Barma in search of a band for Shillong. His intention was to introduce a fresh musical experience to the city, and the effort eventually led to the booking of an international act. Over the years, he began building relationships within the global music industry. When the Meghalaya government came on board with a similar vision of using music as a means of attracting tourists, the idea of a larger festival began taking shape. “The Government of Meghalaya, especially Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma, has played a pivotal role behind the festival,” says Jason.

Organising a festival of this scale comes with challenges. Recalling an early edition during the COVID years, Jason says, “It got too packed. The audience had to be sent home, and the police had to deploy tear gas, which created a law and order situation. That’s when we also started getting a lot of media attention.”

An experience rooted in culture

Convincing international artists to travel to Shillong also requires considerable effort. “We have to really explain to them what Shillong is and what kind of music culture we have here. And we have to make their journey as comfortable as possible. Some artists have even arrived by helicopter,” says Jason. Despite initial reservations about the journey, he says artists are often impressed by the production and audience. “Most of them actually say that it was the best live show they had in a long time.”

Beyond the music, the festival aims to offer visitors an experience rooted in the food and culture of the Northeast. This year, the food line-up will include traditional Khasi, Jaintia and Garo cuisine, alongside a range of barbecue options, reflecting the region’s love for non-vegetarian fare. Some of the food stalls include The Garo Flavours, Garo Food Hub, Jaintia Indigenous Food, The Pnar’s Kitchen, Al Khasi Stall, and Marshra Khasi, among others. Visitors can also explore merchandise stalls featuring local products, apparel and accessories, as well as games and interactive activities, adding to the festival’s distinctly Shillong and Northeast India-centric experience

The festival is also extending its reach beyond the two days of performances. The Indian International Music Week will be held a day before the festival, bringing together delegates from the music industry. It also works alongside Meghalaya’s Grassroots Music Programme, connecting young local musicians with industry experts through workshops, discussions, artist showcases and sessions.

Jason says their growing popularity has also allowed them to support the music economies of other Northeastern States. After helping Sikkim organise its first international music festival last year, called the Orchid Music Festival in Sikkim, the team is now assisting Arunachal Pradesh with artist bookings and logistical planning for Euphonic Voyage.

“For the people of Shillong, the Cherry Blossom Festival is special because it’s truly homegrown - it has grown out of our own soil. It’s bringing artists who have been part of our childhood. Watching these artists live is not just entertainment; it’s emotional healing, and nostalgia,” says Jason.

The Cherry Blossom Festival will be held on November 20 and 21 at the Madan Kurkalang Sports Complex in Bhoirymbong, Shillong. For registration visit www.rockskitickets.com

World.title: New buildings for Rasipuram GH will be inaugurated in four months, says Health Minister
World.content:
Minister for Health K.G. Arunraj said on Sunday (November 15) that construction of new buildings at Rasipuram government district headquarters hospital will end soon and it will be inaugurated in four months.

Minister Arunraj and Minister for Commercial Taxes and Registration D. Logesh Tamilselvan inspected the ongoing construction at Rasipuram Government District Headquarters Hospital.

Speaking to reporters, Dr. Arunraj, said the new buildings with six floors are being constructed at ₹53.39 crore on 6.99 acre. The hospital will have a post-mortem examination building and other facilities.

For levelling works from the main road to the hospital, ₹5 crore has been allocated in the budget for gravel filling and for installing paver blocks. Soon a government order will be issued and work will start. Based on the Chief Minister’s instruction, the new buildings will be inaugurated in the next four months, the Minister added.

Stating that 4,724 nurses were appointed in government hospitals across the State, the Minister said that 284 specialist doctor posts were created for 11 new medical college hospitals, and soon these posts would be filled.

Later the Ministers inaugurated three completed projects worth ₹3.48 crore in the Paramathi Velur Assembly constituency, including a new primary health centre building worth ₹1.20 crore at Paramathi and an additional building worth ₹78.20 lakh at Nallur primary health centre.

Likewise, the Ministers inaugurated three completed projects worth ₹3.15 crore in the Namakkal Assembly constituency, including a sub-health centre building worth ₹45 lakh at Nathamedu, an Ayush building worth ₹1.50 crore at the old government hospital in Namakkal, and a primary health centre building worth ₹1.20 crore at Periyapatti.

In these functions, District Collector L. Madhubalan, MLAs Dileep and Chandrasekar, and officials from concerned departments participated.

World.title: KPSC exam passes off smoothly in Dharwad
World.content:
The Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) probationary gazetted officers examination passed off smoothly in Dharwad on Sunday.

A total of 6,316 candidates had enrolled for the exam at 18 examination centres.

In the morning session, 4,009 candidates appeared for the exam and in the post-lunch session, 3,971 candidates took the exam.

The district administration and the Hubballi-Dharwad Police made elaborate security arrangements to ensure the smooth and transparent conduct of the competitive examinations in Dharwad, in accordance with the directions of the commission.

Deputy Commissioner Snehal R., who inspected the arrangements for the examination, said that candidates have been instructed to keep their bags at designated locations at least 100 metres away from the frisking points where they were screened using metal detectors.

Police personnel were deployed around examination centres to prevent the entry of unauthorised persons.

Identity cards were issued by the Deputy Commissioner’s office to staff assigned examination duties and only authorised personnel carrying valid identity cards were allowed on campuses, she said.

CCTV cameras and signal jammers were installed in every examination hall, with two invigilators appointed for each room.

Police personnel were also involved in screening candidates at the examination centres.

Officials were told to collect examination material from each centre after the completion of the examinations and segregate them into four bundles for distribution to the designated offices.

Of the four bundles collected from each centre, two must be sent to the scanning centre, one to the Deputy Commissioner’s office and the fourth to the District Disability Welfare Officer’s (DDPO) office.

Hubballi-Dharwad Police Commissioner Borase Bhushan Gulabrao said that elaborate police security arrangements were made to ensure the examinations were conducted peacefully and transparently.

Over 400 police personnel and officers were deployed, which was higher than the prescribed requirement.

The number of personnel assigned to frisking and security duties was determined based on the number of candidates, he said.

Frisking arrangements were made for male and female candidates. Standardised, colour-coded handheld metal detectors were used for screening. The police were also keeping a close watch on social media platforms as part of preventive measures to avert any untoward incidents.

World.title: Will discuss induction of woman Minister with high command: Karnataka CM
World.content:
The discussion on Cabinet expansion to fill the remaining two berths appears to be gaining traction again, especially with a little over a fortnight left for the commencement of the Winter Session of the legislature in Belagavi. The absence of a woman minister in the Cabinet has been a particular point of contention.

While the Cabinet headed by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar was expanded in August, two Cabinet berths remain vacant, one following the resignation of B. Nagendra over charges of corruption, and another that has not been filled at all.

On Sunday, the Chief Minister said: “I have brought the matter of inducting a woman into the Cabinet to the attention of the Congress high command in Delhi. I cannot say whether the process will happen tomorrow, but they have told me that they will call me to Delhi to discuss it. This is something that needs to be done and we will definitely see it through.”

Trip to Delhi

The Chief Minister is leaving for Delhi on Monday to attend the launch of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.

The task of inducting a woman has been hanging fire since the Cabinet expansion in August. Though the list of legislators to be accommodated in the Cabinet, released by the All India Congress Committee, included the name of Member of the Legislative Council A.V. Gayatri Shanthegowda, her name disappeared when a fresh list was announced after former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah opposed her candidature.

Party sources said that though the name of E. Annapoorna Tukaram had come up for serious discussion earlier, a section of leaders is opposed to her candidature as she is a first-time legislator. “There is a suggestion within the party to accommodate a woman without caste and regional considerations. There is pressure from women legislators on the party leadership too.”

World.title: A 30-year-old power dispute, and a political prize for Himachal CM Sukhu
World.content:
On November 6, the Supreme Court ended an around three-decade-old power-sharing dispute between Himachal Pradesh and four defendants — Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Chandigarh — over the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas projects.

The Court directed Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity in a respective ratio of 58:42 from the Bhakra-Nangal project and 60:40 from the Beas project. The Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), a statutory body, maintains and operates the power projects, delivering approximately 14,000 million units of electricity annually.

Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu described the SC verdict as favourable and credited his government’s sustained efforts for it. Although Opposition BJP leaders hailed the SC verdict, they challenged Sukhu for taking the entire credit.

History



The projects were proposed to be constructed in 1944 and completed after independence. The Bhakra-Nangal project was inaugurated in 1954, and the Beas project became operational in the 1970s.

The Bhakra-Nangal and the Beas projects were built in Bilaspur (27,869 acres) and in Kangra district (65,050 acres), respectively — both form part of the present-day Himachal Pradesh. But power generated by these projects was also enjoyed principally by the composite State of Punjab — and by Haryana and Rajasthan and the Union Territory of Chandigarh after the reorganisation of Punjab in 1966.

Raja Anand Chand of the erstwhile princely estate of Bilaspur ceded to the dominion of India by the Bilaspur Merger Agreement on August 15, 1948. Before this, on July 7, 1948, a draft agreement was prepared between the Government of Bilaspur and the then Government of East Punjab on the terms on which land of Bilaspur territory would be made available for the Bhakra project, and the compensation payable, including a provision for allocation of power to the erstwhile state of Bilaspur. But this draft was not formally signed or executed.

Bilaspur, thereafter, continued to be administered as a Chief Commissioner’s Province under the States Merger (Chief Commissioners’ Provinces) Order, 1949, and was included as a Part C State. In 1954, Bilaspur and the Himachal Pradesh region were united to form a new State of Himachal Pradesh under the Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur (New States) Act, 1954. The geographical area was further enlarged in 1966 by the transfer of territory from the composite State of Punjab under Section 5 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, and finally Himachal Pradesh became a full State of the Indian Union on January 25, 1971.

The dispute



The dispute originated after the reorganisation of Punjab on November 1, 1966, when Haryana was carved out as a separate state, and Himachal Pradesh’s claim to a share in the electricity generated by the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas projects became contentious. In 1996, Himachal moved a suit under Article 131 in the Supreme Court against the Union of India, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan and Chandigarh. Under the then chief minister Virbhadra Singh, Himachal’s demands included 12 per cent of the net electricity generated as a host state, since the projects were situated in its territory. Second, it sought a 7.19 per cent share based on the population-transfer ratio following the reorganisation of Punjab. The state also demanded compensation of Rs 2,199.77 crore for the electricity withheld since November 1, 1966, along with interest.

SC’s 2011 judgment — a cornerstone

The November 6 judgment is rooted in the SC’s 2011 decree, settling the fundamental legal question of Himachal’s entitlement to power from the two projects, while rejecting the principal objections raised against Himachal’s suit about the maintainability and merits. The judgment held Himachal’s claim “maintainable under Article 131 of the Constitution” and ruled that the merger of Bilaspur with Himachal did not extinguish the state’s independent legal claim. It further held that the dispute was not barred by Articles 363 or 262(2) of the Constitution, as it concerned the sharing of electricity rather than the use of inter-state river waters.

The apex court also confirmed certain entitlements for Himachal: the state will get 6.095 per cent of the total electricity generated, effective November 1, 1966, from Bhakra-Nangal Project; the state will get 5.752 per cent of the total electricity generated, from the commencement of production, from Beas Unit I; and 2.984 per cent of the total electricity generated, from the commencement of production from Beas Unit-2. These represented Himachal’s total 7.19 per cent entitlement attributable to the erstwhile composite Punjab, applied to the respective projects. The court also determined the corresponding shares of Punjab and Haryana at 51.8 per cent and 37.51 per cent, respectively, while Chandigarh’s 3.5 per cent requirement was to be met by Punjab and Haryana from their shares.

The SC, however, excluded Rajasthan from the list of defendants because Rajasthan had never formed a part of composite Punjab. But the Court rejected Himachal’s separate claim for 12 per cent free electricity under the host-state principle.



BJP’s Prem Kumar Dhumal was the chief minister in 2011.

How Nov 6 judgment differs and what lies ahead for four defendants

The 2011 judgment established Himachal’s legal entitlement to electricity, but the actual calculation and delivery of accumulated arrears remained unresolved. The November 6 judgment provided the mechanism for implementing the earlier decree, with the Court converting the state’s legally recognised entitlement into a time-bound supply arrangement, providing it with a potentially valuable source of revenue.

The state will receive approximately 11,973 million units, or nearly 1,197.3 crore units, of electricity over 20 lean seasons (between October and March yearly). This translates into an annual supply of approximately 598 million units. But the state will not receive the entire 13,066 MU calculated as arrears. Its capital-cost liability of Rs 420.77 crore has been deducted from the outstanding amount, with the adjustment valued at Rs 3.85 per unit, equivalent to approximately 1,093 MU. The remaining 11,973 MU is what Punjab and Haryana must supply.



In the recent judgment, the SC rejected Punjab’s objections that the arrears should be reduced by accounting for the daily supply of 1.2 lakh units to Himachal. It also disputed the method used to calculate the capital-cost liability, arguing the current operation and maintenance rate of 79 paise per unit should be applied instead of Rs 3.85 per unit. The Court found these objections unconvincing. Also, Punjab wanted the electricity arrears to be supplied over 30 years instead of the proposed 15 years, but the Court rejected it and granted some relief by extending the repayment period to 20 lean seasons.

Thus, the electricity will be supplied in the following inter-state proportions: Bhakra-Nangal Project: Punjab and Haryana will share the supply in the ratio of 58:42. Beas Projects: Punjab and Haryana will share the supply in the ratio of 60:40. Thus, both states will have to divert a portion of the electricity otherwise available to them towards fulfilling Himachal Pradesh’s outstanding entitlement. The court has also clarified that Himachal Pradesh must pay the charges determined by the BBMB for the year in which each tranche of electricity is received.

Shot in the arm for Sukhu

Coming after the success of the 422-MW Kishau Multipurpose Project signing in September, the recent SC verdict may prove a shot in the arm for the Sukhu government ahead of the Assembly elections, depending on how the Congress converts it into electoral gains.

World.title: Why Dr Nene recommends this age-old Ayurvedic post-meal ritual: ‘Try Shatpawali’
World.content:
Dr Shriram Nene, a cardiothoracic surgeon and husband of Bollywood actor Madhuri Dixit, regularly shares valuable health tips and tricks on social media. In his latest Instagram post, the doctor spoke about the Ayurvedic concept of “Shatpawali – 100 relaxed steps after lunch or dinner.”

“Before glucose monitors, step counters and wellness apps, Indian homes had one simple line: After a meal, take a short walk. And maybe that old habit was smarter than we realised,” Dr Nene shared in the video.



“No workout clothes. No step target obsession. Just 2 to 5 minutes of gentle movement before returning to your day. The number 100 is traditional, not magical. The real win is teaching your body that a meal does not always have to end with sitting,” he elaborated in the caption of his Instagram post.

World.title: Caretaker booked for allegedly siphoning off Rs 1.77 crore from late actress Nimmi’s FDs
World.content:
The Santacruz police have registered an FIR against a caretaker of late Bollywood actress Nimmi, alleging that he misappropriated fixed deposits worth Rs 1.77 crore, sold her car for scrap and attempted to take control of two flats in Santacruz (West) after her death in 2020.

The case concerns the assets of Nawab Banu, popularly known by her screen name Nimmi, who died on March 25, 2020. According to the FIR, the two flats, two parking spaces and fixed deposits were among the assets she had left behind for her beneficiaries under a will.

The complainant, Mohammad Yunus Salim Durrani, 48, a relative of the actress’s family, told police that Nimmi and her husband, noted scriptwriter Ali Raza, had purchased two flats in the B Wing of Neha Apartment on Juhu Tara Road in 2003. The properties were registered in Nimmi’s name. The couple also held fixed deposits of Rs 1.23 crore with the State Bank of India and Rs 54 lakh with Saraswat Bank.

World.title: PT Usha cleared for IOA polls despite objections; 71 voters, big names in fray
World.content:
Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha was cleared to contest the December 5 elections after the Electoral Officer rejected the objections raised against her nomination on Sunday. With the final electoral roll of 71 members published, Usha is back in the race for a second term, with Olympic medallists Anju Bobby George, Saina Nehwal and Gagan Narang also eligible to contest for various positions in the IOA Executive Council.

The Electoral Officer rejected the objections, noting that neither the IOA Constitution nor the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, and its accompanying rules contained a provision that automatically disqualified an individual from representing a national sports federation merely because they were associated with another federation.

World.title: Film, politician and trademark battle: Why NCP leader Rupali Chakankar is upset
World.content:
Ahead of release of the film based on self-styled godman Ashok Kharat, NCP leader Rupali Chakankar Sunday warned of taking legal action against those using her photographs and videos for commercial purposes without prior permission.

Chakankar, who got embroiled in the controversy involving the self-styled godman after photographs showing her proximity to him emerged, claimed that she has officially registered a trademark for her name, photograph, identity, and personal style.

“Trademark registration has been done regarding my name, my photo, my identity, my personal style, and my specific manner of presenting myself. Without my prior permission, if anyone uses my name, photo, identity, or my specific style for personal gain or commercial purposes to create, use, or publish any kind of photos, videos, films, reels, teasers, promotions, or any other material, strict legal action will be taken against such a person according to the law,” Chakankar said in a post on X.

World.title: Romance, money and sabotage: Police uncover ISI plot behind Rajasthan railway track blast
World.content:
The sabotage of a railway track in Sri Ganganagar earlier this month was undertaken at the behest of Pakistan’s intelligence agency, Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), the Rajasthan Police said after its ATS arrested two accused, including a woman, in Punjab’s Gurdaspur on Saturday.

The accused have been identified as Mahakdeep Kaur, 21, and Davinder Singh, 23. Police said while Kaur is the main accused in the case, Singh is her accomplice.



As per preliminary investigation, Kaur was in contact with two Pakistani handlers and, along with her accomplice, carried out the blast.

On November 3, a blast had taken place at the railway track passing through Ramsinghpur area in Sri Ganganagar district on the Indo-Pak border. Police said that the accused had tried to attempt similar blasts earlier as well.

World.title: After Gurugram couple chased on Diwali night, accused held; stolen vans recovered
World.content:
After a video showing a couple allegedly being chased in Gurugram on the night of Diwali went viral, police took suo motu cognizance of the matter and arrested a man, officers said on Sunday. The accused allegedly chased the couple’s car for nearly a kilometre near the Southern Peripheral Road (SPR).

A joint team from the Crime Branch units of Manesar and Sector 65 apprehended the accused, identified as Monu from Sohna, near Tulip Chowk at Sector 72. Two stolen Eeco vans, including the one used to chase the couple, were from his possession, said police.

A senior police officer said, “After the couple refused to lodge a complaint, Gurugram Police took suo motu cognisance of the matter.”

The chase that raised the scare



The alleged incident came to light on November 13 after Gurugram resident Shubham Jain shared dashcam recordings and housing society CCTV footage on X. Jain said the chase happened around 11:55 pm on the night of Diwali on November 8 while he was driving home with his wife.

According to the couple, a van pulled alongside their car on Darbaripur Road in Sector 70. He initially assumed the driver was overtaking his car, but he tried to speed away when the van halted abruptly. “I kept on gunning the car until I reached my society’s gates and till that time the car had already tried to cut across and stop me. It still gives me goosebumps as I type this,” Jain wrote on X.

Private security guards intercepted the van at the entrance of Jain’s housing society and prevented it from entering.

Jain, who said he moved to the city just seven months ago, alleged that the van had two occupants — a man in his mid-20s and a teenager. The accused allegedly argued with the guards for nearly 20 minutes before leaving.



He also alleged that the vehicle’s rear number plate had been removed while the front plate was hidden.

As he credited his dashcam and the society guards, he also hinted that there was not enough police presence in the area. “This is what my 40% tax gets? Only to be saved by private security?” Jain wrote.

Badshahpur Station House Officer Inspector Manoj Kumar and Head Constable Samrita contacted Jain after his social media posts went viral. Jain, however, stated on X that he had decided against submitting a written complaint “for my own reasons”.

Accused cites sudden cut, drove stolen van

During questioning, Monu, in his 20s, allegedly told the investigators that the confrontation began over a driving manoeuvre near Tulip Chowk and denied knowing the couple. “The accused said that the driver of the car seen in the viral video suddenly cut in front of his vehicle, following which he chased the car to stop him. He further claimed that he did not know the person beforehand,” a senior police officer said.



Police said the Eeco van used in the chase was a stolen vehicle. “The Eeco vehicle used by him to chase the car had been stolen by him on October 12 from Beriwala Bagh in Shanti Nagar on October 12. A case regarding this theft is registered at the Shivaji Nagar police station,” an officer added.

Wanted in tyre-theft case

Police said that Monu’s criminal record revealed that he was wanted in a tyre theft case registered at the Sector 10 police station. A resident had filed a complaint at the Sector 93 police post on May 8 after finding all four tyres and rims stolen from his friend’s car parked outside a housing society in the area.

Police Sunday formally arrested Monu in the tyre theft case. Senior police officers said the accused allegedly admitted to 19 theft incidents in Gurugram during questioning, and records show eight theft cases are already registered against him in the city.

Monu was produced before a court on Sunday and taken into police remand for further questioning and recovery.

World.title: UPSC Essentials daily subject quiz : International Relations MCQs (Week 188) — Check out answers with explanations
World.content:
UPSC Essentials brings to you its initiative of subject-wise quizzes. These quizzes are designed to help you revise some of the most important topics from the static part of the syllabus. Attempt today’s subject quiz on International Relations to check your progress.

🚨 Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for October 2026. Share your views and suggestions in the comment box or at manas.srivastava@indianexpress.com🚨

With reference to the East Asia Summit (EAS), consider the following statements:

1. The objectives and principles of EAS are outlined in the 2005 Kuala Lumpur Declaration.

2. The 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) will be held in the Philippines.

3. The Chairmanship of the EAS can only be held by an ASEAN member country.

How many of the statements given above are correct?

(a) Only one

(b) Only two

(c) All three

(d) None

Relevance: It is relevant to India’s engagement with ASEAN-led regional institutions and its Act East Policy. It connects with regional cooperation, Indo-Pacific geopolitics and India’s role in the evolving East Asian security architecture.

Explanation



— A summit of the Quad leaders is expected to take place in Manila next week, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be attending the ASEAN-India and East Asia summits.

— The East Asia Summit (EAS) process was initiated in 2005 with the convening of the 1st East Asia Summit in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The East Asia Summit’s objectives and principles are outlined in its basic documents, including the 2005 Kuala Lumpur Declaration on the East Asia Summit. Hence, statement 1 is correct.

— Under the Kuala Lumpur Declaration, the EAS is hosted and chaired by an ASEAN member country that assumes the ASEAN Chairmanship. Hence, statement 3 is correct.

— The 21st East Asia Summit is scheduled to be held in the Philippines in 2026. The Philippines holds the ASEAN Chairmanship in 2026. Hence, statement 2 is correct.

Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

(Other Source: eastasiasummit.asean.org)



QUESTION 2

The ‘NUTEC Plastics’ aims to address the global challenge of plastic pollution. It is an initiative of:

(a) Global Environment Facility

(b) Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change

(c) United Nations Environment Programme

(d) International Atomic Energy Agency

Relevance: The question connects with topics such as plastic waste management, recycling technologies, marine pollution and sustainable development. It is relevant to the role of international organisations in developing scientific and technological solutions for environmental protection.

Explanation

— NUTEC Plastics is the IAEA’s flagship initiative to address the global challenge of plastic pollution.

— It brings together countries and partners from around the world to fight plastic pollution on two fronts: at point of source, by introducing new technologies to improve plastic recycling; and in the ocean, where the bulk of plastic waste ends up.

Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

(Source: http://www.iaea.org)



QUESTION 3

Consider the following statements about the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE):

1. It is an international non-governmental, non-profit organisation.

2. It is headquartered in Geneva.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

(a) 1 only

(b) 2 only

(c) Both 1 and 2

(d) Neither 1 nor 2

Relevance: The question is relevant to international environmental organisations and their role in promoting environmental education and sustainable development. It is useful for understanding the institutional framework supporting environmental conservation and sustainability at the global level.

Explanation

— The Blue Flag is an internationally recognised voluntary eco-label awarded to beaches, marinas and tourism boats that meet prescribed standards of environmental management, water quality, safety, accessibility and environmental education.

— The programme is run by the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), an international non-governmental, non-profit organisation headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark. It began in France in 1985 and has since grown into a global certification programme. Hence, statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is not correct.

Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.



QUESTION 4

The Disaster Risk Financing Platform aims to secure access to more than $3 billion in risk financing to protect 75 million people and their livelihoods from potential climate shocks and natural hazards by 2030. The Disaster Risk Financing Platform was launched during:

(a) 7th United Nations Environment Assembly

(b) 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference

(c) 56th World Economic Forum Annual Meeting

(d) 14th G20 Leaders’ Summit

Relevance: The question links to international cooperation on climate change, disaster risk reduction and climate resilience. It is relevant to India’s engagement with multilateral climate negotiations and international climate-financing mechanisms.

Explanation

According to http://www.fao.org,

— “The United Nations today launched a new initiative at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, aiming to secure access to more than $3 billion in risk financing to protect 75 million people and their livelihoods from potential climate shocks and natural hazards by 2030.

— Bringing together six UN agencies, the UN Disaster Risk Financing (DRF) Platform aims to make disaster response funding more predictable, increase the availability of funding for early action during major crises, and maximise the impact of every dollar by combining available resources with private sector support.



— The platform will enable agencies to share expertise, pool data, and coordinate joint solutions to expand the UN’s use of pre-arranged financing. Combining robust data and predictive analysis with funds will help governments and agencies help turn early warnings into anticipatory actions. This will strengthen emergency responses before, during, and after disasters.”

Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

QUESTION 5

With reference to the Berlin West Africa Conference, consider the following statements:

1. The Conference set rules governing European expansion on the continent.

2. The Conference divided up and partitioned the entire continent of Africa among European powers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

(a) 1 only

(b) 2 only

(c) Both 1 and 2

(d) Neither 1 nor 2



Relevance: The question is relevant to the study of European imperialism, colonial expansion and the Scramble for Africa during the 19th century. It connects with themes such as colonialism, geopolitical rivalries and the changing political map of Africa.

Explanation

— The Berlin West Africa Conference, held from November 15, 1884, to February 26, 1885, resulted in the adoption of the General Act, which set rules governing European expansion on the continent. Hence, statement 1 is correct.

— Among other things, the Act established conditions under which European powers could acquire territory along the African coast, internationalised navigation on the Congo and Niger rivers, called for a renewed campaign against the overland slave trade, and declared a vast area of Central Africa, designated the ‘conventional basin of the Congo’, neutral.

— The Conference did not legally partition the African continent amongst European nations. Instead, it established laws that allowed and legitimised further European territorial expansion and the Scramble for Africa. Much of the actual dividing occurred through subsequent accords and colonial invasions. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.
